the imam reciting aloud in the audible prayers a man was praying the obligatory ish prayer on his own when another man came and joined him as a follower the first man did not recite aloud is the prayer valid or not and is it necessary for an imam to recite aloud in the audible prayers if the man formed the intention of leading the prayer then reciting aloud was necessary if he did not form the intention of leading reciting aloud was not necessary and the prayer is valid for an imam reciting aloud in the audible prayers is necessary al durr al mukht r states

praying behind an imam who wears false teeth a man has lost some of his teeth and has had false teeth fitted which can be taken out without them certain letters sh n and d for example are not pronounced properly if this man does not put the teeth in even though they are at home or in his pocket and leads the prayer in that condition will the prayer be valid or not in the case described if without the false teeth he falls into an open error of pronunciation la n jal then he must put the teeth in before leading the prayer without them the meaning is altered and the prayer becomes invalid if without the false teeth he only falls into a hidden error of pronunciation la n khaf then putting the teeth in is better and preferable but not required the details of open and hidden errors can be looked up in the books of fiqh or learnt directly from a scholar trained in recitation fat w sh m states

praying behind an imam who holds barelw beliefs if a person finds himself praying behind an imam who holds barelw beliefs should he give up the congregation or join it and what should he do if he has no choice but to pray behind him barelw beliefs vary a great deal some of them for instance holding that the prophet knows the unseen that he is present and watching everywhere that he has absolute discretion that he disposes of the affairs of the world calling him the remover of difficulties and the fulfiller of needs and describing him as a reflection of allah most high are beliefs that carry a man to disbelief so if a person holds the beliefs just mentioned prayer behind him is not valid and if someone is forced to pray behind him he must repeat the prayer if there is a fear of strife he should simply go through the outward motions along with the worshippers and then repeat his prayer afterwards this

the imam's duty to inform the congregation that the prayer was invalid if the imam's prayer became invalid because of bleeding and the imam only realised this after the prayer is he obliged to inform the congregation or not if for some reason the prayer was not valid the imam is obliged to inform those who prayed behind him if the imam is an upright man they must then repeat the prayer otherwise repeating it is recommended but if the followers cannot be identified or informing them is difficult then he is not obliged to inform them al durr al mukht r states

informing people of an invalid prayer after a long time has passed a man used to lead the prayers in a mosque and a good deal of time has passed since once or twice it happened that during the prayer he suspected or thought it likely that a drop of urine had come out on another occasion on the first night of ramadan the sighting of the moon had not yet been announced and the imam had already prayed his own witr then once the moon had been announced he led the people in witr again after the tar w even though the tar w had been led by someone else at the time he made no announcement that the prayer should be repeated on account of the drop of urine which was either doubtful or merely thought likely he now has no connection at all with that p in the case described since the breaking of the imam's ablution by a drop was doubtful or merely thought likely he should have made the announcement at the time so that the prayer could be repeated the established anaf position is that the imam's prayer carries the follower's prayer with it this has been explained already in volume two p 234 in view of the difficulties in the situation described however there is a ruling among the jurists which shows that the announcement is not necessary tu fat al mul k states in his commentary on it mu ammad ibn abd al la f ibn

whether a woman may lead men in prayer can a woman lead men in prayer or not a woman cannot lead men in prayer consider the evidence all mah al l s may allah have mercy on him says in r al ma n all mah al nasaf may allah have mercy on him says

tabl gh workers holding congregational prayer at the gathering ground what is the sharia ruling on the following matter work on preparing for the gathering begins about six or seven weeks in advance and many people come from different areas we normally pray at the gathering ground itself whether or not there is a mosque nearby there are several reasons for this 1 it is far more convenient and saves a great deal of time 2 after every prayer there are discussions and talks of encouragement and instruction and consultation is held as needed after fajr there is the collective recitation of s rah y s n supplication remembrance of allah and other regular practices after most of the prayers necessary appeals are put before the gathering 3 in t in the case described the better and more meritorious course is for the congregational prayer to be performed in the mosque but if because of some valid excuse people hold their own congregation they will still obtain the merit of congregational prayer since the workers of tabl gh remain occupied with tasks at the gathering ground and people come there in such numbers that it becomes difficult for everyone to go to the mosque and some of them have to stay behind to guard the belongings they may hold their own congregation all mah ibn bid n al sh m may allah have mercy on him writes

holding congregational prayer in an open ground instead of the mosque some people object to the tabl gh jam at saying that they leave the mosque and hold their congregation outside at the gathering ground the objectors claim that congregational prayer in the mosque is an emphasised sunnah and that there is no merit in a congregation held outside is this claim correct or not they also cite a report of abdull h ibn mas d may allah be pleased with him in which congregational prayer in the mosque is called one of the ways of guidance if a congregation is held outside the mosque the reward of congregational prayer is obtained the reward for a congregation held in the mosque however is greater than that al fat w al sir jiyyah states al a w 's gloss on mar q al fal states fat w q kh n states

performing the ish prayer at the place where tar w is held in ramadan in ramadan the tar w prayer is held at several places within a single locality for instance in study halls in a hall and in various homes the question is this should these people perform the obligatory ish prayer in congregation in the mosque and then go to their respective places for tar w or may they perform the obligatory prayer in congregation at their own place as well there is some disagreement about this among us kindly explain the correct sharia ruling we shall be most grateful in the case described the better and more meritorious course is to perform the ish prayer in congregation in the mosque and then go on to one's own place of tar w this is because two separate sunnahs are involved here 1 performing the obligatory prayer in congregation and 2 that this congregation for the obligatory prayer be held in the mosque so if a person does not perform the obligatory prayer in congregation in the mosque without a valid excuse one sunnah will have been left out and its reward will not be gained if however there is a valid excuse for example the place of tar w is a good distance from the mosque and there is no transport or it is close by but walki

shortening the ablution for fear of missing the congregation if the congregational prayer has already begun and washing each limb three times in ablution means there is a risk of missing the prayer with the congregation should the congregation be given preference or should one give preference to performing the ablution as the sunnah requires since washing three times is a sunnah of ablution in the case described the congregational prayer should be given preference and the ablution shortened a parallel to this is found in the statements of the jurists may allah have mercy on them a sunnah may be left out for fear of missing the congregation consider what fat w sh m states in another place he says

going to another mosque after missing the congregation in one's local mosque if a person can catch two units of the prayer in his own local mosque while at another place that is not his local mosque he could catch the whole prayer in congregation should he travel the extra distance or should he simply join the last two units in his own mosque praying in congregation is either necessary or an emphasised sunnah furthermore praying in congregation in the mosque of one's own neighbourhood is better and that mosque has a right over him and if the congregation in one's local mosque has been missed it is not necessary to go searching for a congregation in another mosque

attending the mosque for congregational prayer with a bag collecting bodily waste a man is ill and a bag has been fitted to his abdomen into which waste the kind normally passed through the back passage collects by means of a tube what is the ruling on this man coming to the mosque and praying with the congregation does this count as bringing filth into the mosque or not and does it make any difference whether there is a bad smell or not in ordinary circumstances it is strictly disliked to bring foul smelling things or filth into the mosque especially when there is a risk of soiling the mosque but in the case of a person who is legally excused as in the case asked about this bag takes the same ruling as his own stomach and belly so if there is no smell the bag is concealed and it causes no revulsion to others it is permissible and correct for him to go to the mosque filth passing into the bag does break the ablution but since this man is legally excused and filth keeps coming out of his stomach continuously his ablution will break with the expiry of the prayer time unless something else occurs that breaks it it

women holding a congregation of their own can women form a congregation of their own and pray together it is better for women to pray individually praying in congregation is disliked for them nowadays however where there is a need for example a woman who has memorised the qur'an needs to keep it fresh in her memory then if the women of a household or a few women or a group of women who have memorised the qur'an gather and hold a congregation this should be permissible without any dislike if there is a fear of discord or temptation it remains disliked consider the evidence for the view that it is disliked fat w sh m states al a w 's gloss on mar q al fal states

women going to the mosque in the light of the qur'an and the sunnah what is the ruling on women going to the mosque for prayer in the light of the qur'an and the sunnah it appears that it is better for women to pray at home indeed in an inner corner of the house in an age full of temptation when indecency is widespread going to the mosques does not befit women who keep to modesty nor has the sacred law looked upon it with favour consider the evidence 1 in the noble qur'an allah says concerning the pure wives of the prophet who are the mothers of all muslims that is settle in your homes so how can it be fitting for other women to go out to the mosques for prayer where there is also mixing with men likewise the teachings of the prophet in the hadiths concerning women are the

women praying in congregation in the two sacred mosques nowadays women pray in the two sacred mosques what is the ruling on this the better and more meritorious course is for women not to come to the two sacred mosques to pray if there is a valid excuse such as fear then a woman may come it is also proper to come for the circumambulation and to visit the blessed tomb of the prophet and if the time of a prayer arrives while she is there there is room for her to pray there in ordinary circumstances it is better for her to pray in her room the hadiths also show the merit of this consider what the hadith states

holding a second congregation within the precincts of a mosque what is the ruling on holding a second congregation within the precincts of a mosque in a mosque that has an appointed imam and muezzin holding a second congregation within the mosque precincts in the same manner as the first is strictly disliked if the manner is changed that is if it is held without the call to prayer and away from the prayer niche or from the line of the niche then it is permissible though mildly disliked it is better where there is a room or a madrasah adjoining the mosque for the second congregation to be held there people should also take care to attend the first congregation making a habit of the second congregation is not good since it removes the standing and dignity of the first congregation from people's hearts in a wayside mosque h

holding a second congregation in the courtyard of a mosque some men arrived at the neighbourhood mosque after the congregation was over if they pray in the courtyard of the mosque should they pray in congregation or each on his own holding a second congregation in a neighbourhood mosque is not correct it is strictly disliked if the manner is changed it is permissible with a mild dislike the reason is that if repeating the congregation were permitted generally the importance of the first congregation would no longer remain so it is far better for them to pray individually there is no harm in holding a congregation in the courtyard of the mosque where that courtyard lies outside the mosque proper provided they do not make a habit of it consider what shams al a immah all mah al sarakhs may allah have mercy on him says

a second congregation in a mosque that has an appointed imam but no fixed congregation there is a mosque by the roadside neither its congregation nor its neighbourhood is fixed but it does have an appointed imam can a second congregation be held in this mosque or not since the imam is appointed this mosque takes the ruling of a neighbourhood mosque and a second congregation in it is disliked the congregation should instead be held in a room or a madrasah adjoining the mosque or at some place outside it if there is no appointed imam either then it is permissible shams al a immah all mah al sarakhs says

the call to prayer and the iq mah for a second congregation if a second congregation is to be held should the call to prayer and the iq mah be given for it or not if a second congregation is to be held outside the mosque in open country it should be held with the call to prayer and the iq mah if it is held in a settlement or a town the iq mah alone is sufficient but a second congregation in the mosque with the call to prayer and the iq mah is disliked consider what al fat w al hindiyyah states

leaving a gap between the men's row and the children's row in some mosques two or three rows are left empty and the children are made to stand behind them so that men who come later can stand in the front rows is this practice correct or should the children stand in the row immediately behind the men and then the men who arrive stand alongside them or behind them as a general rule the children's row should be formed behind however many rows of men there are in the mosque after that if adults arrive and there is no room ahead of them they should stand at the back imd d al fatt states 349

making a young child stand in the row of adults a man makes his young son who has not yet reached puberty stand in the first row during the congregational prayer is this correct also where does sharia place children who have not reached puberty in the rows please answer in detail with the evidence if the first row of the mosque is normally filled by adults then making a young child stand in the first row is contrary to the sunnah and is disliked if however the first row is normally not filled by adults then the child should not stand on his own but should join the men if there are a number of children the row of young children should be behind the row of the men this is the place sharia assigns them al ba r al r iq states

a single child standing at the edge of the men's row the children's row should be behind the men but if there is only one child may he stand at the edge of the men's row the basic rule is that the children should be behind the rows of men if however they are unruly one or two of them may be placed at the ends of the rows some jurists have allowed this so if there is only one child it is all the more permissible to place him at the edge of the men's row al durr al mukht r states taqr r t al r fi states

a woman standing in the men's row may a woman stand in the row beside a man and pray or not in prayer a woman's place is behind the man so she may not stand beside him in the row and pray consider the following hadith another hadith states at home however it is permissible for a wife to stand level with her husband while each of them prays their own pra

a girl who has made herself a boy standing in the men's row a girl has made herself into a boy may she stand in the row of the men or not she has even grown a beard the jurists have explained with regard to the khunth a person of indeterminate sex that once the marks of a male become apparent such a person comes under the ruling of a man and it is correct for him to stand in the row with the men so a girl who has made herself a boy and in whom the marks of a boy have appeared may stand in the men's row and everyone's prayer will be valid such an act is however a repugnant one it comes under altering the creation of allah and is forbidden one must give it up and fear the anger of allah consider al durr al mukht r

forming a row between two pillars what is the ruling on forming a row between two pillars where there is no need to do so and the mosque is spacious forming a row between two pillars is disliked a prohibition of it has come in the hadith where space is tight and there is a genuine need however it is permissible as shams al a immah al sarakhs may allah have mercy on him has stated that a row between two pillars is permissible without any dislike his words may also be understood to mean that the dislike involved is not the strict kind sunan al tirmidh states

an explanation of mu dh t a woman standing level with a man in prayer please explain the question of mu dh t a woman standing level with a man in prayer the definition of mu dh t if in prayer a woman stands ahead of a man or level with him that is in such a way that at any moment during the prayer her foot comes opposite any limb of his the man's prayer becomes invalid the feet being level and opposite means that the shin and the ankle are level according to the sound view this is what counts so if the woman's ankle and shin are level with the man's ankle and shin mu dh t is established and the man's prayer becomes invalid even if because her foot is smaller than his some of the front of her foot falls behind his but if her foot is so far behind his that the ankles and shins are not level at all her ankle and shin bein

women praying behind the imam on an upper floor and the rule of mu dh t if a large number of women pray behind the imam on the upper floor of the mosque and behind the women there are men praying at ground level is the men's prayer valid or not if the women's row is on the upper floor of the mosque and the men's row is at ground level and the women are not ahead of the men's row the prayer is valid where they are ahead of it there is some slight difference among the jurists but since the standard texts do not call the men's prayer invalid when a barrier is present on the contrary they call it valid the men's prayer will be valid in this case as well consider shar munyat al mu all which states

a solution to the problem of women standing level with men in the aram the problem of women standing level with the men mu dh t in the aram seems insoluble is there any room for leniency in it or any room to give a ruling according to the school of another imam have the jurists dealt with this matter explicitly or not the rule that a woman standing level with a man invalidates the prayer belongs to the hanafi school alone in the view of the other three imams standing level counts for nothing furthermore the only evidence the hanafis have on this question is the statement of abdull h ibn mas d may allah be pleased with him mull al al q r may allah have mercy on him said in shar al niq yah that the report is not sound as a saying traced back to the prophet though it is sound as a statement of abdull h ibn mas d may allah be pleased with him himself even then all that can be established from it is a recommendation that it is recommended for women to pray

a verification of the hadith it is well known in the books of hadith that this report is narrated from ibn mas d may allah be pleased with him as a statement of his own whereas in mishk t al ma b on the authority of raz n it is narrated as a saying of the prophet why then do the scholars call it a statement of a companion and deny that it is a saying of the prophet

men following the imam from a rear room with women in the room in front behind the imam in the room in front there are women and the men are in the room behind them is it valid for the men to follow the imam or not if the women are in the front room and the men in the room behind the jurists differ as to whether the men's following of the imam is valid the safer course is to hold that it is not valid and this is the position all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him preferred there is moreover no necessity in this case since the men can stand in the front room and the women in the room behind consider al durr al mukht r which states

following the imam from another room if the imam is in one room with a few followers and because of the shortage of space some of the followers pray in a separate room is their following of the imam valid or not in the case described if the two rooms adjoin each other and there is no wide passage or empty space the width of two rows between them those in the second room are validly following the imam otherwise they are not consider radd al mu t r which states

following the imam from the roof or courtyard of a house adjoining the mosque if a house adjoins a mosque with only a wall between them and the imam's takb rs can be heard is it valid to follow him from the roof or the courtyard of that house it is valid to follow the imam from the roof or the courtyard of a house adjoining the mosque provided the rows are joined and there is no empty space or wide passage in between consider imd d al fatt which states

following the imam from the roof of a house adjoining the mosque if a house adjoins the mosque is it permissible to stand on its roof and follow the imam or not where a house adjoins the mosque there is no empty space in between and the imam's takb rs can be made out it is permissible and valid to follow him even so the safer course is not to do so since the two are not in one and the same place consider mar q al fal shar n r al which states

following the imam in a large mosque when the rows are not joined in large mosques it often happens that people pray without the rows being joined that is a good deal of empty space is left in between what is the ruling of sharia in this case this happens frequently in the two arams differing statements on this question are found in the fatwa works some record that in a large mosque a wide gap prevents one from following the imam while others do not mention this restriction keeping in view the conditions of our own day prayer in a large mosque should be valid without any such restriction for the mosques of the two arams the sacred mosque and the prophet's mosque are very large indeed and on ordinary days the rows are not joined otherwise the prayers of thousands of people would be spoiled all mah al a w may allah have mercy on him has also given a sound explanation of the matter when the imam's movements are clear to the followers following him is

following an imam who is praying a different obligatory prayer if the imam is praying sunday's fajr and the follower is praying saturday's fajr is it permissible to follow him or not if the obligatory prayer of the follower is different from that of the imam it is not valid to follow him consider mukhta ar al qud r which states al jawharah al nayyirah states n r al states see also

a standing follower praying behind an imam seated on a chair suppose there is a hanafi imam who has severe pain in his knees and suffers from arthritis he is able to stand and to perform the bowing properly but an expert muslim doctor has told him that if he goes down into prostration his knees will be ruined permanently the question is this may such a man lead the prayer while seated on a chair performing the prostration by a gesture please also explain how much concession there is for him and what the solution is in the case described the imam is one who prays by gesture that is he indicates the prostration rather than performing it and the prayer of someone who does not pray by gesture is not valid behind one who does if however the imam sits on the ground and performs the bowing and the prostration on the ground then the prayer of a follower who is standing is valid so the imam should on the advice of an expert doctor lead the prayer seated on the ground while performing the bowing and the prostration consider al hid yah which states

one person with a chronic excuse following another whose excuse is different if the imam has the excuse of uncontrollable passing of wind and the follower has the excuse of urinary incontinence is it valid to follow him or not when the two excuses differ following the imam is not valid so in the case described according to the sound position it is not valid for a man with urinary incontinence to follow one who passes wind uncontrollably as is clear from the statements of all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him and all mah al a w may allah have mercy on him consider radd al mu t r which states

following an imam who has two excuses when the follower has only one if the imam has two excuses uncontrollable passing of wind and urinary incontinence and the follower has only the excuse of passing wind is it permissible to follow him or not in the case described it is not permissible to follow him because the imam is in a weaker state than the follower consider radd al mu t r which states al jawharah al nayyirah states imd d al fatt states

newcomers joining a congregational prayer that is being repeated a man's prayer became invalid because he omitted a necessary act he did not perform the prostration of forgetfulness and he is now repeating it can three new men who have not yet prayed follow him or not both positions are reported from the jurists on this question whether the obligation was discharged by the first prayer or by the second for the sake of ease then it is valid for a newcomer to follow him but the cautious course is not to follow him imd d al fatt states 11 radd al mu t r states

a sh fi following a hanafi imam in the fajr prayer a sh fi followed a hanafi imam in the fajr prayer and the imam did not recite the qun t was the sh fi follower's prayer valid or not the prayer of a sh fi follower behind a hanafi imam in fajr is valid he should though recite the qun t the supplication recited in the fajr prayer and then join the imam in the prostration if he does not recite it he should perform the prostration of forgetfulness and even if he does not perform that either his prayer is still valid according to one position consider shar al muhadhdhab which states shar al waj z states

saying the opening takb r before the imam if someone says the words before the imam is his prayer valid or not if a follower finishes his opening takb r before the imam finishes his his following of the imam is not valid so in the case described this man's following of the imam is not valid either consider shar munyat al mu all which states

a resident hanafi following a travelling sh fi imam in the uhr prayer if a hanafi follows a sh fi who is travelling in the uhr prayer and the sh fi prays the full four units is the hanafi follower's prayer valid or not our senior scholars may allah have mercy on them differ over this question a rat muft mu ammad shaf ib may allah have mercy on him for example wrote in imd d al muft n that the hanafi follower's prayer is not valid in the view of certain other scholars however the prayer is valid and so in the case described the hanafi follower's prayer should be valid abdull h ibn mas d may allah be pleased with him used to pray the full prayer while travelling behind uthm n may allah be pleased with him even though in his own view shortening the prayer was required consider a al bukh r which states

the rules of following an imam of one's own school and of another school if a hanafi prays four units of uhr behind a sh fi or anbal imam while travelling your fat w d r al ul m zakariyy declares this permissible whereas a great many muftis say that such a prayer must be repeated and articles on the subject have also appeared in some journals we had written a detailed fatwa on this which was shortened in the book for the sake of brevity its substance is that in the above question there are two kinds of following 1 following an imam of one's own school 2 following an imam of another school in following an imam of one's own school since in the view of both the imam and the follower supererogatory and obligatory units have been mixed together the prayer must be repeated as for following an imam of another school the statements of the jurists bear witness that so long as the imam does not according to the follower's school do anything that invalidates the prayer or omit any obligatory element the prayer is sound and

reciting in the remaining units after praying behind a travelling imam if a resident prays two units behind a traveller and then stands up to complete his own remaining two units does he recite in those two units or not some books of fiqh record the position that he does not recite the wording of certain other books however shows that he is in the position of one praying alone so there is no harm in his reciting indeed reciting should be recommended consider bad i al an i which states shar al niq yah states

praying behind a jinn as imam if someone follows a jinn in prayer is the prayer valid or not if the jinn is in human form it is valid to follow him and the prayer is sound otherwise it is not consider what all mah badr al d n al shibl al anaf writes in his book being in human form is necessary because otherwise it is difficult to make out his movements consider al durr al mukht r which states

a latecomer who says the opening takb r as the imam gives the sal m a man joined the prayer just as the imam was giving the sal m or a little before that but the imam gave the sal m before he had sat down for the final sitting was his following of the imam valid or not and if it was not valid should he break his intention or carry on with the prayer he has already begun if the latecomer said the opening takb r takb r ta r mah before the imam's sal m his following of the imam is valid but if the imam had already given the sal m to one side and only then did the man say the opening takb r his following is not valid he should now say a fresh opening takb r and pray on his own fat w sh m states al durr al mukht r states

a latecomer who gives the sal m along with the imam by mistake if a latecomer gives the sal m along with the imam by mistake does he have to perform the prostration of forgetfulness or not if the latecomer gave the sal m at the same moment as the imam or before him the prostration of forgetfulness sajdah sahw is not necessary if he gave it after the imam's sal m it is necessary in practice people almost always give the sal m a moment after the imam so the prostration of forgetfulness will be necessary al durr al mukht r states

joining an imam who has stood up for a fifth rak ah if the imam mistakenly stood up for a fifth rak ah and a man came and joined him is that valid or not and what is the ruling if the imam then returned and sat down for the final sitting and what if he did not return but went on to add a sixth rak ah as well a latecomer's joining of the imam in the fifth rak ah is valid only if the imam returns before performing the prostration of that fifth rak ah if the imam went on to add a sixth rak ah the latecomer's joining is not valid because in that case it would be a case of an obligatory prayer performed behind someone praying a voluntary one and the jurists do not permit this fat w q kh n states

a latecomer who follows the imam into a fifth rak ah if a latecomer follows the imam into a fifth rak ah what is the ruling on his prayer and will this extra rak ah count as obligatory or as voluntary for him if the imam stood up for a fifth rak ah by mistake and the latecomer followed him then if the imam had already sat in the fourth rak ah the latecomer's prayer becomes invalid this is because a latecomer is at that point praying on his own and for a latecomer to follow anyone else invalidates his prayer fat w q kh n however records that his prayer does not become invalid even when the imam had sat in the fourth rak ah if the imam had not sat in the fourth rak ah the prayer does not become invalid so long as the imam has not performed the prostration of the fifth rak ah once the imam performs that prostration the obligatory prayer of everyone comes to an end and turns into a

when a latecomer should stand up to make up the prayer he missed should a latecomer stand up after the imam's first sal m or after the second a latecomer should stand up to make up what he missed only when he is certain that the imam has finished his prayer and has nothing left to perform and this is usually at the time of the second sal m the marginal notes on taby n al aq iq state

a latecomer who deliberately gives the sal m with the imam at the prostration of forgetfulness if a latecomer deliberately gives the sal m along with the imam at the prostration of forgetfulness what is the ruling on his prayer the latecomer's prayer becomes invalid if he gave the sal m deliberately otherwise it does not sh m states al fat w al hindiyyah states al ba r al r iq states fat w ma m diyyah states a latecomer must perform th

following a latecomer in prayer after the imam had given the sal m a latecomer was completing the rest of his prayer and a man came and prayed behind him is this valid or not a latecomer is required to pray alone and cannot act as an imam so in the case asked about this following is not valid shar munyat al mu all states

a latecomer completing his missed rak ahs by watching another latecomer a latecomer often forgets how many rak ahs he has missed so when he makes them up he watches the man next to him and completes his missed rak ahs accordingly is his prayer valid if he does this or not it is correct to pray while watching another latecomer but it is not correct to follow him as one follows an imam fat al qad r states shiyat al a w states see also fat w ra miyyah 1 137 maktabah ra miyyah and fat w ma m diyyah 6 564 b b al

a latecomer reciting aloud in the rak ahs he makes up is it permissible for a latecomer to recite aloud when making up a missed rak ah of the dawn prayer in the rak ahs he makes up a latecomer has the status of one praying alone and a person praying alone has a choice in the prayers in which recitation is aloud so the latecomer too may recite aloud in a missed rak ah of such a prayer provided this does not disturb the prayer of other latecomers sh m states al a w 's notes on mar q al fal state al

how a latecomer makes up two missed rak ahs of the sunset prayer if a man missed two rak ahs of the sunset prayer should he sit between the two rak ahs when making them up or not and if he does not sit is the prostration of forgetfulness required or not the way to make up two missed rak ahs of the sunset prayer is to recite in both of them and also to sit between them but if he did not sit it is still permissible by juristic preference the prayer is valid no prostration of forgetfulness is required and there is no need to repeat the prayer majma al zaw id states

how a resident latecomer completes his prayer behind a travelling imam a latecomer joined a travelling imam at the final tashahhud how should he complete his prayer our senior scholars have differed on this question some of them say that once the travelling imam has finished such a man is a l iq one who has fallen behind as well as a latecomer he therefore performs the first two rak ahs without reciting since in respect of them he is a l iq and performs the third and fourth rak ahs with recitation this is the answer written by muft az z al ra m n the chief muft of deoband and it bears the signatures of shaykh al hind may allah have mercy on him mawl n ashraf al th nw may allah have mercy on him and a rat mawl n anwar sh h kashm r these scholars argue from the following words of sh m

how a resident latecomer completes his prayer behind a travelling imam in the noon prayer a latecomer joined a travelling imam in the second rak ah of the noon prayer how should he complete the rest of his prayer scholars differ on this question according to the verifying scholars however the resident follower leaves off following the imam and becomes one praying alone he therefore performs all three remaining rak ahs as a latecomer does he performs the first of them with the recitation of al f ti ah and a s rah and then sits and he performs the last two with al f ti ah alone and does not sit between them al durr al mukht r states

how a follower who falls behind the imam completes his prayer a man's ablution broke during the second rak ah and by the time he had gone and performed ablution two rak ahs had passed how should he now perform his prayer after the imam gives the sal m in the case asked about after performing ablution he should pray the rak ahs that he missed because of the ritual impurity and he should do so without reciting then if the imam is still in the prayer he should join him otherwise he should complete his prayer on his own al durr al mukht r states

appointing a substitute when the imam's ablution breaks after the first sal m if a man's ablution breaks after he has given the sal m once is his prayer complete or not or should he perform ablution come back and give the second sal m and if he is the imam what is the ruling should he appoint someone to take his place or not according to the sounder view the second sal m is necessary so the man in question should perform ablution return and give the second sal m and if he is the imam he should appoint someone to take his place al durr al mukht r states al a w states al durr al mukht r states

a follower stepping forward as substitute imam without being appointed if an imam's ablution broke and he left and then a man came forward on his own from the second or third row and completed the prayer was the prayer valid or not if the follower took the imam's place before the imam had left the mosque and completed the prayer the prayer is valid whatever extended movement occurred was for the sake of putting the prayer right so it does not invalidate it care must be taken however that this does not involve turning one's back to the qiblah for otherwise the prayer becomes invalid fat w q kh n states sh m states

reciting from a written copy of the qur'an during prayer is it permissible to recite in prayer while looking at a copy of the qur'an or not and if it is permissible according to which imam in the view of the hanafis reciting from a written copy of the qur'an while in prayer invalidates the prayer the prayer becomes void whether it is an obligatory prayer a voluntary one or tar w al a w 's notes state

switching off a ringing mobile phone during prayer with extended movement if switching off a mobile phone calls for extended movement does the prayer become invalid or not extended movement invalidates the prayer so in the case asked about if extended movement was involved in switching off the mobile phone the prayer becomes invalid imd d al fatt states

saying to someone who sneezes during prayer a man sneezed during the prayer and said and another man answered him with has the prayer of either of them become invalid or not the man who sneezed and said has not invalidated his prayer though he should not say it deliberately the man who answered him with however has invalidated his prayer al a w 's notes state imd d al fatt states

a hanafi behind a sh fi imam who omitted the final sitting and prostrated for forgetfulness in the fifth rak ah a hanafi was praying behind a sh fi imam the sh fi imam did not sit at the fourth rak ah and then performed the prostration of forgetfulness in the fifth rak ah is the hanafi follower's prayer valid or not in the case asked about the sh fi imam did something that in the hanafi view is one of the things that invalidate the prayer the hanafi follower's prayer is therefore invalid and he must repeat the obligatory prayer fat w sh m states ta r r al mukht r states al a w s

a woman follower prompting the imam during prayer if a woman was praying behind an imam and she prompted him should the imam accept her prompt or not when a woman is among the followers and the imam makes a mistake during the prayer she should clap that is strike one hand against the other rather than prompt him aloud if she does prompt him aloud the imam should avoid taking the prompt from her and if he does take it no invalidity is caused to the prayer because according to the sounder view a woman's voice is not awrah something that must be kept concealed imd d al fatt states al ba r al r iq states

replying to a greeting in prayer with the words if someone greeted a man who was praying and in reply the man said the words what is the ruling on his prayer since this supplication was uttered by way of a reply and since in common usage such words are used to convey a greeting to another person out of caution the prayer is treated as invalid a al bukh r states imd d al fatt states

whether saying invalidates the prayer a man was praying either behind an imam or on his own and he began to say is his prayer valid or not and does it make a difference whether he did so by mistake or deliberately in the case asked about if he said by way of a reply or in order to alert someone the prayer becomes invalid whether he did so deliberately or by mistake but if he said it to drive away distracting thoughts or simply as a remembrance of allah then in both cases the prayer does not become invalid even if he said it deliberately al lamg riyyah states al a w

praying with chewing gum in the mouth a man had chewing gum in his mouth while praying and a little of its sweetness was going down his throat is his prayer valid or not in the case asked about the prayer is invalid there are in general several cases of praying with something in the mouth 1 if it is something sweet and its sweetness reaches the stomach it invalidates the prayer 2 if its sweetness has gone but the person keeps chewing it this too invalidates the prayer 3 if what is in the mouth is small and does not hinder recitation it does not invalidate the prayer but the prayer is disliked 4 if it is large and hinders recitation it invalidates the prayer sh m states

praying with a bottle of urine in one's pocket if a man has in his pocket a rotten egg whose contents have turned to blood or a bottle filled with urine is his prayer valid or not filth does not invalidate the prayer so long as it is in its natural place and source but it does invalidate the prayer when it is not in its natural place so in the case asked about if a man prayed with a bottle of urine in his pocket his prayer is invalid but if he prayed with a rotten egg full of blood in his pocket his prayer is valid because the filth is in its natural place sh m states al ba r al r iq states

a woman praying with some of her hair uncovered a woman prayed while some of her hair was showing is her prayer valid or not if as much as a quarter of the hair remained uncovered the prayer is invalid but if less than a quarter remained uncovered the prayer is not invalid al a w 's notes state sh m states fat w al laknaw stat

whether a kiss between a man and a woman during prayer invalidates the prayer the books of fiqh generally state that if a man is praying and a woman kisses him his prayer does not become invalid but that if a woman is praying and a man kisses her her prayer does become invalid if this ruling is correct what is the reason for the difference between the two cases on this question the verifying scholar ibn al hum m may allah have mercy on him said that is allah knows best the reason for the difference all mah abd al ayy al laknaw may allah have mercy on him said that analogy would require the prayer to be invalid in both cases but that the woman's prayer is invalid because a man's kiss has the status of intercourse in her regard since she is already receptive to it unlike a kiss given by a woman he gave a second reason as well that desire is generally stronger in women than in men so when a man kisses a woman she too feels desire and her prayer therefore becomes invalid that a man's kiss should invalidate

supplicating in prayer in a language other than arabic or with words resembling ordinary speech when a certain woman prays she recites this supplication in english while in prostration or while sitting o allah protect my husband and my children has this woman's prayer become invalid or not supplicating in a language other than arabic during prayer is strictly disliked makr h ta r m and any supplication that resembles ordinary human speech invalidates the prayer so in the case asked about the woman's prayer has become invalid and she should repeat it fat w q kh n states o allah forgive me

removing the doubt that using a loudspeaker invalidates the prayer some people declare praying aloud over a loudspeaker impermissible or at least doubtful is prayer over a loudspeaker sound or not and what is the reality of the objection raised about it namely that the congregation is taking its cue from someone other than the imam jad d fiqh mas il states is prayer by means of a loudspeaker valid or not in the beginning the scholars differed over this question some were of the view that the sound of a loudspeaker is not the imam's own voice but an echo of that voice on that view the movements of the followers would be based on a second sound rather than on the imam's voice and it is not permissible for a follower to move on the voice of anyone other than the imam against this others held that the use of a loudspeaker for prayer is nevertheless correct and that there is a precedent for it in the sharia a case in which worshippers moved on the word of a man who was outside the prayer when the ka bah repl

further research on praying over a loudspeaker some people declare praying aloud over a loudspeaker impermissible or at least doubtful is prayer over a loudspeaker sound or not and what is the reality of the objection raised about it namely that the congregation is taking its cue from someone other than the imam praying over a loudspeaker is permissible and sound without any doubt and it is not correct to declare it doubtful consider the following evidence that is if a worshipper acts on words spoken by someone outside the prayer his prayer is not invalidated the importance of acting on words spoken by someone outside the prayer appears in the question of praying over a loudspeaker some scholars say that prayer over a loudspeaker is not valid or that it is doubtful their reasoning is that the sound reaching the follower is not really the imam's voice the loudspeaker

switching off a ringing cell phone during prayer with a slight movement if a cell phone starts ringing during prayer may one switch it off with a slight movement or not if a phone rings during prayer it is permissible to switch it off with a slight movement that is to slip one hand into the pocket and turn it off the prayer will not be invalidated though it will be disliked a worshipper should put his phone on silent or switch it off before he begins to pray and should take particular care about this but if for some reason he forgets and it starts ringing during the prayer he should switch it off at once with a slight movement because a phone that goes on ringing causes real annoyance to the other worshippers and also disturbs his own prayer a hadith relates that the prophet was once leading the prayer when the sound of a child crying was he

praying with a jacket draped over the shoulders if a person drapes a jacket over his shoulders during prayer and does not put his arms through the sleeves does this create any fault or defect in the prayer or not draping a coat over the shoulders in this way during prayer without putting the arms through the sleeves comes under the ruling of sadl letting a garment hang loose and this is disliked so in the case asked about the prayer will be disliked consider what al hid yah states

letting the ends of a shawl or scarf hang loose in prayer is there any defect in the prayer if the worshipper lets one end of his scarf or shawl hang down or both ends and leaves them loose if he places one end of the scarf or shawl over his shoulder there is no defect in the prayer but if he leaves both ends loose and lets them hang the prayer will be disliked consider what imd d al fatt states

praying with the sleeves rolled up what is the position on praying with the sleeves rolled up that is leaving the elbows uncovered during prayer praying with the sleeves rolled up for no reason is disliked if a person has rolled them up for ablution or for some other reason he should roll them down and then begin the prayer if in his eagerness to catch a rak ah he has already entered the prayer it is better to roll them down little by little in a way that does not amount to a substantial action imd d al fatt states radd al mu t r states

hitching up the trousers when going into bowing or prostration if a worshipper gathers up his trousers or shirt as he goes down into prostration does this create any flaw in the prayer or not lifting the trousers with both hands while going down into bowing or prostration makes the prayer disliked but the prayer is not invalidated still making such a movement in prayer and turning it into a habit is objectionable and disliked and it may well lead to a substantial action and so become a cause of the prayer's invalidity avoiding it is therefore necessary imd d al fatt states

praying in the long kurtas kept at the mosque these days mosques keep long kurtas and ordinary people who come to pray straight from work put one on and pray in it since they do not think it proper to pray in their working clothes is there any dislike in praying this way or not some people say that because one would not go to a public gathering in these garments the prayer ought to be disliked is that correct on the face of it praying in such clothes is not disliked because they cover the body better than the person's own clothes do besides these clothes produce a kind of humility in the prayer when a man comes to allah's court he performs his worship in a garment set aside for it rather than in fashionable clothes furthermore the jurists agree that praying with the sleeves rolled up is disliked and some fatwa collections such as fat w ma m diyyah and fat w ra miyyah indicate that praying in sleeveless clothes is disliked as well so no dislike will arise in the prayer from these garments as for the view of some that they should be disliked because one does not go to a public ga

yawning in prayer and letting out the sound h h h h when a yawn comes during prayer should one place the right hand over the mouth or the left and when people let out the sound h h h h is that strictly disliked or mildly disliked yawning in prayer is an act of satan and should be avoided as far as one is able still if it comes involuntarily then in the standing position one should place the right hand over the mouth so that there is not too much movement and in the other postures one should use the left hand as for letting out the sound h h h h if it is done deliberately it is strictly disliked if it is involuntary it is excused just as certain letters escape a person when he sneezes though even then it is not free of dislike consider what radd al mu t r states

praying with coins bearing an image in one's pocket if metal coins bearing a raised image are kept in the pocket is the prayer valid or not having coins bearing an image in the pocket does no harm to the prayer they should however be kept carefully so that they do not fall on the place of prostration consider what imd d al fatt states radd al mu t r states

reciting a supplication in a language other than arabic during prayer if a person recited this supplication in urdu while sitting in prayer o allah forgive all the muslims what is the ruling on his prayer according to the preferred view supplicating in a language other than arabic during prayer is strictly disliked though there is also a view that it is only mildly disliked so if the person did not repeat that prayer there is no harm in it according to the view of some scholars consider what radd al mu t r states fat w q kh n states

praying with something the size of a chickpea in the mouth something the size of a chickpea was left in a man's mouth and he came to know of it only after the prayer was his prayer valid or not if something the size of a chickpea remains in the mouth the prayer will not be invalidated the prayer will however be disliked al fat w al t t rkh niyyah states fat al qad r states al fat w al hindiyyah states

lifting both feet during prostration for the length of three tasb s if someone lifted both feet during prostration for the length of three tasb s and then put them down again was his prayer valid or not keeping some part of the feet on the ground during prostration even a single toe is obligatory and indispensable without it the prayer is not valid since in the case asked about he put his feet down again after lifting them the prostration was performed it was however contrary to the sunnah method and for that reason the prayer will be disliked imd d al fatt states

praying in places where music is played will the prayer be valid if it is performed in places where music is played such as a market and the like if the place of prayer is separate and the sound of the music does not reach it there is no harm in praying there but praying in a place where music is played when the sound reaches the worshipper and disturbs his prayer is not free of dislike a hadith states that the prophet forbade praying in foul and unsuitable places any place where music is played comes under the same ruling so the prayer will be disliked consider what al bayhaq records imd d al fatt states

the imam's sutrah is sufficient for all the followers in a prayer hall the way in is at the end of the first row and worshippers keep arriving even after the prayer has begun so they usually have to pass in front of the followers there is a wall in front of the imam which serves as his sutrah the screen set up before a worshipper but it is not a sutrah for the followers will the wall in front of the imam be sufficient as a sutrah for all the followers or not the imam's sutrah is sufficient for all the followers so no other sutrah is needed however once the congregational prayer has ended if worshippers are praying their sunnah prayers passing in front of them will be forbidden likewise if a latecomer prays the part he missed after the imam's prayer has ended he too does not need a sutrah imd d al fatt states radd al mu t r states

using one's hand as a sutrah a man made his hand a sutrah the screen set up before a worshipper for the person praying behind him in this case will it be permissible to pass in front of that worshipper or not the point of a sutrah is this if there is something in front of the worshipper a cubit long and about the thickness of a finger then passing in front of him is permissible and no sin is incurred so when a whole hand has been used in place of a sutrah it is all the more clearly permissible and correct consider what imd d al fatt states

using one's own hand as a sutrah while passing in front of a worshipper if a person who is passing in front of someone praying lets his own hand hang down as a sutrah a screen in front of the worshipper and then passes by what is the ruling can the hand of the person passing serve as a sutrah or not the meaning of a sutrah is that something other than the body of the person passing stands between the worshipper and the one who passes so in the case asked about the hand of the person passing cannot serve as a sutrah consider what al hid yah states al bin yah shar al hid yah states the passages quoted show that a limb of the person passing cannot serve as a sutrah since the word

passing in front of a worshipper by hanging down a scarf or standing up a stick in order to pass in front of someone who is praying may a person hang down his scarf or stand his stick upright and then pass by or not on the face of it this appears permissible another form of it is that a person stands his stick upright passes by and takes hold of it again before it falls consider what radd al mu t r states all mah anwar sh h states umdat al fiqh states if the person passing has with him a stick

using a wire or a rope in place of a sutrah if there is no stick or anything similar available will placing a wire or a rope in front serve in place of a sutrah the screen set before a worshipper or not for a sutrah it is necessary that the object be about as thick as a finger and a wire or a rope is not usually that thick moreover the instruction is to fix the sutrah upright merely laying something down is not sufficient in the view of most scholars so in the case asked about it should not be sufficient either however since at a time of excuse there is room for drawing a line on the ground placing a rope or a wire will be correct all the more clearly but this only means that the worshipper's attention will remain settled and will not be scattered the person who passes in front will still be sinful since this is not enough to permit passing consider what imd d al fatt states

whether the small desks of a madrasah can serve as a sutrah what is the ruling on the sutrah the screen set before a worshipper and the size it must be and can the small desks in this madrasah which measure one cubit serve lengthwise in place of a sutrah or not setting up a sutrah is commendable al ba r al r iq describes prayer without a sutrah as disliked its size is given as one cubit roughly a foot and a half and the small desk in this madrasah can serve the purpose of a sutrah lengthwise the aim of a sutrah is that a person who is passing should realise that someone is praying there and that distinguishing mark is achieved by it al durr al mukht r states radd al mu t r states

using a hollow object as a sutrah is an object with a hollow space in it such as a small stand sufficient as a sutrah the screen set before a worshipper using an object with a hollow space in it as a sutrah is correct consider what a al bukh r states umdat al q r states al bin yah shar al hid yah states

the difference between a large and a small mosque in passing in front of a worshipper is there any transmitted position among the jurists in which whether in a small mosque a large mosque or open country the prohibition on passing in front of a worshipper is confined to the place of his prostration alone it appears from the statements of the jurists that if a person is praying in open country or in a large mosque the prohibition on passing in front of him is confined to the place of his prostration and as regards the place of prostration the soundest view is that the worshipper's gaze should not fall on the person passing in a small mosque one to which the definition of a large mosque does not apply passing in front of a worshipper is strictly disliked consider what al hid yah states al bin yah states

praying witr in congregation outside ramadan may the witr prayer be prayed in congregation outside the blessed month of ramadan or not congregation for witr is particular to the blessed month of ramadan outside ramadan if someone does it occasionally once or twice it is permissible since it is established from umar may allah be pleased with him and the companions may allah be pleased with them did not object to him to do it most of the time however is an innovation and disliked the reason being that regular practice of it is not established from the prophet or from the noble companions may allah be pleased with them mar q al fal states

praying witr before the ish prayer a man prayed witr before ish when he entered the mosque the witr was being prayed in congregation so he joined it and afterwards he prayed ish was his witr valid or not since the time of ish and of witr is one and the same if a person prays witr first out of forgetfulness the prayer will be valid and repeating it is not necessary but if he did so knowingly repeating it will be necessary because keeping the order between the two is necessary that is praying ish first is necessary and forgetfulness makes the requirement of order lapse consider what bad i al an i states

a sh fi leading the witr for half of ramadan and a anaf for the other half the worshippers at one mosque are partly anaf s and partly sh fi s in the blessed month of ramadan they all pray tar w together behind a single imam but for witr a separate congregation has to be held these men say that they should pray witr behind a single imam as well with a anaf imam for some days and a sh fi imam for the rest would that be correct all the worshippers are agreed on it please state the ruling in the case asked about it is correct to pray witr behind a single imam when the sh fi imam leads however he should lead the three rak ahs with one sal m all mah al nawaw may allah have mercy on him held this to be preferable yes if the sh fi imam gives the sal m at the end of two rak ahs the anaf follower should not give the sal m he should instead take the position of a latecomer and complete the remaining rak ah along with the qun t supplication the prayer will then be valid and there will be no need to pray it separately al ba r al r iq states

a sh fi praying witr as three rak ahs with one sal m behind a hanafi imam if a sh fi prays the witr prayer behind a hanafi that is three rak ahs units of prayer with a single sal m is his witr valid or not the witr of a sh fi who follows a hanafi imam is valid and correct this is because according to the sh fi s witr may be prayed as one rak ah three five seven nine or at most eleven imam al nawaw may allah have mercy on him held in shar al muhadhdhab that joining the three rak ahs together with a single sal m is better since it avoids the disagreement so in the case asked about the witr prayer is valid shar al muhadhdhab states

a hanafi praying witr with two sal ms behind a sh fi imam if a hanafi prays the witr prayer behind a sh fi with two sal ms what is the ruling if the sh fi imam leads three rak ahs units of prayer with a single sal m the hanafi's witr is valid if he leads it with two sal ms then the hanafi follower should stand up and complete his own witr his witr is valid and there is no need to pray it again al ba r al r iq states fat al qad r states

not adding a s rah in the third rak ah of witr out of ignorance a man used to treat the witr prayer like the maghrib prayer and did not add a s rah in the third rak ah unit of prayer now that he has learned the ruling does he have to make up all his past witr prayers or not adding a s rah after s rat al f ti ah in the third rak ah of witr is necessary and not knowing the ruling is no excuse so in the case asked about he must make up all the past witr prayers that he prayed without adding a s rah consider what imd d al fatt states shiyat al a w al mar q al fal states

praying witr before tar w a man prayed the witr prayer before tar w is he now required to repeat the witr or not it is permissible to pray witr before tar w as well though praying it after tar w is better so in the case asked about the witr prayer was valid and there is no need to repeat it consider what mar q al fal states al durr al mukht r states

reciting the qun t supplication when in doubt about the number of rak ahs of witr if someone becomes unsure about the number of rak ahs units of prayer in witr whether he has prayed two or three in which rak ah should he recite the qun t in the case asked about he should recite the qun t supplication in the very rak ah in which the doubt arose and he should also sit since it may be that this is the third rak ah he should then stand up for the third rak ah recite the qun t in that one too and complete the rak ah and at the end perform the prostration of forgetfulness sajdah sahw consider what al durr al mukht r states khul at

reciting some other supplication when one does not know the qun t if a person does not know the qun t supplication what should he recite if a person does not know the qun t supplication he should say or he should say or he should say three times consider what mar q al fal states

reciting s rat al ikhl in place of the qun t supplication if a person cannot recite the well known qun t supplication because of old age or weakness may he recite s rat al ikhl in its place the hanafi jurists have said that whoever cannot recite the qun t supplication should say three times or or three times this is better he may indeed also recite s rat al ikhl because when a person does not know the qun t supplication no particular supplication is definitively fixed for him and praising the generous one amounts to asking of him consider what al ba r al r iq states

raising the hands to supplicate in the third rak ah of witr and the congregation saying am n some people raise their hands and make supplication in the third rak ah of witr the imam recites the supplication while those praying behind him raise their hands and say am n is this established by any authentic hadith or not doing this in the third rak ah of witr is not established by any authentic narration traced back to the prophet a few reports are related from the companions and the successors and most of them are weak on account of layth ibn ab sulaym moreover prayer rests on stillness and dignity so acting in this way is not good consider what mu annaf ibn ab shaybah states

the proofs of the sh fi s and anbal s for raising the hands in the qun t of witr the sh fi s and anbal s keep their hands raised throughout the qun t supplication in witr what are their proofs is there any explicit authentic hadith for this or not after a search through the books it emerges that the sh fi s and anbal s have no explicit narration traced back to the prophet on this point they have argued from one hadith found in al mustadrak of al kim but the verifying scholars have said that is this narration is not generally to be found in al mustadrak of al kim apart from that they argue from the practice of a few companions and from narrations about supplication in general in which the raising of the hands is mentioned consider the proofs of the sh fi s al bay n states

the wording of the qun t of calamity as given in the books of fiqh what wording of the qun t of calamity is recorded in the books of fiqh what should one recite may a person recite whatever he wishes the supplication recorded in sh m is what is generally practised and that is what should be recited suitable wording other than it may also be recited but what is in sh m is better long wording sometimes becomes a burden for those praying behind and at times the standing after bowing even ends up longer than the second rak ah itself consider what sh m states n r al

reciting supplications other than the transmitted one in the qun t of calamity is it permissible to recite supplications other than the sunnah one in the qun t of calamity and what is the ruling if the imam adds other supplications alongside the sunnah one supplications other than the one that has been transmitted may also be recited in the qun t supplication provided they are not like worldly requests for example o allah grant a gold mine in such and such a place or arrange my marriage to such and such a girl sh m records this supplication all mah al khw razm has recorded a similar supplication in al kif yah shar al hid yah at 1 379

reciting the qun t of calamity to ward off afflictions should the qun t of calamity be recited for warding off afflictions for thirty days only or for longer than that when and at what time is it recited may it be recited in the fourth rak ah of ish the qun t of calamity should be recited to ward off afflictions and there is no limit of thirty days it is recited for as long as the affliction and trial is widespread it is recited in the second rak ah of fajr in the standing after bowing and it may also be recited in the fourth rak ah of ish consider what al durr al mukht r states
