making up a prayer that was deliberately omitted if someone deliberately omits a prayer does he have to make it up or not in the case described according to the majority of scholars he is obliged to make it up some of the hir s hold a different view bid yat al mujtahid states

making up missed sunnah prayers is making up missed sunnah prayers established or not sunnah prayers are not made up except for the sunnah of fajr which may be made up along with the obligatory prayer before midday and the sunnah prayed before uhr which may be prayed after the obligatory prayer apart from these two making up the sunnah prayers is not established see what a muslim states ibn m jah states taby n al aq iq stat

performing the lifetime make up prayer qa umr in congregation in some areas it is the custom to perform qa umr the make up of a lifetime's missed prayers collectively in congregation the way it is done is that on the last friday of ramadan after the friday prayer people pray all the prayers from fajr to ish behind an imam in congregation is this practice correct or wrong is there any evidence for it from the best generations of islam or not please explain with proofs this form of qa umr making up prayers on the last friday of ramadan and regarding that as sufficient for all the prayers one has missed is an innovation it has no basis in the sacred law and all the reports quoted in connection with it are fabricated consider what mull al al q r may allah have mercy on him writes

repeating al f ti ah and the prostration of forgetfulness if someone repeats some of the verses of s rat al f ti ah is the prostration of forgetfulness necessary or must the prayer be repeated if al f ti ah is repeated by mistake the prostration of forgetfulness is necessary and if it is repeated deliberately the prayer must be repeated as to how much repetition makes the prostration of forgetfulness necessary or makes repeating the prayer necessary sh m mentions most of al f ti ah while al a w mentions part of it the two can be reconciled by taking part to mean most that is more than half and there is ease in this so if more than half is repeated by mistake the prostration of forgetfulness is necessary and if it is done deliberately repeating the prayer is necessary consider what al a w states

repeating a single verse of al f ti ah and the prostration of forgetfulness if for some reason someone repeats a single verse of s rat al f ti ah during the prayer is the prostration of forgetfulness required or not if a single verse of s rat al f ti ah is repeated the prayer is valid and the prostration of forgetfulness is not necessary repeating most of al f ti ah however does make the prostration of forgetfulness necessary and there is ease in this position so repeating a single verse should not make the prostration of forgetfulness necessary consider what radd al mu t r states al ba r al r iq states

the prostration of forgetfulness after giving the sal m on both sides a necessary act was omitted in the prayer and the person remembered it only after giving the sal m should he perform the prostration of forgetfulness or must he repeat the prayer in the case described if he is still sitting in the same place after the prayer and has not spoken that is nothing has occurred that invalidates the prayer he should perform the prostration of forgetfulness and his prayer will be valid but if he has done something that invalidates the prayer then repeating the prayer is necessary consider what al durr al mukht r states

reciting the tashahhud while standing before al f ti ah if someone recites the tashahhud while standing before al f ti ah is the prostration of forgetfulness necessary or not in the case described if the tashahhud was recited in the second unit before s rat al f ti ah the prostration of forgetfulness becomes necessary reciting the tashahhud before s rat al f ti ah in the first third or fourth unit does not make the prostration of forgetfulness necessary consider what al a w states

reciting s rat al f ti ah in place of the tashahhud in the sitting someone recited s rat al f ti ah in place of al ta iyy t is the prostration of forgetfulness necessary or not in the case described if al f ti ah or some other recitation was made in place of the tashahhud the prostration of forgetfulness becomes necessary consider what al fat w al hindiyyah states

reciting s rat al f ti ah again after the prostration of recitation if a fi performs a prostration of recitation during the tar w prayer and then recites s rat al f ti ah again does the prostration of forgetfulness become necessary or not in the case described al f ti ah has been repeated after a s rah had already been joined to it so the prostration of forgetfulness is not necessary consider what shar munyat al mu all states al jawharah al nayyirah states

reciting the blessings on the prophet in the first sitting if someone recites the blessings on the prophet in the first sitting of an emphasised sunnah prayer is the prostration of forgetfulness necessary or not if a person recites the blessings on the prophet by mistake in the first sitting of the emphasised sunnah prayers the prostration of forgetfulness becomes necessary the four units after the friday prayer however are an exception among the emphasised sunnah prayers since it is not obligatory to pray those four units with a single sal m reciting the blessings on the prophet in the first sitting does not make the prostration of forgetfulness necessary consider what al durr al mukht r states

reciting part of a quiet prayer aloud and the prostration of forgetfulness if a person praying alone recites two or three verses aloud in a prayer that is recited quietly is the prostration of forgetfulness necessary or not and what is the ruling if an imam does this in the case described there is no prostration of forgetfulness upon a person praying alone if however the imam recites three short verses or one long verse aloud the prostration of forgetfulness becomes necessary consider what al hid yah states

a latecomer who gives the sal m with the imam by mistake if a latecomer gives the sal m along with the imam by mistake that is forgetfully does the prostration of forgetfulness become necessary or not if the latecomer gave the sal m at the same moment as the imam's sal m or before the imam's sal m the prostration of forgetfulness is not necessary if he gave it after the imam's sal m the prostration of forgetfulness is necessary and as a rule people give the sal m only after the imam so the prostration of forgetfulness will be necessary consider what al durr al mukht r states

not joining a s rah in the first unit made up by a latecomer a man missed three units of the prayer when he stood up after the imam's sal m he did not join a s rah to s rat al f ti ah in the first of the units he made up although he did join a s rah in the two units after it is his prayer valid or not and is the prostration of forgetfulness necessary or not the jurists are agreed that in the first unit which a latecomer performs after the imam's sal m joining a s rah is required so in the case described because it was omitted by mistake the prostration of forgetfulness is necessary and the prayer will be valid consider what radd al mu t r states

beginning a s rah in the third unit of an obligatory prayer if a person began reciting a s rah after s rat al f ti ah in the third unit of an obligatory prayer and then stopped when he remembered what is the ruling on his prayer is the prostration of forgetfulness necessary or not in the third unit of an obligatory prayer the sunnah is to recite s rat al f ti ah alone joining a s rah to it is contrary to what is preferable and is disliked it does not however make the prostration of forgetfulness necessary consider what shar munyat al mu all states

repeating the prostration of forgetfulness when it becomes necessary a second time after performing the prostration of forgetfulness a man began reciting s rat al f ti ah in place of al ta iyy t should he perform the prostration of forgetfulness a second time or not in the case described it is not required to perform the prostration of forgetfulness a second time the first one is enough for repeating the prostration of forgetfulness is not prescribed consider what taby n al aq iq states khul at al fat w states sh m states

reciting s rat al f ti ah after the tashahhud in the sitting if someone recited the tashahhud in the sitting and then began reciting s rat al f ti ah is the prostration of forgetfulness necessary or not if s rat al f ti ah was recited after the tashahhud in the first sitting the prostration of forgetfulness is required otherwise it is not consider what shiyat al a w states

standing up after the tashahhud in the final sitting and then returning a man sat in the fourth unit and recited the tashahhud then stood up when he remembered he sat back down should he now recite the tashahhud again or should he perform the prostration of forgetfulness in the case described he should not recite the tashahhud a second time the first is enough he should perform the prostration of forgetfulness and then complete the prayer by reciting the tashahhud the blessings on the prophet the supplication and so on consider what al durr al mukht r states mar q al fal states

performing the prostration of forgetfulness after turning the chest away from the qiblah a man forgot the prostration of forgetfulness gave the sal m on both sides and also turned his chest away from the qiblah can he still perform the prostration of forgetfulness or must he repeat the prayer in the case described as long as he has not left the mosque he should perform the prostration of forgetfulness and complete the prayer the prayer will be valid and repeating it is not necessary but once he has left the mosque repeating the prayer is necessary consider what al durr al mukht r states

following the imam in the prostration of forgetfulness before finishing the tashahhud the imam began the prostration of forgetfulness before the follower had finished the tashahhud what should the follower do should he finish it or follow the imam at once in the case described the follower should quickly finish the tashahhud and then join the imam in the prostration of forgetfulness there is also a view that he should follow the imam at once but that entails leaving out a necessary act whereas finishing the tashahhud involves no more than a delay which is the lighter of the two difficulties for that reason this course should be adopted consider what al a w al mar q al fal states

a latecomer who does not sit at the end of his first make up unit a man missed three units of a uhr prayer when he made them up he did not sit after the first unit but sat after two units is the prostration of forgetfulness necessary for him or not in the case described the way to make up the missed units is that after the imam's sal m he should sit at the end of the first unit then pray two units and sit at the last one completing the prayer in this way but if someone did not sit at the first unit and instead sat at the second one after the imam that too is permissible and valid by juristic preference neither the prostration of forgetfulness nor repeating the prayer is required consider what majma al zaw id states

forgetting to join a s rah to al f ti ah and the prostration of forgetfulness if a person forgets to join a s rah and goes down into bowing must he return to the standing position or should he complete the bowing and perform the prostration of forgetfulness at the end in the case described he should return recite the s rah and then perform the bowing again but if he did not return and performed the prostration of forgetfulness at the end the prayer is valid consider what shiyat al a w states mar q al fal states

performing the prostration of forgetfulness when it was not needed the prostration of forgetfulness was not necessary yet a person performed it what is the ruling the author of al durr al mukht r has said that it invalidates the prayer but all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him said that according to the position on which the fatwa is given the prayer is not invalidated consider what al durr al mukht r states

reciting aloud in the last two units of uhr if someone recited part of the recitation aloud in the last two units of uhr is the prostration of forgetfulness due from him or not note that he recited quietly in the first two units for the imam reciting aloud is necessary in the prayers that are recited aloud and in the same way reciting quietly is necessary in the prayers that are recited quietly so if he recites aloud where the recitation should be quiet the amount of three verses or more the prostration of forgetfulness becomes necessary if a man is praying alone he has the choice of reciting quietly where the recitation is aloud but he does not have the choice of reciting aloud where it should be quiet so the same ruling applies to him too namely that if he recites aloud the amount of three verses or more the prostration of forgetfulness becomes necessary all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him

the measure of three verses or of one long verse what is the measure of three verses or of one long verse the measure of a single verse by which the obligatory recitation of the prayer is fulfilled is that it should equal three short verses and the measure of three short verses is 10 words and 30 letters consider what al durr al mukht r states

performing the prostration of recitation after reciting several more verses a man recited a verse of prostration during the prayer but did not perform the prostration he realised it after reciting three more verses what should he do now in the case described he should perform the prostration of recitation immediately as soon as he remembers and the prayer will be valid mar q al fal states if he remembers while performing some other element of the prayer he should still perform it at once and it is recommended that he repeat tha

where the prostration falls in s rah d is the prostration of s rah d at the word or at and if someone performed the prostration at instead of at what is the ruling in the case described the prostration of s rah d is at if someone performed it at then according to one view it is still valid in places other than s rah d if a person prostrates before the word of prostration a second prostration becomes necessary and the prostration of forgetfulness becomes necessary as well consider what bad i al an i states mar q al fal states

repeating a verse of prostration while riding if a man riding a mount keeps reciting a verse of prostration are several prostrations due or only one if a verse of prostration is repeated while riding and the person is in prayer only one prostration is necessary if he is not in prayer several prostrations are necessary in the same way on a sea going ship repeating a verse of prostration will make several prostrations necessary the statements of the jurists suggest that only one is necessary but in their day ships sailed by the wind whereas in our time the crew drive them by engine and the like so because the place does change several will be necessary consider what al durr al mukht r states

hearing a verse of prostration on the radio if someone hears a verse of prostration on the radio is the prostration necessary or not in the case described if the recitation had been recorded on some device a cassette a cd a tape recorder and so on and that recording is being broadcast on the radio then the prostration is not necessary for the listener but if a reciter is actually reciting and he recites a verse of prostration the prostration of recitation is necessary for the listener in short the prostration of recitation becomes necessary through the recitation itself it does not become necessary through a copy or a reproduction of it consider what shiyat al a w al mar q al fal states

prostration of recitation and reward for listening to the qur'an on a tape recorder while listening to the noble qur'an on a tape recorder or a cd player a verse of prostration is recited what is the ruling for the listener does he have to prostrate and if the prostration is not necessary does he still earn reward for listening to that recitation for the prostration of recitation to become necessary upon a listener he must hear a valid recitation and a valid recitation only comes about through reason and discernment a tape recorder or a cd player is nothing more than a device that transmits sound the prostration of recitation is therefore not necessary a parallel to this is found in the words of the jurists who write that prostration does not become necessary on hearing a verse from birds or from an echo as for reward that is achieved simply by the words of allah reaching one's ears and it is earned by staying silent and listening with due respect consider what imd d al fatt states

prostration of recitation when a child recites a verse of prostration if a young child who has not reached puberty recites a verse of prostration is the prostration necessary upon the listener or not in the case described if the child is old enough to understand the prostration of recitation is necessary upon the listener otherwise if the child lacks discernment the prostration of recitation is not necessary upon the listener consider what imd d al fatt states fat al qad r states

prostration of recitation when most of a verse of prostration is recited if someone recites only the words in which the prostration is mentioned but does not recite the whole verse for example he recites does the prostration of recitation become necessary or not in the case described if he recited most of the verse of prostration then the prostration of recitation is necessary otherwise it is not so reciting alone does not make the prostration necessary consider what al fat w al hindiyyah states

repeating the same verse of prostration in prayer after having already prostrated a fi recited a verse of prostration during tar w and then performed the prostration after that he recited the same verse again what is the ruling in this case in the case described there is no need to prostrate a second time the first prostration is enough consider what al fat w al hindiyyah states bihisht z war states if a person recites the same verse of prostration several times during a prayer only one prostration is necessary whether he recites it every time and performs the prostration at the end or recites it once performs the prost

hearing different verses of prostration from different people a person is sitting in one place and is hearing different verses of prostration from different people how many prostrations become necessary in the case described since he is hearing different verses of prostration from different people a separate prostration becomes necessary for each verse so the number of prostrations that become necessary will match the number of verses he hears consider what sh m states

repeating the prostration when the sitting changes if someone heard a verse of prostration inside the mosque and then heard the same verse in the mosque courtyard the courtyard being outside the mosque proper what is the ruling in the case described the courtyard lies outside the mosque so two prostrations become necessary because the sitting has changed consider what al fat w al hindiyyah states fat w q kh n states shiyat al a w states

moving from one spot to another within the same place if the mosque courtyard is not outside the mosque but both areas are part of the mosque itself how many prostrations are required now in the case described only one prostration is necessary because the place is one and the same imd d al fatt states

the imam intending the prostration of recitation during the bowing if the imam made the intention of the prostration of recitation during the bowing but the followers did not is the followers' prostration fulfilled or not there is a difference of opinion on this question but the view closest to sound reasoning is that the imam's intention should suffice on behalf of the follower just as when a travelling imam makes the intention of a traveller's prayer or a resident imam makes the intention of a resident's prayer it suffices for the followers so in the case described once the imam made the intention of the prostration of recitation during the bowing that intention suffices on behalf of the followers and the prostration of all of them is fulfilled the better course however is to perform a separate prostration in an audible prayer so that ordinary people who do not know the ruling are not left confu

whether compensation must be paid for a missed prostration of recitation if someone misses a prostration of recitation does he pay compensation for it or not it is fine to pay compensation for a prostration of recitation as a precaution but it is not necessary consider what sh m states a rat muft mu ammad shaf wrote in jaw hir al fiqh if prostrations of recitation have been missed the precautionary course is to give one and three quarter s r of wheat or its value in charity for each prostration jaw hir al fiqh 1 393 rulings on compensation for prayer fasting and the like maktabah d r al ul m karachi

performing the prostration of recitation by bowing outside prayer can a person perform the prostration of recitation by bowing when he is outside prayer or not in the case described although some scholars have held it valid to fulfil it by bowing in the view of the leading researchers it is not valid to do so because bowing is not an act of worship in its own right the wording of al fat w al hindiyyah however indicates that it is permissible for someone who is ill consider what al durr al mukht r states

praying while seated on a chair what is the ruling on praying an obligatory prayer while seated on a chair as long as a person is able to stand it is not permissible to pray an obligatory prayer sitting down and if he is unable to prostrate he may pray sitting those who are able neither to stand nor to prostrate are instructed first of all to pray seated on the ground praying on a chair is not correct if a person is able to stand but unable to prostrate the requirement of standing falls away this does not mean that praying on a chair becomes permissible standing falls away because the real object of the prayer is the prostration while standing and bowing are only a means to it for this same reason praying seated is better once the prostration has fallen away since sitting resembles p

standing for a person who is unable to prostrate a man is able to stand but does not have the strength to go down into prostration he can however sit on the floor with his legs stretched out and pray with gestures which posture is better for him to pray in if this man is unable to prostrate standing is waived for him until he recovers so he should pray seated performing the bowing and the prostration by gestures because standing is only a means to the prostration and once the prostration is gone standing falls away consider what al mabs states taby n al aq iq states

prostrating on a table placed in front of oneself a man with a valid excuse prays on a chair if he places a table in front of him and prostrates on it what is the ruling if a person is so ill or so disabled that even sitting is difficult and he prays on a chair then it is valid for him to prostrate on a table or something similar but placing a board in front of him is not necessary a gesture is enough for the prostration and prostrating on a table also counts as a gesture consider what al durr al mukht r states

a table in front is not required for someone praying on a chair a man with a valid excuse is praying seated on a chair and is able to place a table in front of him and prostrate on it is prostrating on the table necessary or not some muftis say that placing a table is necessary see for example fat w bayyin t 2 390 and a san al fat w 4 54 when a man with a valid excuse prays on a chair it is not necessary to place a table in front of him the reason is that for a prostration actually to take place the forehead one of the two hands one of the two knees and one toe of the feet must be placed on the ground even if only for a moment without this no prostration takes place these things cannot happen when prostrating on a chair and a table so a man with a valid excuse should perform the bowing and the prostration by gestures and placing a table is not necessary consider what imd d al fatt states

facing the qiblah when praying lying down if a person has a valid excuse and prays lying down should he point his feet towards the qiblah or should he lie on his side and turn his feet away from the qiblah in the case described a person with a valid excuse who prays lying down should turn his face towards the qiblah and bend his legs slightly so that they do not point towards the qiblah this method is better and preferable to praying lying on one's side consider what al durr al mukht r states

the sharia ruling on a person with a chronic excuse a man suffers from a problem of breaking wind after performing ablution his ablution does not last more than 5 minutes he wants to know the ruling on praying in congregation and on reciting the qur'an and performing the sunnah and voluntary prayers and so on he has sought medical treatment for several years but it has not proved helpful please inform us of the sharia ruling on this if the complete time of one prayer passes even once in such a state that the wind keeps breaking continuously that is it does not stop even long enough for him to perform ablution and complete the prayer of that time then this man is a person with a chronic excuse the ruling for him is that he must perform a fresh ablution for every prayer time with that ablution he may go on praying the obligatory prayer the sunnah and voluntary prayers reciting the qur'an and praying whatever he wishes whether on time or as a make up prayer the breaking of wind will not break his ablution what breaks his ablution is the expiry of the prayer time so a separate ablution is required for each pra

the prayer of a person with a wound that keeps bleeding 1 my hand was cut i cleaned the wound until i was satisfied that it had dried and there was no blood at all then i performed ablution and once the wound was dry i put a plaster on it then i went for the friday prayer two hours later i removed the plaster and saw some traces of blood on it was my friday prayer valid 2 would it have been correct for me to clean the wound put a plaster on it and then wipe over it is it necessary for the bleeding from the wound to stop what should a person do on such an occasion 3 i intended to read the qur'an but because of the traces of blood on the wound i was not in a state of ablution every time i wiped the wound with a tissue traces of if blood gets onto the dressing of a wound but does not appear on the outside that is it is not flowing blood the ablution is not broken so in case 1 the wound was cleaned and washed ablution was performed and the dressing was then applied two hours later traces of blood were found on the plaster dressing since this does not come under the ruling of flowing blood and it did not appear on the outside the ablution was still intact and the friday prayer was valid 2 the blood had been washed away so wiping over the dressing after applying it is correct on such an occasion when blood came out and he then washed it and cleaned it and applied the plaster dressing the prayer an

attending congregational prayer in the mosque while wearing a colostomy bag a man is ill a bag has been fitted to his abdomen into which waste the kind that normally comes out through the back passage passes through a tube what is the ruling on this man coming to the mosque and praying with the congregation does this fall under the ruling of bringing filth into the mosque or not and does the presence or absence of a bad smell make a difference to the ruling in ordinary circumstances it is strictly disliked to bring foul smelling things or filth into the mosque especially where there is a risk of soiling the mosque but for a man with a chronic excuse as in the case described this bag takes the ruling of his stomach and belly so if there is no bad smell and it is covered and it does not cause people revulsion then it is permissible and correct for him to go to the mosque yes filth passing into the bag does break his ablution but since this man has a chronic excuse and filth keeps coming out of his stomach continuously his ablution will only break with the expiry of the prayer time unless some other thing that breaks ablution occurs

where a sharia journey begins is the sharia travel distance counted from one's house or from the boundary of the city the sharia travel distance begins from the last house of the city before that a sharia journey has not begun even if the person has left his house consider what mu annaf abd al razz q states al hid yah states sh m states

where a journey begins and ends when the city is very large if a person sets out on a journey and the city he travelled from is very large such as bombay or karachi when does his journey end on his return when he enters the city or when he reaches his house and when does the journey begin when he leaves his house or when he leaves the city in the case described the man's sharia journey comes to an end as soon as he enters the city and his sharia journey begins once he passes the last house of the city consider what mu annaf abd al razz q states it also states

where a sharia journey begins when two settlements have merged through growth these days in some places two settlements become joined together because of population growth in such a case from where is the journey reckoned from one's own settlement or from the adjoining settlement in the case described even though the second settlement adjoins the first if the two have separate names and separate boundaries have been fixed for each then both count as independent settlements and the sharia journey is reckoned from the point at which a person passes beyond his own settlement but if they have been joined in such a way that the government has made them one and the second settlement serves as a district of the first then it is part of the city and so the rulings of a sharia journey will only apply once a person passes beyond it consider what al durr al mukht r states

having more than one home town a a man married in india and his wife lives there he also married in africa and that wife lives in africa do both count as his home town can a person have more than one home town b if a person holds the passports of two countries do both count as his home town on that basis in the eyes of the sacred law a person may have more than one home town if a man has married four women and all four are in separate cities or towns and he visits each of them from time to time then he has four home towns so in case a both india and africa are home towns for the man described b in the eyes of the sacred law merely obtaining a country's passport is no proof that it is a person's home town unless he takes up permanent residence there consider what bad i al an i states

shortening the prayer at the airport on the return journey if a person has returned from a journey and is at the airport and he lives in newtown should he shorten his prayer at the airport or pray it in full a traveller shortens his prayer until he enters his own city or forms the intention of staying for 15 days so in the case described the man will shorten his prayer at the airport because the airport lies outside newtown and is counted as a separate area consider what mu annaf abd al razz q states lamg riyyah states

the distance at which the prayer is shortened according to the anaf school what distance must a person cover for the rulings of travel to apply in the anaf school according to the hir al riw yah the school's authoritative transmitted position the distance is three days' journey at a moderate pace apart from this no account has been taken of farsakhs miles and the like consider in the present age however for the convenience and ease of ordinary people the later scholars have taken farsakhs and miles into account there are also various positions on fixing the number of farsakhs 15 16 18 and 21 for example have been reported from the three imams then there are also differing views as to which position is the one given in fatwa some s

covering the travel distance without having intended it from the outset a man set out from roshnee to go to johannesburg on reaching there he decided to go on to laudium is he now a traveller or a resident each stage on its own is less than the travel distance while the two together equal the sharia distance a person shortens his prayer only if at the very start of the journey he intends to cover the whole sharia distance otherwise he does not so in the case described this man is a resident not a traveller yes on the return journey he will shorten his prayer consider what al durr al mukht r states

shortening the prayer on the way back after giving up the journey a man set out from johannesburg for durban after he had travelled 50 kilometres he gave up the intention of going any further will he now shorten his prayer on the way back or not in the case described since he did not cover the sharia distance he will not shorten his prayer on the way back he will pray it in full consider what al durr al mukht r states

shortening the prayer after taking the longer route that meets the sharia travel distance a man sets out from home and there are two roads to his destination one is shorter and the other most probably covers the sharia travel distance if he takes the road that covers the sharia distance may he shorten his prayers after 30 kilometres or not in the case described if he intends to travel to that destination and his strong assumption is that the road covers the sharia distance then after 30 kilometres he will shorten his prayers and will not pray them in full consider what al fat w al hindiyyah states

repeating a prayer that was prayed in full while travelling someone did not shorten his prayers on the way because he thought the distance was less than the sharia limit later on checking he learnt that it was in fact the sharia travel distance must he repeat those prayers or not and what is the ruling on the return journey in the case described if he sat for the first sitting the obligation has been discharged but praying in this way is disliked and repeating the prayer within its time is necessary on the return journey he will shorten his prayers consider what al ba r al r iq states

a traveller deliberately praying in full on a sharia journey if a anaf traveller deliberately prays the full four rak ahs what is the ruling for a anaf traveller to pray in full deliberately while on a sharia journey is strictly disliked and a serious sin and repeating the prayer is necessary consider what sh m states mar q al fal states fat

whether travelling away and leaving one's belongings behind cancels a place of temporary residence a man's home town is durban but he is staying in lenz and his belongings and so on are also in lenz lenz however is not his home town it is only a place of temporary residence he then travelled to white river and on his return he intends to stay in lenz for only 5 days during those 5 days will he shorten his prayers or pray them in full our senior scholars may allah have mercy on them differ on this question some of them hold that any journey at all cancels a place of temporary residence others hold that it is not cancelled because his belongings are still there and so when he returns he will pray in full among the scholars of our own time a rat muft rash d ib a rat muft abd al satt r ib a rat muft far d ib and some others have given the fatwa on this latter view for the sake of ease consider what al ba r al r iq states

praying maghrib again when the sun becomes visible once more if a man prayed maghrib at the airport and the plane then flew westwards so that the sun became visible again and afterwards set once more does he have to pray maghrib a second time in the case described it is not necessary to pray maghrib again consider what a san al fat w states question a man performed the maghrib prayer and then boarded an aeroplane the plane flew westwards so fast that the sun became visible again does he then have to pray maghrib a second time it is not necessary to pray maghrib again

travel undertaken while menstruating a woman was menstruating when she left johannesburg and by the time she reached durban she had become pure she is staying in durban for three days will she shorten her prayers there or pray them in full as far as these rulings are concerned travel undertaken while menstruating counts for nothing it is not taken into account so a menstruating woman who becomes pure during her stay in durban will pray in full on the return journey however she will shorten her prayers consider what sh m states

a second view on the journey of a menstruating woman a second view on the journey of a menstruating woman on the question just discussed one view is that the journey is reckoned from the place where she became pure as was mentioned above other jurists however have written that what counts is the point at which the journey began not the place where she became pure on that view the woman in question will shorten her prayers in durban consider what all mah shurunbul l may allah have mercy on him says

becoming pure at the place of stay and praying there a woman is travelling from joburg to durban while menstruating and she became pure on reaching pietermaritzburg she will now pray in full for the rest of the way to durban because durban is 60 kilometres from there that ruling is already known and is recorded in fat w d r al ul m zakariyy what i now want to know is a further ruling if this woman's menstruation continued until she reached durban her stay in durban is 16 days and she became pure 6 days after arriving there is she then like a resident or like a traveller for the remaining ten days that is will she shorten her prayers or pray them in full travel undertaken while menstruating is not taken into account so in the case described since the woman became pure 6 days after reaching durban she is like a resident she will pray the full prayers for the remaining ten days on the return journey to joburg however she will shorten her prayers consider what shar munyat al mu all states shiyat al a w states fat

shortening the prayer when the distance is covered without intending it what do the scholars say about this case zayd travelled to a place a which is 60 kilometres from his home and that place was all he intended from there for some reason he travelled on to another place b which is 40 kilometres from a but when he reached b his intention was to stay there for two hours and then return through a and go home will he shorten his prayers at b or pray them in full and when he comes back to the first place a on his return will he shorten them or pray in full in the case described zayd will pray in full at b because place b is 40 kilometres from place a which is less than the sharia distance on the way home however the total comes to 100 kilometres so he will shorten his prayers at a consider what al durr al mukht r states

shortening the prayer when staying at one's in laws' home if a husband goes to his in laws' home and a wife goes to her parents' home will they shorten their prayers or pray them in full if after the marriage the husband settled permanently in that same town it now counts as their home town and they will pray in full there even if the husband himself does not live in that town but his wife and family are permanently settled there he will still pray in full but if the wife moved to her husband's home after the marriage and the two of them live in another town then when the husband visits his in laws and the wife visits her parents they will shorten their prayers if they intend to stay less than fifteen days the correct view is that marrying in a place does not by itself bring the ruling of praying in full unless the person makes it his home consider what fat w q

a married woman shortening her prayers at her parents' home if a girl is married into a town more than 81 kilometres away from her parents and she then comes to her parents' home to spend ten days will she shorten her prayers or pray them in full after the marriage the girl made her husband's town her home town and took up residence there so if she then comes to her parents' home to spend ten days she will shorten her prayers consider what al ba r al r iq states imd d al a k m states if a wife does not li

shortening the prayer when a man visits his wife whom he has settled in another town a man lives in one place and has settled his wife in another and he goes back and forth to his wife's place regularly on these visits if he intends to stay less than 15 days will he shorten his prayers or pray them in full in the case described on these visits the husband will pray in full at his wife's place because it is a home town of his and a person may have more than one home town consider what al fat w al sir jiyyah states al ba r al r iq states mar q al fal states

a resident praying behind a traveller recites in the rak ahs he completes on his own if a resident prays two rak ahs behind a traveller and then stands up to complete his own remaining two rak ahs should he recite in those two rak ahs or not the wording of some books of fiqh shows that in these rak ahs he is like a person praying alone so there is no harm in reciting indeed reciting ought to be recommended some other books however record the view that he does not recite consider what bad i al an i states shar al niq yah states

a anaf traveller's prayer behind a sh fi traveller who prays in full a anaf traveller followed a sh fi traveller in the uhr prayer and the sh fi prayed the full four rak ahs is the anaf 's prayer valid or not if the imam's intention is taken into account the anaf 's prayer is valid because in the sh fi school praying 2 rak ahs is a concession and praying 4 is also allowed most jurists however have written that what counts is the school of the follower and in the light of that view the follower's prayer ought not to be valid but a rat th nw may allah have mercy on him said that taking the follower's school into account amounts to this the imam must complete the obligatory elements as the follower holds them to be and must not do anything that invalidates the prayer if the imam omits something that is merely necessary in the follower's school that is still enough for the prayer b

a traveller who prays in full behind a resident and then repeats the prayer after it is invalidated if a traveller prayed four rak ahs behind a resident and the imam's prayer became invalid then when the traveller prays his prayer again will he pray four rak ahs or two in the case described since the imam's prayer became invalid the traveller will pray two rak ahs if he prays on his own consider what sh m states al fat w al hindiyyah states umdat al fiqh states a traveller may follow a resident imam within the time of the prayer so if a traveller follows a resident imam within the time he prays the full four rak ahs in order to keep with the imam if he then invalidates that prayer or it becomes invalid for some reason and he now prays alone or follows

shortening the prayer when the return route covers the sharia distance a man travelled from springs to lenz by a route on which the sharia distance was not covered so he did not shorten his prayers in lenz his return journey however was by another route that does amount to the sharia distance may he shorten his prayers on the way back or not in the case described the man will shorten his prayers on the return journey consider what sh m states

a person remains a traveller until he enters his home town a man has been staying at the madrasah for several years at first he used to go home after two or three weeks now he goes every week his home is in roshnee and it is obvious that a resident of roshnee is not a traveller here he went to durban for a day on some errand and has come back is he now a traveller or a resident before he reaches home a person who has covered the sharia travel distance is treated as a traveller until he enters his own town or forms the intention of staying somewhere for 15 days or more in which case he will then pray in full consider what al fat w al hindiyyah states sh m states see also

a traveller's prayer when the resident imam breaks the prayer a traveller was following a resident imam and in the sitting after the second rak ah the imam deliberately broke the prayer should the traveller now pray two rak ahs or four because of the ta r mah the opening takb r he made earlier in the case described if the traveller joined the imam for an obligatory prayer he will pray two rak ahs but if he joined him intending a voluntary prayer he will pray four consider what al fat w al hindiyyah states al ba r al r iq states

passing again through a place of temporary residence after travelling from it a man travelled to another country and stayed there for six months then travelled on to another place about 600 kilometres away when he returns to the first place intending to stay only five days will he shorten his prayers or pray them in full and what should he do if he leads the prayer as imam a place of temporary residence is cancelled by a sharia journey provided that no belongings and the like are left there and there is no intention of returning so in the case described when he comes back and intends to stay less than 15 days he will shorten his prayers and if he leads the prayer as imam he must still shorten it consider what bad i al an i states sh m states

a travelling follower who intends to pray in full behind a travelling imam a traveller came to the mosque and going by what he thought most likely made the intention of praying four rak ahs of uhr behind the imam afterwards he learnt that the imam was a traveller too is his prayer valid or not a mistake in the number of rak ahs does not invalidate the prayer so in the case described the travelling follower's prayer behind the travelling imam is valid one doubt may arise here he did not know the imam's situation so how can the prayer be valid the answer is that it need not be known at the outset learning of it during the prayer or immediately after it is enough for the prayer to be valid consider what al lamg riyyah states al durr al mukht r st

a traveller who forgetfully stands up for a third rak ah and then remembers a traveller was praying uhr and forgetfully stood up for a third rak ah and then remembered that he was a traveller what should he do now in the case described if the traveller had sat for the first sitting and remembered before making the prostration of the third rak ah he should return to the sitting and complete his prayer if he remembered after the prostration he should complete four rak ahs and the last two will count as the sunnah of uhr in either case sajdah sahw becomes necessary because of the delay in giving sal m but if he had not sat for the first sitting and had also made the prostration of the third rak ah then his prayer is invalid and he must pray the shortened prayer again from the beginning consider what al fat w al t t rkh niyyah states

one home town is cancelled by taking another as one's home a man's home town was benoni he moved from there to balfour and made it his home after his marriage he came back to benoni with his family and made benoni alone his home town will he now be a traveller or a resident when he goes to balfour if a person leaves his home town and takes another place as his home town the first home town is cancelled so the questioner's home town is now benoni balfour is no longer his home town and when he goes there he will count as a traveller consider what al durr al mukht r states

shortening the prayer at the place where one's parents live a man used to live with his parents and then moved from there to another place where he works is it correct for him now to treat his place of work as his home town and to count himself a traveller in his former home town in the case described once the questioner moved to his place of work with his family and his belongings and made up his mind to live there that place of work became his home town so when he comes to the first place he counts as a traveller because the mere presence of his parents there is not enough to make it his home town consider what al hid yah states bad i al an i states

a man's claim that his parents' town is also his home town a man has moved with his family to the place where he works but his parents live somewhere else he regards his parents' town as his home town as well is this correct or not in the case described if the man has not made his place of work his home town but merely intends to stay there and he treats the place where his parents live as his home town then that is correct because a home town is not cancelled by a place of temporary residence if he counts both places as home towns certain conditions apply for example that he married in the second place and his wife lives there or that he has a house in both places with his belongings there and that he intends to go on living there and has not moved away and so on as the question stands however it appears that for this man the place of work has the status of a home town and his parents' place is not his

covering the travel distance within the area around one's own town if someone travels 90 kilometres around his own town for example lenasia eldorado park and daxina will he shorten his prayers or not since in common usage lenasia and daxina are counted as a single settlement he will not shorten his prayers because his travelling took place within the town limits a person counts as a traveller in the sharia sense only once he leaves the town limits intending a sharia journey consider what sh m states

a travelling imam who leads four rak ahs and then performs sajdah sahw a travelling imam mistakenly led four rak ahs and performed sajdah sahw at the end is the prayer valid or must it be repeated in the anaf school shortening the prayer is necessary for a traveller and there is no room for praying in full if he did sit for the first sitting the obligation has been discharged but praying in this way is disliked if he did it deliberately he is gravely sinful and repeating the prayer within its time is necessary in either case the prayer of the resident followers is not valid and they must pray it again consider what al ba r al r iq states

praying optional prayers while driving on a journey a man drives along a perfectly straight road where very little effort is required for instance he is on the road to cape town and the car practically drives itself may he pray optional prayers while doing so the jurists have permitted a person to pray outside the city while riding a mount even if he holds a whip in his hand and uses it to startle and prod the animal they counted all such movements as minor actions reasoning by analogy from this a person may pray optional prayers while driving keeping one hand on the steering wheel if he uses both hands however the prayer becomes invalid because that amounts to excessive movement one should also make sure that the road is open and that the traffic is not heavy otherwise it is better to limit oneself to words of remembrance since protecting one's life takes precedence even over optional prayers consider what shiyat al a w state

combining two prayers while travelling we are often on the road with our luggage and stopping the vehicle along the way is not without danger may we combine two prayers since it is permitted in another school according to the hanafi school combining two prayers in the real sense is not permitted what is permitted is a formal combination jam r which is done as follows one prays zuhr at the very end of the first shadow length and asr at the beginning of the second shadow length this is valid according to one opinion or one prays zuhr at the end of the second shadow length and asr at the beginning of the third which counts as a formal combination according to the other opinion maghrib and ish are handled in the same way one prays maghrib just before the twilight disappears and ish once it has disappeared and this is correct consider what a al bukh r states

why hanafis do not combine two prayers when the sh fi s permit it according to the sh fi s a traveller may combine two prayers someone raises the objection why then is it not permissible for a hanafi to do the same he will not accept the matter however much it is explained to him and he is a salafi type of person all the imams derived the rulings of the sharia from its evidence with complete honesty and integrity and whichever position they found established by the evidence and the texts they judged to be the stronger one it is therefore necessary for each of us to follow the imam whose follower he is and not to follow his own desires otherwise religion will no longer be religion but the pursuit of whim in this question too the hanafis in the light of the evidence and the decisive texts have preferred the position that combining two prayers is not permissible and that wherever narrations about combining two prayers occur they do not mean a real combination but a formal one that is one praye

the view that combining two prayers is permissible from the writings of some of our jurists and some of our senior scholars it appears that a hanafi may combine two prayers zuhr with asr or maghrib with ish when travel makes it necessary do our muftis give a ruling to that effect or not consider the following passages al ba r al r iq states this is a question of a follower acting on the position of another imam and at a time of need it is permissible for a layman to do so he should regard them all as being upon the truth if acting on the position of his own imam causes him difficulty he may act on the ruling of another imam he should not put himself under such hardship for that leads to harm and to distress in religion this alone is the position of our teachers as our teachers' teacher sh h wal ull h may allah have mercy on him has written fat w rash diyyah p 286 further on in his recorded sayings he may allah have mercy on him says in the view of our imam ab an fah may allah have mercy on him combi

giving a talk before the friday sermon a talk is given before the friday prayer and its sermon does this have any basis or not also in some places time is set aside for the sunnah prayers before the sermon while in other places people pray their sunnahs during the talk which of these two practices is better there is no harm in giving a talk after the first adhan before the sermon and the prayer so long as the worshippers are willing a narration in al mustadrak of al kim records that ab hurayrah may allah be pleased with him used to give an admonition and relate hadiths before the preacher delivered the sermon consider the following in the same way all mah al zab d may allah h

an objection to the admonition given before the sermon and its answer what do the scholars say about this matter the trustees of a mosque object to the admonition and talk given before the friday prayer they say that in the time of the prophet there was only a single sermon in arabic so there is no need for an admonition and that this is a new practice in religion the mosque in question is the largest in the city and has a large number of worshippers the admonition and talk given in the local language before the arabic sermon is established by the practice of the companions so it is not correct to call it a new practice we do not regard it as a sunnah but as a matter of benefit consider what al mustadrak of al kim states

performing the friday prayer in a small town about 45 kilometres from venda there is a village where the muslim population is extremely small only a handful of people live there while the total non muslim population is around 10 000 in one house there five to seven men gather and perform the five daily prayers and the prayers are performed regularly at their proper times people also come out daily from venda to the surrounding area for trade and return in the evening and towards the end of the month when they are rather busier these men would like to perform the friday prayer in that same town there is however neither a mosque nor a prayer hall in the village is the friday prayer valid in this house and is it necessary f in the case described since the town's population is about 10 000 and the necessities of life are readily available performing the friday prayer there is valid and correct according to the hanafi school it is not necessary for forty people to be present for the friday prayer to be valid consider what a al bukh r states explaining this hadith all mah al ayn may allah have mercy on him says that people traded extensively at jaw th it was as it were a trading market and that where trade is brisk and mercha

the friday prayer in a small town and the settlements attached to it may the friday prayer be established in zakariyya park and the settlement adjoining it or not the friday prayer may be established in zakariyya park and the settlement adjoining it in fact it will be necessary to establish it because most of the necessities of life are met there and its population is between three and four thousand the jurists have given various definitions of a city and of a large settlement all mah al ayn may allah have mercy on him says in al bin yah his commentary on al hid yah

performing the friday prayer at an airport respected mufti ib does our johannesburg airport fall under the ruling of the outskirts of a city or not may the friday prayer be established there and is the friday prayer binding on those who work there in the case in question the airport adjoins the city of kempton park so praying the friday prayer there is permissible that is it lies within the outskirts of the city and once the friday prayer is valid and correct at the airport performing it becomes binding and necessary for those who work there consider what the author of al hid yah says

the friday prayer in a city or town where the muslim population is small according to the hanafi school if a large city or town has a mostly non muslim population and very few muslims is the friday prayer necessary or not in the case in question wherever the conditions for the friday prayer are met in a large city or town praying it is obligatory and necessary even if the muslim population is small because in the view of the hanafis it is not necessary for forty people to be present consider what al ba r al r iq states

establishing the friday prayer in a prison respected sir we draw your attention to a question may the friday prayer be prayed in a prison kindly favour us with an answer if the government does not forbid it but rather permits it the friday prayer may be prayed in a prison as for the ban on the general public entering a prison that is an administrative restriction it is not meant to keep people from the friday prayer just as the gate of a fort is closed because of an enemy or by long standing custom consider what al durr al mukht r states see also fat w ma m

praying the friday prayer in factories and workshops what is the ruling on praying the friday prayer in various factories that outsiders cannot enter schools and colleges are in the same situation so what is the ruling on praying the friday prayer in them in the case in question if the factory school college and the like are situated in a city where the conditions for the friday prayer are met or in the outskirts of such a city then establishing the friday prayer in all of them is valid and correct the fact that people from outside cannot come in is no obstacle consider what al durr al mukht r states it also states

praying the friday prayer in a park we prayed the friday prayer in a park about 40 kilometres from the town of grahamstown there is no mosque in this park though there is a prayer hall with room for about 80 people and ten or fifteen labourers live there was our friday prayer valid in this park or not ordinarily the friday prayer is not performed at that place according to the hanafi school it is a condition for the validity of the friday prayer that the place be a city or a town the friday prayer is not valid everywhere in the case described the park is neither a city nor a town and there is no large city in the surrounding area either so the friday prayer performed in this park was not valid consider what mu annaf ibn ab shaybah states sh m state

holding the friday prayer before the sun passes its zenith in some mosques in america the friday prayer is prayed before the sun passes its zenith does this accord with any school of law and may followers of another school pray behind them according to the hanafi school and according to all the other schools apart from the anbal s it is not correct to pray the friday prayer before the sun passes its zenith even among the anbal s it is better and preferable to pray it after that point if anbal s perform it before the sun passes its zenith followers of another school cannot pray behind them consider what al fiqh al isl m states

praying the friday prayer in a mosque where innovations take place a man sat for the friday prayer in a mosque in which innovations are practised will the friday prayer in that mosque be valid or not in the case described the friday prayer will be valid and this is not an acceptable excuse for leaving out the friday prayer it is better and preferable however to perform the friday prayer in another mosque where there are no innovations or corrupt practices consider what mar q al fal states al fat w al hindiyyah states

praying the friday prayer in the congregational mosque is better does a person receive greater reward for praying the friday prayer in the congregational mosque or in a small mosque or in a prayer hall praying the friday prayer in the congregational mosque is better and preferable nevertheless if the friday prayer is also held in the mosque of one's own neighbourhood praying it there is valid and correct consider what mull al al q r may allah have mercy on him wrote in his commentary on mishk t under one of the hadiths that is the prophet said that a man's prayer in his house counts as one prayer his prayer in the mosque of his own loca

eating drinking or opening a shop after the first adhan on friday is it permissible to eat and drink or to open a shop after the first adhan on friday or not what is the position of imam al a w may allah have mercy on him on this and has anyone given a fatwa to that effect most of the jurists hold that all kinds of business dealings must be given up after the first adhan imam al a w may allah have mercy on him the author of fat w at b and others however treated the second adhan the one that comes immediately before the sermon as the point at which dealings must be given up caution lies in the first view while at a time of need there is room to act upon the second consider what umdat al q r states

answering the second adhan on friday on friday should the second adhan which is given in front of the preacher be answered or not the authentic hadiths show that answering the adhan is a sunnah in general terms and the second adhan of friday is just as much an adhan so answering it will also be a sunnah there is no text to the contrary on the basis of which a prohibition could be established that listening to the sermon is necessary is agreed but at that moment the sermon has not even begun so how can listening to it be necessary the narration that the jurists usually quote goes back only to al may allah be pleased with him ibn abb s may allah be pleased with him and ibn umar may allah be pleased with him and not to the prophet all mah sh m may allah have

not getting time for the sunnah prayers after the friday adhan on friday only enough time is left between the adhan and the sermon for two units to be prayed and then the imam begins the sermon according to the hanafi school how is a person to complete the four units in the case described if the preacher does not allow enough time one should pray the four units briefly with a short recitation if the sermon begins in the middle of the sunnah prayer there is room to complete it it should not be broken off consider what shiyat al a w states

the preacher giving the greeting of peace when he ascends the pulpit how is it for the preacher to give the greeting of peace as he ascends the pulpit the statements of the jurists generally indicate that the preacher should not give the greeting before the sermon it is mentioned in the hadiths however so it is not proper to deny that it is legitimate in itself yes if there is any fear of discord it is better to leave it otherwise it is correct for the preacher to give the greeting consider what i l al sunan states

adopting a position when reasoned analysis is supported by a narration have the hanafi jurists laid down the principle that when a ruling agrees with the hadith that ruling should be the one adopted for fatwa for example the question mentioned above about the preacher giving the greeting of peace from the pulpit the writings of the jurists throw light on this question where a point of fiqh agrees with the hadith one should not turn away from it that is that narration should be the one adopted for fatwa consider what sh m states

the muezzin's recitation in front of the preacher before handing the staff to the preacher the muezzin recites blessings on the prophet in a loud voice and urges those present to do the same what is the ruling on this in the case described it is not correct for the muezzin to do this this practice did not exist in the time of the companions may allah be pleased with them nor in the time of the successors nor is any such thing reported from the early generations it is therefore not something the sharia approves of rather it is better to leave it consider what al fiqh al al madh hib al arba ah states

the preacher turning to right and left during the sermon while delivering the sermon should the preacher keep facing straight ahead or may he turn to the right and left it is sunnah for the preacher to keep facing forward during the sermon turning to the right and left is disliked consider what shiyat al a w states sh m states

raising the hands when the preacher supplicates when the preachers make supplication during the friday and eid sermons is it permissible for those listening to raise their hands and say amen or not in the case described it is permissible and correct to say amen inwardly without raising the hands raising the hands and saying amen aloud however is strictly disliked consider what sh m states umdat al fiqh states when the preacher supplicates in the sermon for the muslims it is not permissible for those listening to raise their hands or

limiting the sermon to recitation of the qur'an on fridays some people recite the noble qur'an in both sermons for example part of s rat al ujur t in the first sermon and part of it in the second what is the ruling on this in the sharia and what should be recited in the two sermons reciting the noble qur'an in the sermon is a sunnah and was the practice of the prophet but one should not confine oneself to that there should also be the two testimonies of faith and supplication for the muslims blessings upon the prophet and mention of the rightly guided caliphs may allah be pleased with them with the prayer that allah be pleased with them and so on all of these are recommended moreover people generally think ill of mu wiyah may allah be pleased with him so he should be mentioned as well consider what a muslim states

holding a staff during the sermon what does the sharia say about the staff for the sermon on friday is it necessary or obligatory or sunnah will a person who does not hold a staff become an unbeliever the jurists have written that if a city was conquered by the sword the imam should hold a sword in his left hand and deliver the sermon leaning on it all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him has explained the wisdom behind this consider the following that is he shows the people that this city was conquered by the sword and if you turn away from islam the sword is still in the hands of the muslims and they will fight you and bring you back to islam if a city or country was not conquered by the sword however but came to islam through in

a preacher omitting the brief sitting between the two sermons if a preacher does not sit briefly between the two friday sermons what is the ruling according to the anaf school the brief sitting between the two sermons is a sunnah so the sermon itself is still valid but leaving the sitting out is contrary to the sunnah and is disliked consider what mar q al fal states fat w ma m diyyah states not sitting between the two sermons is contrary t

prompting the preacher when he misreads a verse in the sermon if a person recites a qur'anic verse incorrectly during the sermon is it right to prompt him or not in the case in question if he makes a gross mistake in the verse correct him by passing him a written note so that the gross mistake is removed this is so even though every kind of speech is forbidden during the sermon just as every kind of speech is forbidden in prayer and yet there is room for prompting there moreover according to one view it is only worldly speech that is forbidden religious speech is not prohibited consider what shiyat al a w states

delivering the sermon in a language other than arabic is it necessary to deliver the sermon in arabic or is it a sunnah and if someone delivers the sermon in a language other than arabic what is the ruling delivering the sermon in arabic is an emphasised sunnah and is required delivering it in any other language is strictly disliked throughout their lives the practice of ras lull h and the companions may allah be pleased with them was to deliver the sermon in arabic they spread through the east and the west conquered non arab lands and delivered sermons there yet there is not a single instance of their delivering the friday or eid sermon in a language other than arabic some people raise the objection that the sermon is a reminder and an admonition so it ought to be in the language of the listeners but they should consider that the sermon is an act of remembrance allah says in th

evidence for starting to pour earth from the head end of the grave is there evidence in the hadith for starting to pour the earth from the head end when burying a body in the grave the practice of starting to pour the earth from the head end after the deceased has been placed in the grave is established in the hadiths consider what sunan ibn m jah states see also

moving a body to another place because of flooding if a grave comes into the path of a flood and there is a danger of the body being washed away may the body be moved to another place or not there is a difference of opinion about moving a body when water overwhelms the grave what appears closest to sound reasoning is that if by strong likelihood the body of the person in the grave is still whole and intact then there is no harm in moving it as a rat j bir may allah be pleased with him moved his father's body at u ud since the earth does not consume the bodies of the martyrs if that is not the case the body should not be moved consider what al a w states
