counting zakat paid in excess of what was due towards the following year a man paid a year's zakat on an estimate when he later worked out the figures he found that he had paid more than was due may he count the extra amount towards the following year's zakat or not in the case described he may count the extra amount towards the following year's zakat al fat w al walw lijiyyah states kit b al fat w states question a man paid ten thousand rupees as zakat but when he worked out the figures only eight thousand rupees of zakat were due from him may he count that extra amount towards his zakat in future answer yes once a person owns the nisab the zakat of more

zakat money for a madrasah stolen from the collector someone gave zakat money to a madrasah's collector and the money was then lost or stolen from him two things need to be established 1 has the zakat been discharged or not 2 is the collector liable for the loss or not 1 our senior scholars may allah have mercy on them are agreed that the collector is the agent of the needy students of the madrasah and an agent's possession is the same as the possession of the one who appointed him on this basis the zakat has been discharged 2 the collector is an agent and a trustee so if he made proper arrangements to safeguard the money and it was still lost or stolen he does not have to make it good but if he was negligent he must make it good consider what al mas il states if zakat money is stolen from madrasah collectors or is stolen or lost from the principal and there was no shortcoming on their part in safeguarding it they are not liable

zakat collected for a clinic that is then lost there is a clinic which has a zakat fund medicines are bought from it and distributed among poor patients if zakat is taken for this purpose and is then lost while in the agent's hands has the zakat been discharged or not as a rule those who benefit from a hospital are the people of the surrounding area just as in the case of a madrasah it is the students of that madrasah who are meant so here it is the poor patients of the hospital who are meant the zakat is therefore discharged and does not have to be paid again this case is exactly like the case of the madrasah collector and the evidence for it has already been given

deducting the dower when paying zakat if a man owes his wife her dower and the amount is one hundred thousand rand is that hundred thousand deducted when he pays his zakat or not or must he pay zakat on the whole sum if the husband has no intention of paying the dower or if the wife by custom does not ask for it zakat must be paid on the whole sum but if he does intend to pay it he pays zakat on what is left after deducting the amount of the dower consider what al fat w al hindiyyah states even though the dower is deferred if the man is concerned to pay it now zakat is not due on that amount otherwise it is due imd d al muft n vol 2 p 451 fat w ma m diyyah 9 319 chap

deducting expenses from zakat money suppose a man sends money from his zakat to build a house for someone or sends books that a person needs or sends someone to deliver the zakat money to the poor can the cost of transport be deducted from the zakat or not in the case described one should first try to meet such expenses from funds other than zakat but if no other arrangement can be made there should be room to meet them from the zakat money kif yat al muft states there is room to pay those who collect and bring in zakat money a wage for their work out of that money even if they are well off kif yat al muft 4 286 mawl n kh lid sayfull h says just as the officials appointed over zakat and ushr keep themselves busy protecting the rights of the poor so further staff may be needed for the accounting and the distribution of zakat and ushr the juris

deducting government tax when paying zakat if tax imposed by the government has not been paid by the time zakat falls due is it deducted or is zakat due on the whole sum in other words does tax prevent zakat from becoming obligatory or not if the government imposes a tax and its amount has been fixed for example you are told we have levied a tax of 50 000 on your shop this year which you will have to pay then this is a debt and zakat is paid on what remains once it has been deducted if however the shopkeeper or the company owner makes an effort and gets the tax reduced to 30 000 so that 20 000 is left over he should then pay zakat on that 20 000 because it is no longer part of the debt consider what shiyat al a w states

zakat money stolen from the agent entrusted with it a man gave zakat money to another person to distribute and the money was stolen from this agent has the zakat been discharged or not and is the agent liable to make good the loss if the recipients were not specified and the agent was to spend the zakat money at his own discretion then the zakat has not been discharged and must be paid again an agent is a trustee so if he was not negligent in safeguarding the money he is not liable for the loss and bears no responsibility for it if the recipients were specified for instance if the agent was the collector or the principal of an institution the ruling on that has already been given consider what al durr al mukht r states

an agent spending the zakat money on himself a man gave someone zakat money to spend on the poor since this person was himself entitled to zakat he spent the money on himself has the zakat been discharged or not if the owner used the wording of giving it out then it must be given to someone else but if he said use it as you wish the agent may use it himself provided he is entitled to zakat consider what the marginal commentary on taby n al aq iq states al durr al mukht r states

an agent paying the zakat with different money a man gave me one thousand rand and appointed me his agent to deliver his zakat to a certain person in india i sent this sum through a transfer along with other funds and my representative there paid the zakat out of the other money has the zakat been discharged or not as long as the zakat money is still with the agent and he pays the zakat from other funds it is discharged but if he has already spent the original zakat money and then pays from other funds the zakat is not discharged in the case described the original money was still there so the zakat has been discharged besides rand are not current in india so delivering the zakat there means delivering it after converting it and since converting it is permitted the zakat has been discharged consider what al durr al mukht r states

whether zakat is discharged by the methods of transferring ownership used in some madrasahs some careful madrasahs run the following system for transferring ownership of zakat they give a needy student 400 rand of zakat money another administrator then takes 300 rand from him for his lodging electricity tuition and food and 100 rand remains with the student on the face of it this system is very attractive and appealing but some scholars raise the following objections to it 1 if a student is absent the cost of the days of his absence should not be taken from him yet there is no accepted procedure for returning any part of the money deducted 2 if the student dies before the stipends are handed out the money is held in trust and so should be returned to his heirs giving zakat money to needy students is in reality a transfer of ownership then when the student pays the fee of 300 rand that falls under a conditional donation in return for the donation the student is provided with food lodging and the like as a stipulated condition a conditional donation is a gift made for a return so if the student is absent for a few days his money does not have to be returned and if a student has paid the fee for a whole year and leaves in the middle of the year the fee for the remainder of the year does not have to be returned either because in a gift made for a return the donor cannot ask for the gift back and here the money has already been spent or m

spending zakat money on extending a house a poor relative of mine has a house but it is very small smaller than he needs and he is also entitled to zakat may zakat money be given to him to enlarge his house in the case described it is permissible to give zakat money for the repair or extension of a house to someone entitled to zakat that is someone who does not own wealth equal to the nisab over and above his basic needs consider what al durr al mukht r states

a salaried person in need accepting zakat a man is in employment his wife had an accident and the cost of medicine hospital fees and other expenses has become heavy he cannot meet all these expenses out of his monthly salary is there room for such a man to accept zakat or not in the case described there is room for this man to accept zakat consider what al durr al mukht r states fat al qad r states al fat w al hindiyyah states

giving zakat to a poor brother or sister if a man's brothers and sisters are poor and entitled to zakat may a well off brother give them zakat or not giving zakat to a brother or sister who is entitled to it is permissible indeed it is better because it also amounts to keeping family ties al fat w al hindiyyah states al fat w al t t rkh niyyah states

giving zakat to the imams of mosques in our area people appoint an imam for their mosques and do not fix a salary for him instead once the crop is harvested they give him grain and other produce out of their zakat if the imam is entitled to zakat is the zakat discharged or not is this not a wage may zakat be given as a wage in the case described there are two ways in which zakat may be given 1 if the mosque's imam is entitled to zakat giving it to him as a poor man is valid indeed it is better 2 the zakat may be given to the imam as payment for leading the prayers in this case the zakat is not discharged although the imam may lawfully take it as a salary leaving aside the two situations above the better and preferable course is to fix a wage for the imam and then since it is plain that he cannot manage on it to give him charity and zakat as well consider what al durr al mukht r states al

giving zakat to a salaried man who is in debt a man owes 70 000 rand and the debt is payable now but he does not have the money to pay it he also owns nothing beyond his basic needs though he does receive a monthly salary may zakat money be given to him or not in the case described it is permissible and correct to give zakat money to the debtor so that he can pay off his debt consider what sunan ab d w d states badhl al majh d states al ba r al r iq states sh m states

building a house with zakat money and making a poor man its owner if someone buys a house with zakat money and makes a poor man the owner of that house has the zakat been discharged or not in the case described if the house has been put in the poor man's name and he has been given its papers and made its owner the zakat is discharged it is necessary however that once the house has been built its value be fixed according to the market it should not happen that two hundred thousand was spent on the house its market value is two hundred and fifty thousand and the person paying zakat prices it at three hundred thousand rather he should price it at the ordinary market rate there is admittedly a drawback here in that a single poor person has been given more than the amount of the nisab but in view of the poor man's need the provision of housing for his family and the

paying a poor man's debt from zakat through an agent suppose a man is entitled to zakat because of his heavy debts but if zakat is given to him he will squander it may this man appoint an agent to pay his debt on his behalf in the case described if the poor man appoints an agent and the agent takes the zakat money and pays off the debt on his behalf this is permissible and the zakat is discharged and if he has not appointed anyone as his agent but has merely given permission the zakat is still discharged it is as though the creditor took possession on the poor man's behalf and then put the money in his own pocket consider what bad i al an i states

giving zakat to a well off student of religious knowledge i have read in some books that a scholar or a student of religious knowledge may be given zakat even if he is well off because he is occupied in serving the religious sciences and that if he does not keep receiving zakat his life will be brought to a standstill is this ruling correct or not all mah al a w may allah have mercy on him and all mah al sh m may allah have mercy on him state that according to the chosen view it is not permissible to give zakat to a well off scholar or student because poverty is a condition for zakat and what is mentioned in certain books is not reliable al durr al mukht r states

giving zakat to the infant daughter of a wealthy man a wealthy man who owns the nis b the threshold of wealth at which zakat becomes due has a small daughter two months old who is in hospital because of a hole in her heart this man is not in a position to bear the cost can zakat be given to her for the hospital bills and so on or not in the case in question it is not correct to give zakat money to the daughter of a wealthy man who owns the nis b it may however be given to her mother who in all likelihood does not own the nis b herself if she does own some jewellery she should gift it to her husband and then take the zakat and spend it on her daughter or she may first spend the money she has on the daughter and then take zakat bad i al an i states

giving zakat to an orphan whose mother is wealthy an orphan boy lives with his mother and his mother is wealthy is it permissible to give zakat to this orphan or not if the orphan is old enough to understand and is able to take possession and is also entitled to zakat then it is permissible and correct to give him zakat even though his mother is wealthy if the child is very small and does not understand taking possession and is not capable of dealings then his guardian should take possession on his behalf this is permissible and the zakat will be discharged al durr al mukht r states al a w

paying teachers' salaries out of zakat money is it permissible to pay the salaries of the teachers of islamic madrasahs out of zakat money or not in the case in question it is not permissible to pay salaries out of zakat money yes if the zakat money is given to students who are entitled to it and tuition fees are then collected from them that money may be spent on salaries for with zakat money it is necessary to make a poor person the owner of it without any return consider what kanz al daq iq states fat w ma m diyyah states for obligatory charities to be discharged they must be spent on the proper recipients the poor and so on by way of transfer of ownership without an

the sharia ruling on funds received by arabic madrasahs arabic madrasahs receive obligatory charities as well as non obligatory ones that is donations and the like what is the ruling on this money does it leave the ownership of its owner or not and once a year has passed will zakat be due on it or not further when is the zakat of the owners discharged after the money has been spent or once the administrators have taken possession of it three kinds of funds generally come into madrasahs 1 donations gifts voluntary charities and the like that is funds in which transfer of ownership is not obligatory 2 zakat vows expiations and the like that is funds in which transfer of ownership is obligatory 3 funds which the donor earmarks for a particular purpose a particular room for example or a particular floor covering the ruling on each of them is as follows 1 in donations too that is in funds in which transfer of ownership is not obligatory the principals of madrasahs and their deputies are agents and representatives but whatever rule of expenditure has been laid down and settled within the bounds

spending zakat money contrary to what the donors specified someone gave zakat money for people affected by an earthquake and for various reasons the money could not be spent there is it now permissible to use this zakat money somewhere else or not in the case in question it is not permissible to spend the zakat money in another place the permission of the owners is necessary yes if the money is the zakat of a number of different people and it is difficult to inform them all and it is also impossible to spend it on the purpose specified then it will be permissible to spend it elsewhere on a valid recipient of zakat consider what al fiqh al anaf wa adillatuh states al sh m states fat w ma m diyyah states

giving zakat to someone who owns a television a man is poor in the technical sense but he owns a television t v and lives at the ordinary standard of life he also has a good many items lying about that are surplus to his needs is such a person entitled to zakat or not in the case in question if the television t v he owns is an old one which is worth very little then owning it does not make a man wealthy or an owner of the nis b the threshold of wealth at which zakat becomes due yes if along with the television t v he has other things too that are surplus to his needs and they come to the value of the nis b then he is an owner of the nis b but the other members of his household will still be entitled to zakat so let him give it to them consider what al fat w al hindiyyah states

giving zakat to someone who is insane or unconscious if a person is insane or unconscious and is also poor how is zakat to be given to him seeing that he does not understand what it is to take possession in the case in question the zakat should be given to his guardian or executor and if there is no guardian or executor it should be given to the person who looks after him al sh m states bad i al an i states

giving zakat money for medical treatment muslims from other countries live here and work as labourers very often a large sum is needed for medical treatment and the like and they do not have that much money with them is it permissible to give them zakat for treatment and so on or not in the case in question it is permissible to give zakat money for medical treatment and the like to a salaried patient who is in straitened circumstances al fat w al t t rkh niyyah states al ba r al r iq states al durr al mukht r states

an agent spending zakat money contrary to his principal's instruction a man gave someone zakat money in south africa and told him to take it to india and give it there to those entitled to it may this man give part of that money or all of it to the poor here or not in the case in question if he did not rule out any other place but simply said that it was to be spent in india then it may be spent on the poor of south africa but if he did rule out any other place if for example he said spend it only in india do not spend it here then it is not permissible to spend it on the poor of south africa consider what al ashb h wa al na ir states

a woman taking zakat money when she has not been given her inheritance a woman's father owned a good deal of property after his death she became his heir and was entitled to a share but her brothers did not give her that share and the woman does not own wealth to the value of the nis b the threshold of wealth at which zakat becomes due either may she take zakat money or not in the case in question the woman is entitled to zakat and so she may take zakat money al durr al mukht r states fat w al walw lijiyyah states

the difference between the recipients of zakat and the recipients of interest money is there a difference between the proper recipients of zakat and the proper recipients of interest money or not if there is please inform us the recipients of zakat and the recipients of interest money are the needy and the destitute the difference however is that zakat money cannot be given to a poor non muslim whereas interest money may be given to a poor non muslim consider what allah says in the noble qur'an al durr al mukht r states

taking zakat when one's mother is a h shim but one's father is not if a person's mother is a h shim but his father is not may such a person take zakat or not is there a difference between the shafi is and the hanafis on this in the case in question it is permissible for the person mentioned to take zakat since lineage is reckoned through the father consider what al sh m states i nat al lib n states

paying adaqat al fi r before eid may adaqat al fi r be paid during ramadan before eid al fitr or not and is that contrary to what is recommended or not in the case in question adaqat al fi r will be discharged by paying it during the blessed month of ramadan but what is recommended is that one pay it on the day of eid al fitr before setting out for the place of the eid prayer paying it during ramadan is also correct and indeed in the light of one narration it may be paid even before ramadan consider what al hid yah states al sh m states

giving items not specified in the texts as adaqat al fi r may we have clothes made up and give them to poor children as adaqat al fi r or not and what is the ruling on giving other items that are not specified in the texts it is permissible and correct to work out the value of the items specified in the texts and then with that amount to buy items which are not so specified and give them it is likewise correct to have clothes made up and give them to poor children the adaqat al fi r will be discharged consider what al durr al mukht r states al ba r al r iq states bad i al an i states

how a foreign resident should work out the value of adaqat al fi r if a man from pakistan or india is living in south africa is it correct for him to work out the value according to his own country and pay his adaqat al fi r on that basis or not it is not correct for a foreigner who is staying in south africa to pay adaqat al fi r according to the rates of his own country rather he should work out the value according to south africa itself and pay his adaqat al fi r accordingly consider what al sh m states al ba r al r iq states

how a foreign resident should work out the adaqat al fi r of his children a man living in south africa has his wife and children in pakistan should he pay according to the rates of pakistan or according to the value in south africa the man in question is obliged to pay the adaqat al fi r of his children according to the value in south africa paying it according to the value in pakistan is not correct consider what al ba r al r iq states al in yah shar al hid yah states al sh m states

using adaqat al fi r money to cook food and serve it if the money collected for adaqat al fi r is used to have food cooked and the prisoners in a jail are then seated together and served this food on the day of eid is adaqat al fi r thereby discharged or not in adaqat al fi r the charity of eid al fitr just as in zakat transfer of ownership is necessary when people are seated together and fed no transfer of ownership takes place it is merely permission to use the food since they do not have the right to dispose of it as they please adaqat al fi r is therefore not discharged in this way if however the food is placed in each person's own vessel and handed over as his property then adaqat al fi r is discharged it should also be borne in mind that some prisoners in a jail own the nisab giving to them will not discharge it either consider what al ba r al r iq states

sighting the crescent moon from an aeroplane if a person flies in an aeroplane and sees the crescent moon but nobody on the ground is able to see it will a sighting made only from the aeroplane be taken into account or not if a person flew in an aeroplane and saw the crescent moon while nobody on the ground could see it then a sighting made only from the aeroplane does not count in the sharia if however the aeroplane is not at a great height and someone sitting in it sees the moon his sighting will be accepted because the jurists have stated plainly that if a person sees the moon outside the city or from some elevated place his sighting is accepted consider what al fat w al hindiyyah states

making a student fast as a punishment if a teacher makes a student keep a fast as a punishment is that correct or not and will the student get the reward of that fast or not it is correct for madrasahs to make students fast as a punishment there is no harm in it and the reward of the fast will also be given this is like what the prophet said about children once a child turns seven tell him to pray and after ten smack him for leaving prayer so that he becomes used to praying although children are not yet addressed by the rulings of the sharia they are still given the reward of prayer see the hadith likewise praying in front of people

keeping a fast of only a few hours is it permissible in the religion of mu ammad to keep a fast of four or five hours the reason for asking is that in our area some people give up food and drink from the morning on the day of eid al a and stay like people who are fasting saying we are fasting then they break it after the eid prayer and some of them eat from their own sacrifice is doing this permissible or not can they drink tea and the like in the morning or not in the religion of mu ammad a fast runs from true dawn until sunset there is no such thing as a fast of a few hours however on eid al a it is recommended for those who intend to offer a sacrifice to eat nothing in the morning and to begin after the eid prayer with meat from their own sacrifice this is established from hadith it should be called ims k holding back from food not a fast it is not necessary either only recommended so if someone wishes to drink tea or the like in the morning that is not forbidden it is permissible without any dislike for those who cannot afford a sacrifice or who have their sacrifice carried out somewhere else holding back is also better

when the family objects to a man going for an obligatory hajj a man wants to go for hajj but his wife and children are afraid to stay in the house and tell him not to go what should he do and does it make any difference whether the hajj is obligatory or voluntary a person on whom hajj has become obligatory must perform it that same year delaying it is not correct his wife and children's refusal is not a valid ground and he should not take it into account so long as the conditions for hajj are met there is nothing preventing him and the man himself does not think there is any real danger to his wife and children if however the hajj is voluntary then the wider benefit will be considered he should first make arrangements to set his family's minds at rest and then perform it he should weigh what is best and decide himself see bad i al an i

a woman travelling for hajj with her son in law may a woman travel for hajj with her son in law or not in the case described the woman may travel for hajj with her son in law but if there is a fear of temptation she should not go and in any case being alone together and the like must be avoided fat w ra miyyah states a son in law is a ma ram for his mother in law marriage between the two is forbidden for ever al fat w al lamg riyyah states lamg r

travelling for hajj with one's sister's grandson may a woman go for hajj with her sister's grandson or not in the case described since marriage between them is forbidden for ever it is correct for her to travel for hajj with him for this woman is the maternal aunt of his father and a father's maternal aunt has the same status as one's own maternal aunt see al fat w al lamg riyyah

ramal praying near maq m ibr h m and reciting the talbiyah aloud for women is it recorded anywhere in islamic history that women may not perform ramal walking briskly in aw f that they may not run between the two green markers that they may not pray near maq m ibr h m and that they may not recite the talbiyah loudly has any prohibition of this been reported from the prophet and did the prophet's blessed wives perform these acts or not there are certain things that women are forbidden to do for instance they should not recite the talbiyah loudly they should not perform i ib uncovering the right shoulder during aw f they should not perform ramal during aw f they should not run between the two green markers they should not climb up on af they should not kiss the black stone when there is a crowd and likewise they should not pray near maq m ibr h m when there is a crowd the prohibition of these acts is established in the light of the narrations furthermore the act of a rat h jar was retained for men and not for women because her running was something she did at one particular moment and out of necessity

letting a cloth hang over the face in the state of i r m the hanafi position on women in the state of i r m is that a woman keeps her face uncovered and lets a cloth hang down over it what one usually sees however is that women find this difficult because of that some women who normally observe the veil give it up altogether during these days and in that there is a fear of temptation other women who observe the veil insist on covering and hang a cloth over the face which then makes it hard for them to see where they are going and to perform aw f so the point to consider is this do these two reasons 1 hardship and 2 the fear of temptation leave any room for using an ordinary face veil or if there is some other way of removing t in the case in question women are not permitted to use an ordinary face veil if one is worn for a whole day a dam a sacrificial penalty becomes obligatory this is because a woman's i r m lies in her face that is the basic rule is that the face must be left uncovered and that no cloth should touch it since there is a fear of temptation however permission has been given to let a cloth hang down over the face provided it does not touch it this is established from the mother of the believers a rat ishah may allah be pleased with her for she used to give this very instruction if there is hardship in it let it be borne cheerfully for a few days for the journey of hajj is in

the hajj of a woman who was struck by insanity during the standing at muzdalifah a woman suffered an attack of insanity during the standing at muzdalifah and the condition has continued until now so she has been left without performing the aw f al ziy rah what can now be done for her to come out of i r m and what expiation is due for the delay in the case in question if someone has performed the aw f al ziy rah on her behalf her hajj is discharged then once she recovers she will be obliged to perform the aw f al ziy rah herself and nothing by way of expiation will be due from her for the delay because this is a state of excuse and that is pardoned lub b al man sik states ghunyat al n sik states

the hajj of one who dies before the aw f al ziy rah if a person dies after the standing at arafah but before the aw f al ziy rah what is the ruling on his hajj if he went for hajj in the very year in which it became obligatory upon him then no bequest for the aw f al ziy rah is required of him and his hajj is complete because by performing the hajj in that first year he did as much as he was able to do but if he delayed it after it became obligatory then because of that shortcoming a bequest for a dam a sacrificial penalty is required of him al sunan al kubr states shar al lub b states

shortening the prayer at araf t muzdalifah and min is the ruling that one shortens the prayer at araf t muzdalifah and min on account of the hajj or on account of travel will the people of mecca also shorten their prayers the shortening of the prayer at araf t muzdalifah and min is on account of travel not on account of the hajj indeed there is no connection whatever between the hajj and shortening the prayer for the hajj is by its very nature a matter of hardship with which shortening does not sit well the shortening then is because of travel a hadith states ma rif al sunan states

bleeding before and after the aw f al ziy rah and the validity of the aw f a woman performed the aw f al ziy rah on the third day of eid then performed the farewell aw f and then returned to her home country india before the aw f she had bled for four days and had then become pure and after that she performed the aw f when she reached home eight days after becoming pure the bleeding began again and continued for five days her former habit was seven days is her aw f valid or not and what should she do now it will be easier to follow the position of imam mu ammad may allah have mercy on him where the bleeding and the purity within ten days are equal the bleeding is counted as menstruation and the purity is treated as a dividing line that is in the case in question according to imam mu ammad may allah have mercy on him the first four days of bleeding count as menstruation and the days after that count as days of purity the aw f was therefore valid and sound the bleeding that came afterwards is isti ah irregular bleeding since the woman has already returned to her own country giving the ruling on this view is the easier course and removes hardship and difficulty so it is app

performing the aw f during four days of purity and then bleeding again a woman menstruated for three days and then remained pure for four days and during that time of purity she performed the aw f al ziy rah after that she bled for one day is her aw f al ziy rah valid or will she have to repeat it the crowds and the strain there are so great that they are often themselves the cause of menstruation in the case in question a period of purity falling within the days of menstruation is treated like continuous bleeding the aw f will therefore be counted as having been performed during menstruation so if the woman is still in mecca she should perform the aw f again otherwise a dam becomes obligatory al hid yah volume one states sh m states umdat al ri yah states

performing the aw f al ziy rah while menstruating if a woman's aw f al ziy rah has been delayed because of menstruation but she is unable to stay on in any way can she come out of i r m without performing the aw f al ziy rah or not and what is she to do about the obligatory aw f in the case in question she should do her best to stay on somehow and perform the aw f al ziy rah in a state of purity but if in spite of her efforts she cannot stay and performs the aw f al ziy rah while menstruating the aw f is discharged and a badanah the sacrifice of a large animal becomes obligatory upon her and that sacrifice must be offered within the sacred precinct bad i al an i states al ba r al r iq states

menstruation beginning during the farewell aw f a woman was performing the farewell aw f when her menstruation began part way through what is the ruling on her aw f does she have to make it up or not the farewell aw f is not obligatory upon a menstruating woman and if her menstruation began part way through and she left the aw f making it up is not obligatory either a al bukh r states taby n al aq iq states

shortening the hair when a woman has lost her hair through cancer a woman has lost the hair of her head because of cancer how is she to shorten her hair in hajj and umrah and how will she come out of i r m in the case in question the woman should pass the scissors over her head whatever hair comes into them and is cut off is enough if there is no hair at all and nothing is cut that too is in order and she will come out of i r m it is like the case of a bald man who has no hair at all on his head about him the jurists have said that he should pass a razor over his head even though no hair comes away a woman however may not shave her head al durr al mukht r states shi

two days of bleeding after the aw f al ziy rah a woman bled for three days then remained pure for five days and during that time she performed the aw f al ziy rah after that she bled for two days according to the position of imam mu ammad may allah have mercy on him did this aw f take place during menstruation or during purity in the case in question since the five days of purity fell within the days of menstruation they are treated like continuous bleeding the aw f al ziy rah will therefore be counted as having taken place during menstruation even on the position of imam mu ammad al hid yah volume one states sh m states umdat al ri yah states

performing the aw f al ziy rah during six days of purity followed by three days of bleeding a woman bled for three days then remained pure for six days and during that time she performed the aw f al ziy rah after that she bled for three days in the view of imam mu ammad may allah have mercy on him did this aw f al ziy rah take place during menstruation or during purity it will be easier to follow the position of imam mu ammad may allah have mercy on him where the bleeding and the purity within ten days are equal the bleeding is counted as menstruation and the purity is treated as a dividing line that is in the case in question according to imam mu ammad may allah have mercy on him the first three days count as days of menstruation and the six days after that count as days of purity so the aw f was valid and sound the bleeding that came after that is isti ah irregular bleeding on the face of it imam mu ammad's may allah have mercy on him position is the easier one for women and when there is need a ruling may be given on the basis of i

the farewell aw f for people living within the ill a man is employed in jeddah and has been living there for twenty or twenty five years not as a permanent resident but simply doing his job there after finishing the hajj he is going back to jeddah is the farewell aw f necessary upon him or recommended in the case in question the man has not made jeddah his permanent home he is only staying there the farewell aw f will therefore be necessary upon him when he goes back but if he has made jeddah his permanent home and has no intention of moving away from it then the farewell aw f is recommended because it is not necessary but only recommended for the people of mecca and the people of the ill that is those who live inside the m q t ghunyat al n sik states

passing the m q t without i r m if a person from south africa travels straight to mecca whether with the intention of hajj or of umrah or for some other reason but with mecca itself as his destination may he put on i r m in jeddah or not and if he puts on i r m in jeddah will a dam be obligatory or not in the case in question if he wishes to go straight to mecca he must put on i r m before the m q t to pass it without i r m is a sin putting on i r m in jeddah is not correct if he does so a dam becomes obligatory upon him and he is sinful shar al lub b states

i r m when one is heading for madinah at the time of passing the m q t a man wished to go for hajj the agent told him that they were to go to madinah first so he did not put on i r m and set off for madinah after reaching jeddah the agent told him that they were going to mecca first what should the man do now where should he put on i r m and will a dam be obligatory or not in the case in question at the time of passing the m q t his destination was not the sacred precinct but madinah so putting on i r m was not required of him and no dam is due but now that his plan has changed in jeddah and he is to go to mecca he should put on i r m in jeddah itself and then no penalty will be due shar lub b al man sik states jad d fiqh ma

passing the m q t without i r m when intending to stop in jeddah for a few hours if a person decides that he will stop for a few hours in jeddah and only then enter the sacred precinct may he pass the m q t without i r m or not that is will it be valid for him to put on i r m in jeddah or will a dam be due from him in the case in question since the aircraft passes over the m q t or level with it i r m must be put on before coming level with the m q t if someone forms the intention of staying a day or a few hours in jeddah and so puts off his i r m until jeddah that is not correct it is merely a legal device a device may be resorted to at a time of need in order to avoid something forbidden or disliked but a device by which a ruling of the sharia is nullified is not correct it is like the device of the people of the sabbath against which a severe warning is recorded in the noble qur'an a rat mawl n muft shaf may allah have mercy on him has written in it must be rem

entering i r m at jeddah airport can people who are not residents of jeddah enter i r m at jeddah airport or not in the case asked about it is not correct to enter i r m at jeddah airport rather it is necessary to enter i r m before passing the m q t that is before the aircraft passes the point level with yalamlam if this is not done a dam a compensatory sacrifice becomes due see shar al lub b which states

passing the m q t without i r m when travelling to jeddah my son lives in jeddah when i travel for umrah may i enter i r m in jeddah in the case asked about if your intention is only to visit your son and the intention of performing umrah is secondary to that then it is correct to enter i r m for umrah in jeddah after meeting and visiting your son and no penalty will be due but if your aim from the outset is umrah and only afterwards you thought that you would also meet your son then it is necessary to enter i r m at the m q t otherwise a dam becomes obligatory in other words what counts is the original intention and allah knows the state of the heart perfectly well it is therefore very important on this blessed journey to avoid legal devices where there is no genuine need shar lub b al man sik states

drivers agents and the like passing the m q t without i r m is it permissible for agents drivers and others like them to travel to makkah without i r m or not they say that it causes them hardship in the case asked about if the agents and drivers travel back and forth every day then entering i r m should not be necessary for them but those who do not travel repeatedly agents for instance do not usually travel every day will have to enter i r m see what is stated in na e mas il awr ulam ke fay le under present conditions when traders office workers taxi drivers and other working people have to enter the aram sometimes every day and sometimes every second or third day and some of them more than once in a single day it is extremely burdensome and difficult for such people to be bound to enter i r m and perform umrah on every occasion there will therefore be scop

i r m for those who come to jeddah by sea if a person travels from india or pakistan to jeddah by ship and yalamlam is left far off to one side so that the ship does not actually pass parallel to it may such a person enter i r m at jeddah on this question there is some difference of opinion among our senior scholars may allah have mercy on them the considered position of a rat mufti muhammad shaf may allah have mercy on him is that i r m may be delayed until jeddah whereas a rat mawl n y suf binnor may allah have mercy on him used to say that it is not permissible to delay i r m until jeddah even so a rat mufti muhammad shaf may allah have mercy on him also wrote that the more cautious course is to enter i r m before reaching the point parallel to yalamlam see what is stated in jaw hir al fiqh in circumstances such as these where the scholars differ over the question caution lies in entering i r m o

intending qir n after having intended ifr d if someone makes the intention of ajj ifr d and then before beginning the rites of ajj decides on qir n is this valid or not in the case asked about it is valid to make the intention of qir n before beginning the rites of ajj and the sacrifice dam of qir n will become obligatory doing so however is blameworthy see what is stated in al durr al mukht r see also

performing ajj ifr d even though one can afford the sacrifice a wealthy man went for ajj ifr d along with his wife his two daughters and his sister on his return the statement of a certain scholar was quoted to him namely that ajj ifr d is only for the poor when he asked that scholar himself the scholar said that in the earliest period of islam those who performed ifr d were the people who could not afford the sacrifice this man now wishes to know whether ajj ifr d is only for the poor in the case asked about what this scholar said is not correct rather those who are able to offer the sacrifice may also perform ajj ifr d there is no doubt that in the view of the anaf s qir n is the most meritorious of the three but ifr d too is legislated for everyone see what is stated in shar al lub b bad i al an i states

a q rin combining the aw f of umrah with the aw f of arrival if a q rin makes the intention of the aw f of arrival aw f al qud m within his aw f of umrah is this disliked or is it permissible without any dislike in the case asked about it is permissible and correct without any dislike to make the intention of the aw f of arrival within the aw f of umrah see what is stated in the noble hadith tafs r ma har states fat al qad r states

performing the sa y of ajj before eid for the mutamatti and the mufrid if a mutamatti or a mufrid wishes to perform the sa y of ajj before eid may he do so or not if he may is a aw f necessary for it or not and will he perform that aw f in i r m or without i r m further what is the evidence for bringing the sa y forward when the anaf s have the principle it is reported in the hadiths that the prophet performed two sa ys and since the time of each of them is not specified there is no harm in bringing it forward therefore in the case asked about the mutamatti and the mufrid may perform the sa y of ajj before eid although it is better to perform it after the aw f of ziy rah sa y is not legislated without a aw f and he should perform both the aw f and the sa y while in the state of i r m as for this principle relates to the stoning the sacrifice and the shaving not to the aw f of ziy rah and the sa y note that the hadiths mention two sa ys but no time is specified for them

qir n when menstruation begins before the umrah is performed a woman entered i r m for qir n before performing the umrah she began menstruating and she had still not performed the aw f of umrah when the rites of ajj began is a dam now due from her or not and was her qir n valid or not in the case asked about because the umrah was missed the qir n became void and the dam of qir n fell away she must however make up the umrah after the days of tashr q and on account of the abandonment raf of the umrah one dam becomes obligatory see what is stated in lub b al man sik ghunyat al n sik states

a mutamatti performing more than one umrah if a person goes for ajj and performs tamattu may he after coming out of i r m stay on in makkah and perform umrah again and again or not in the case asked about a mutamatti may perform more than one umrah see what is stated in ghunyat al n sik fat w ra miyyah states the stronger view is that during the mont

a mutamatti who travels to madinah after his umrah and then performs umrah on returning a man goes for ajj and performs ajj tamattu after reaching makkah he performs his umrah and then he travels to madinah may this person perform a second umrah when he returns from madinah to makkah or not that is will this be counted as tamattu upon tamattu or not in the case asked about there is scope for performing a second umrah on the return from madinah and it will not be counted as tamattu upon tamattu it is better however to enter i r m for the ajj alone fat w ma m diyyah states a person who has performed umrah during the months of ajj has thereafter presented himself in madinah and will then perform ajj that same year and return home is a mutamatti according to im m ab an fah im m ab an fah forbids such a person once he has performed one umrah to set out from madinah and perform another umrah before the ajj according to the two companions his tamattu became void by his going to madinah so that if he now perfo

some questions concerning tamattu what do the scholars of the religion say about this matter an f q went to makkah during the months of ajj and performed umrah after completing the umrah he travelled to madinah on his return he performed a second umrah and then entered i r m for ajj from makkah 1 is his tamattu valid or not 2 is the dam of tamattu due from him or not 3 is any compensatory dam dam e jabr due from him or not 4 was the tamattu constituted by the first umrah or by the second 5 is it valid for an f q to perform more than one umrah during the months of ajj 6 if he entered i r m for the ajj alone from madinah will the tamattu be valid or not 7 will any compensator if a person performed umrah during the months of ajj and then travelled to madinah and after returning from there came in i r m for the ajj alone his tamattu will be valid this is according to im m ab an fah unlike the two companions in whose view the first tamattu became void yes if he then came from madinah in i r m for umrah and afterwards performed the ajj in their view the tamattu would be valid but according to im m ab an fah he should not do so this passage has been taken from footnote 1 of mawl n shabb r muhammad's marginal notes in mu allim al ujj j p 218 from this passage the answers to all your questions emerge either explicitly or by implication now

a mutamatti performing the sa y of ajj without i r m a man performing tamattu after coming out of i r m performed a voluntary aw f and then performed the sa y of ajj after that voluntary aw f without being in i r m what is the ruling if the sa y of ajj is performed before the standing at arafah i r m is a condition for it but if it is to be performed after the standing at arafah then performing it without i r m is sunnah in the case asked about it appears that he performed it before the standing at arafah so it was not valid without i r m and it will be necessary for him to perform it again see what is stated in ghunyat al n sik um

coming out of i r m by cutting only a few hairs a man performed ajj tamattu after performing the umrah he had only a few hairs cut and then entered i r m for the ajj what is due from him is a dam due or not if so how many dams in the case asked about the mutamatti did not come out of the i r m of umrah by having a few hairs cut his earlier i r m remains in force and since he will also have worn ordinary clothes for two or three days one dam and one adaqah become obligatory the adaqah because he cut a few hairs while in the state of i r m and the dam because he wore sewn garments and the like it is possible that he committed other violations as well but because these overlap only one dam is due furthermore it is not obligatory for a mutamatti to shave before beginning the rites of ajj see what is stated in al hid yah

performing umrah from tan m after the ajj in saudi arabia some people distribute pamphlets in which it is written that one should not perform umrah from tan m after the ajj and they also say by word of mouth that the messenger of allah and the noble companions did not perform umrah after the ajj whereas our own people perform umrah after the ajj in great numbers and regard it as a source of reward what is the ruling of the sharia on this in the view of the anaf s performing umrah is an act of reward throughout the whole year apart from the days of ajj that is one should not perform umrah from 9 dh al ijjah until 13 dh al ijjah while in the rest of the year umrah may be performed at any time when a rat ishah may allah be pleased with her had finished the ajj she went to tan m in order to make up the umrah that was still outstanding from her her brother abd al ra m n was with her and the two of them performed umrah from tan m on the night of 14 dh al ijjah the messenger of allah told abd al ra m n to take his sister outside the aram and have her perform umrah

removing the i r m of umrah because of menstruation a fifteen year old girl entered i r m for umrah and then because of menstruation did not perform the umrah she went back home and removed the i r m what is the ruling concerning the umrah now in the case asked about since the umrah was abandoned because of menstruation it comes under the ruling of abandoning raf the umrah she must therefore make up the umrah and one dam is obligatory upon her see what is stated in ghunyat al n sik al durr al mukht r states fat al qad r states

performing umrah while in the state of menstruation a woman wishes to go for umrah and her stay in makkah will be only six days she is at present in madinah but she knows that her menstruation lasts ten days she is also unable to remain apart from her family and her family are going for umrah changing the arrangements of the journey is likewise extremely difficult what course should this woman now adopt and how should she perform the umrah in the case asked about that woman should go to makkah with her family and perform the umrah after she becomes pure if no way of becoming pure is possible before the return journey and out of necessity she performs the umrah while menstruating then a dam becomes obligatory and this dam is specific to the aram see what is stated in sh m al ba r al r iq states

not trimming the hair after performing umrah a woman did not cut her hair after performing umrah then when she remembered the next day she trimmed it is the umrah valid or not is any dam obligatory or not in the case asked about the woman's umrah is valid yes as long as she had not trimmed her hair the i r m was still in force and it was only after the trimming that the i r m came to an end but if she did nothing contrary to i r m before the trimming no penalty is due from her and if she did do something contrary to i r m then the question should be put again with the details set out and it will be answered accordingly see bad i al an i al fat w al t t rkh niyyah states

performing umrah after stopping menstruation with medicine and then seeing blood again a woman is in madinah during her menstrual days she saw a few drops for three days then she took medicine and became pure and on the fifth day she performed umrah before the ten days were complete she saw blood again was her umrah valid or not is a dam obligatory or not in the case asked about since the bleeding began again within the days of her habitual period the umrah will be counted as having been performed in the state of menstruation she should therefore perform the umrah again and if she does not repeat it a dam will be obligatory see what is stated in sh m umdat al fiqh states if the bleeding of a menstruating woman stops whether by some medicine or without any medicine or does not stop completely and then whether or

whether ajj becomes obligatory upon one who performs ajj on behalf of another a man went to perform ajj on behalf of another ajj badal and did not perform his own ajj some scholars say that since he reached makkah his own ajj became obligatory upon him and that it is now necessary for him to stay on until the following year and perform ajj is this correct or not most scholars say that this person became able only through the ability of another and the principle is that is one who is able through the ability of another will not in reality be called able ajj therefore did not become obligatory upon him and staying on until the following year is in any case both legally and in ordinary practice an extremely difficult matter see what is stated in fat w al sh m

performing ajj on behalf of another when one has not yet performed one's own ajj if a person has not performed his own ajj and wishes to go and perform ajj on behalf of someone else is this disliked or not and if it is which kind of dislike is it tanz h or ta r m it is better for the one who performs ajj on behalf of another to have already performed his own obligatory ajj but this is neither a condition nor a requirement however if ajj has already become obligatory upon the one commissioned and he goes to perform ajj on behalf of another then it is makr h ta r m for him while in respect of the one who commissions him it is makr h tanz h see what is stated in shar al lub b

performing qir n or tamattu when doing ajj on behalf of another when performing ajj on behalf of another may one perform qir n or tamattu or not in the case asked about if the one who commissions the ajj has explicitly forbidden qir n and tamattu then it is not permissible otherwise it is permissible see what is stated in al durr al mukht r shar lub b al man sik states

performing ajj on behalf of a deceased person who made no bequest ajj became obligatory upon a man but he was unable to perform it and passed away and he had also not made a bequest concerning it may someone perform ajj on his behalf or not in the case asked about if someone wishes to perform ajj on behalf of the deceased as a voluntary act of kindness then god willing it is hoped that allah most high will discharge the deceased of his obligation see what is stated in lamg r sh m states shar lub b al man sik states

having ajj performed on another's behalf from the home town of the one commissioning it if ajj was obligatory upon someone and he passed away he used to live in india and now a person performs ajj on his behalf from south africa instead of from india will this be correct or not it is necessary that the ajj be performed from the home town of the one who commissions it provided that a third of the estate left behind allows for it if it does not then by way of isti s n it should be arranged from whatever place before the m q t is possible hence in the case asked about too the ajj should be performed from the home town of the one commissioning it that is from india see what is stated in sh m shiyat al a w states

paying a wage to have ajj performed on one's behalf if a person pays someone else a wage to perform ajj on his behalf is this valid or not that is is hiring someone for ajj isti j r al al ajj permissible or not in the case asked about it is not permissible to have ajj performed on one's behalf by paying a fee ajj is an act of worship of great moment and there is no scope for making it a means of earning a livelihood were that done sincerity too would be lost but if someone has already had it done in this way all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him says that the ajj will be fulfilled on behalf of the one who commissioned it while the hire contract becomes void so that the one commissioned receives only his expenses and is not entitled to a wage see what is stated in al durr al mukht r

slaughtering within the aram when a dam or the like becomes obligatory if a dam or a adaqah or an expiation and the like becomes obligatory during the ajj where should it be discharged is it necessary to send it to the aram or may it also be done outside in the case asked about the sacrificial animal whether it is an offering of thanksgiving or one due for a violation must be slaughtered within the precincts of the aram it is therefore not permissible to slaughter the offerings at any place other than within the precincts of the aram in the case of adaqah there is a choice but spending it on the poor of the aram is better see what is stated in al hid yah shar lub b al man sik states

whether a dam is due for changing the order of stoning sacrifice and shaving according to the three imams may allah have mercy on them and the two companions of im m ab an fah may allah have mercy on them keeping the order between the stoning the sacrifice and the shaving is a sunnah and not necessary please give the views of present day jurists ni m al fat w states question it has been seen at the slaughter area itself that because of the crowds of people and the great number of animals one is thrown into distress and there is a fear of injury as well and on top of that one has to walk three miles in the heat at such a time a vehicle is hard to find and poor people do not even have the fare in the light of these reasons and treating the matter as one of need does a anaf have the right in this particular case to act on the position of the sh fi s since their books plainly show that the order is not necessary answer a few passages are given here to make the matter easier to understand

whether an expiation is due for using vicks if a person in i r m uses vicks or deep heat does a penalty become due or not both have a strong smell and vicks also contains a proportion of camphor in the case asked about since both of these medicines contain 52 percent camphor using them while in the state of i r m is not correct if a person in i r m does use them an expiation will be binding the details are as follows if he applies it to a whole limb or that much a dam the compensatory sacrifice will be due and if he applies less than a whole limb then giving charity adaqah will be binding shar lub b al man sik states

whether an expiation is due when a person in i r m eats something perfumed if a person in i r m eats something perfumed is an expiation binding on him or not eating pure perfume is in the view of im m ab an fah may allah have mercy on him among the things forbidden in i r m so if someone eats a large amount of perfume a dam the compensatory sacrifice will be binding on him and if he eats a small amount giving charity adaqah will be due however if a perfumed substance is cooked into some other food and then eaten no penalty is due likewise if it is used uncooked but the perfumed substance is overwhelmed by the rest again no penalty is due though it is not free of dislike so it should be avoided ghunyat al n sik states

the ruling on using coconut oil what is the position on using coconut oil while in the state of i r m whether as a treatment or otherwise in the case asked about if a person in i r m applies coconut oil to a complete limb a dam the compensatory sacrifice will be binding and if it is less than a limb charity adaqah is due see what shar al lub b states al fat w al hindiyyah states

whether an expiation is due for using olive oil while in i r m if a person in i r m applies olive oil to a wound or the like or rubs it on his hand is a penalty binding or not in the case asked about if the olive oil was used as a treatment no expiation is binding but if it was used simply as such then a dam the compensatory sacrifice is binding if it covered a complete limb and charity adaqah is binding if it was less than that see what bad i al an i states

the ruling on smoking cigarettes while in i r m is there any dislike attached to smoking cigarettes while in the state of i r m or not smoking cigarettes is disliked both in i r m and outside it and in the state of i r m the dislike is severe so avoiding it is binding and necessary those scholars who declared it permissible did so because in their day its harm and the gross waste of wealth it involves were not yet clear moreover most people are pained by its foul smell which is why one is also forbidden to enter the mosque after eating something foul smelling see what a muslim states

whether an expiation is due for using soap while in i r m is any penalty due for using soap while in the state of i r m or not with soap the aim is to clean the hands not to perfume them and anyone who sees it does not regard it as a perfume or a fragrance but as a means of cleaning and it contains only a small proportion of perfuming ingredients and a large proportion of cleansing ones so no dam compensatory sacrifice is due for it though charity adaqah should be given ghunyat al n sik states lub b al man sik states

whether an expiation is due for wearing a mask while in i r m if a man in the state of i r m wears a mask to protect himself from dust will an expiation be binding or not in the case asked about since a mask covers a quarter of the face or more a dam the compensatory sacrifice will be due if it is worn for a full day or a full night or longer and if it is used for less than that charity adaqah will be binding furthermore the dust is not usually so severe that it may be treated as a valid excuse ghunyat al n sik states lub b al man sik states

whether an expiation is due for wearing stitched footwear while in the state of i r m it is necessary to keep the three ankle bones uncovered but is stitching permitted or not some people say that wearing stitched footwear is not permitted what is the truth of this the basic ruling in the state of i r m is that the three ankle bones should remain uncovered and if they are not uncovered the footwear should be cut down if wearing stitched footwear were impermissible what sense would there be in cutting it the hadiths and the passages of the books of fiqh show that if they are not uncovered one should cut the footwear down which shows that stitching is not forbidden without qualification see what the noble hadith states

whether an expiation is due for not making the standing at muzdalifah if someone omits the obligatory standing at muzdalifah will a dam be due from him or not in the case asked about if he omitted it without a valid excuse a dam the compensatory sacrifice is due but if he omitted it because of a valid excuse no dam is binding lub b al man sik states bad i al an i states
