a paper marriage contracted in writing alone to obtain residency in a certain country some people go through a paper marriage in court the man and the woman each write out i marry so and so and the court then issues them a marriage certificate has a marriage really been contracted or not in the case in question the marriage has not been contracted the reason is that writing from both parties is not relied upon in marriage and a written offer and acceptance is not sufficient on its own when nothing at all was said aloud this marriage is therefore of no effect al sh m states al mabs states

a woman conducting the marriage ceremony a palestinian man married a tunisian woman at the municipal office in tunisia a place that resembles a church and a court the marriage was conducted by a woman magistrate in the presence of the woman's father and brother note that the woman magistrate was a muslim and that the bride herself was present at the marriage gathering is this marriage valid or not in the case in question the person who conducted the marriage was a muslim woman and she conducted it in the presence of two witnesses so the marriage is valid for when an adult woman is able to make the offer and acceptance herself she may equally appoint another woman as her agent al sh m states fat w d r al ul m deoband states a marriage conducted through a woman acting as agent is valid so long as the offer and acceptance took place in the presence of two witnesses fat w d r al ul m 7 98 mudall

marrying a woman who is pregnant as a result of fornication a man committed fornication with a woman and now that her pregnancy has become apparent he wishes to marry her does he have to wait until she gives birth or not in the case in question if the pregnancy is from his own seed then after the marriage intimacy with her is also permissible if the pregnancy is from another man the marriage is permissible but intimacy is not he must wait until she gives birth in any event fornication is a major sin and he is bound to repent of it taby n al aq iq states al jawharah al nayyirah states

a marriage contracted with the intention of al lah is binding a man gave his wife three divorces the woman then married another man so that she could become lawful for her first husband again this second husband does not want to divorce her and the woman too is content to stay with him what is the ruling on this marriage now and is it correct to say that because the condition of al lah was attached to this marriage the marriage was not valid and the two of them may not live together in the case in question the marriage is sound and valid if the husband does not wish to divorce her that is for him to decide no one can force him moreover according to the sound position of the school attaching the condition of al lah marrying a woman only to make her lawful again for her first husband has no effect on the marriage the condition itself is void while the marriage is valid although it is disliked to attach such a condition in any case people do not usually make the condition of divorce part of the marriage contract itself it would have been mentioned verbally before the marriage al sh m states

marrying a christian woman in a court of law a muslim man married a christian woman in germany before a judge in court and in accordance with their laws is this marriage valid or not in the case in question if a proper offer and acceptance were made before the judge in the presence of two witnesses the marriage is valid and since the woman is a christian it is not necessary for the witnesses to be muslims either bad i al an i states

taking a second wife while the first wife is still married to him a married man left his home country for another country to earn a living and settled there a long time has passed and he has not gone back home he occasionally sends some money and other things to his family and it is difficult to bring his wife over to him is there any scope for this man to marry a second time in that country in the case in question if he is able to fulfil all the rights of both wives a second marriage is permitted if he is not able to do so he should be content with one wife allah has permitted marrying more than one woman in the noble qur'an he then says that if you are unable to discharge their rights and fear that you will be unfair one wife is enough a hadith states

attaching a condition to the marriage contract if a man stipulated before the marriage that the girl would give him a car what is the ruling on that and what is the ruling on accepting it in the case in question it is not valid to attach such a condition to a marriage the condition itself is void while the marriage is sound and valid taking the car comes under the ruling of a bribe and it should be given back taby n al aq iq states ni m al fat w states when the groom's family take somethi

stipulating that there will be no intimacy before the bride moves in if a young man stipulated at the time of the marriage that he would not have intimacy with his wife before the rukh at and the rukh at has still not taken place but he now wants to have intimacy with her is that permissible or not and is the condition he made valid or not in the case in question it is necessary to keep this condition furthermore even if no such condition had been made it is the custom that people do not have intimacy before the rukh at the bride's formal departure to her husband's home so out of regard for custom as well intimacy should be avoided all mah sh m says consider a few other examples of custom if a person borrows loaves of bread and later returns them going only by the number of loaves this ought not to be valid in strict law since loaves differ in size yet it is permissible because of custom and settled practice likewi

a woman who has newly accepted islam marrying during her waiting period a non muslim woman was married to a non muslim man after some time at the woman's request a judge separated them and the husband signed as well only a week had passed after this when the woman accepted islam and married a muslim man is this marriage valid or not and if it is not what should be done in the case in question according to imam ab an fah may allah have mercy on him no iddah waiting period is required while according to his two companions may allah have mercy on them it is required all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him has judged the view of imam ab an fah to be the stronger one so according to the position of imam ab an fah may allah have mercy on him the marriage described above is valid for non muslims today have no notion of a waiting period at all and they treat the waiting period as a right belonging to the husband moreover once one menstrual period has passed intimacy is permissible too in any case the more cautious course is to obs

renewing the marriage publicly after contracting it in secret a man became engaged to a girl and the marriage has been fixed for eight months' time he cannot wait that long however and wants to contract the marriage secretly now in the presence of a few witnesses and with the guardian's permission so that the girl becomes lawful for him then after eight months they would hold the marriage again formally and in public is it correct to do this or not in the case in question if the first marriage is contracted with a proper offer and acceptance before witnesses and with the girl's consent it is valid and all the rulings of marriage take effect upon it contracting a marriage in this way however is not the better course because only the household know of it while the wider community and the extended family have no knowledge of it there is therefore a strong risk of suspicion and it is extremely important to keep clear of anything that invites suspicion so that no one is given the opening to cast aspersions on another person's chastity and honour in the time of umar may allah be pleased with him it was forbidden to marry in s

contracting a marriage with the jinn can a marriage relationship be entered into with the jinn or not in the case in question it is not permissible to enter into a marriage relationship with the jinn this is the correct view all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him says

the transmitted evidence for prohibition by affinity in the hanafi school prohibition by affinity is established through fornication some people are not satisfied about this ruling to satisfy them please set out the evidence for this ruling in the light of the hadiths and the reports of the early authorities fornication is certainly a grave offence yet the bond of physical parentage is established by it that is the mother of the woman with whom the man fornicated becomes his mother in law and that woman's daughter becomes his step daughter and for this reason marriage with them becomes forbidden to him for ever 1 there is an indication of this ruling in the noble verse

marriage between a woman and her granddaughter's husband is a woman's granddaughter's husband a ma ram to her or not in the case in question the granddaughter's husband is a ma ram to the woman that is marriage between them is forbidden for ever likewise a wife's mother and her grandmothers on both sides are all ma ram al durr al mukht r states al fat w al hindiyyah states fat w ma m diyyah states everyone whom it is impermissibl

marrying the granddaughter of a half sister on the father's side is it permissible to marry the granddaughter of one's half sister on the father's side or not in the case in question it is impermissible to marry the granddaughter of a half sister on the father's side because of the prohibition arising from blood relationship al hid yah states kit b al mabs states

marrying the sister of one's stepmother is the sister of a man's stepmother that is of his father's wife with whom the father has consummated the marriage a ma ram to him or not in other words may he marry her in the case in question the sister of the father's wife with whom he has consummated the marriage that is the sister of the stepmother is not a ma ram and there is scope to marry her al sh m states fat al qad r states fat w ma m diyyah states marriag

two brothers marrying a mother and her daughter zayd and amr are full brothers and both want to marry into the same household zayd wishes to marry the mother and amr the daughter is it permissible to marry in this way or not in the case in question marrying in this way is sound and valid it is lawful coming under the noble verse and no ground of prohibition exists here fat w ma m diyyah states if the daughter married zayd's brother and the daughter's mother married zayd both marriages are valid fat w ma m diyyah 11 281 mubawwab wa murattab see further fat w d r al ul m deoband 7 176 mudallal wa mukammal imd d al a k m 2 251

marrying the co wife of one's mother in law may a man marry the co wife of his mother in law or not that is is the co wife of one's mother in law among the women who are prohibited to him in the case in question it is permissible to marry the co wife of one's mother in law because she is neither among the wife's descendants nor among her ascendants she therefore falls under bad i al an i states fat w d r al ul m states what is the ruling on marrying a step mother

marrying the divorced wife of one's stepson a man's wife has a son from her former husband is he allowed to marry that son's divorced wife or not in other words is it permissible to marry the divorced wife of one's stepson in the case in question it is permissible to marry the divorced wife of one's stepson there is no ground of prohibition here al sh m states al fat w al hindiyyah states

marrying one's son's mother in law a girl named nadh rah was married to a mad after that nadh rah's parents were divorced is it now valid for a mad's father to marry nadh rah's mother in other words is it valid to marry one's own son's mother in law or not in the case in question it is valid to marry one's son's mother in law al sh m states fat al qad r states fat w ra miyyah states is it valid for a father to marry his son's mother in law or not answer yes this relationship is not forbidden but lawful fat w ra miyyah 2 100 fat w aqq niyyah 4 354

prohibition by affinity when a man fornicates with his stepmother if a man commits fornication with his stepmother is prohibition by affinity established or not that is does that woman become forbidden to her husband in the case in question prohibition by affinity is established that is the stepmother becomes forbidden to her husband al sh m states fat al qad r states al fat w al t t rkh niyyah states

prohibition by affinity when a woman fornicates with her aunt's husband if a woman committed fornication with her maternal aunt's husband what is now the ruling on the marriage of the two of them in the case in question the burden of the grave sin of fornication will certainly remain upon them both until they repent their marriages however are not affected in any way the marriage remains in force because prohibition by affinity is limited to ascendants and descendants only al sh m states

fornication with the wife's sister and prohibition by affinity there are two sisters both of them married the younger sister's husband is now involved with the elder sister in unlawful acts and matters have even reached the point of fornication in such a situation does his own wife leave his marriage or not and if she does leave the marriage what should he do now please give a satisfying answer in the light of the sacred law it would be a great kindness in the case described the younger sister's husband becoming involved with the elder sister and committing fornication with her is impermissible indeed forbidden he must repent of this evil act he should have no dealings or contact whatever with the elder sister and it is necessary that he keep away from her nevertheless no effect falls upon either sister's marriage in the sacred law and each sister remains in her husband's marriage as before consider what al durr al mukht r states

touching the paternal uncle's wife with desire and prohibition by affinity a man's paternal uncle's wife placed her hand on him that is she touched his body with nothing in between and at that moment desire arose in him can he now marry this aunt's daughter or not in the case described prohibition by affinity has been established because of the touching with desire so it is not permissible for him to marry this aunt's daughter provided that the desire reached the level required for prohibition by affinity which is set out below al sh m states

the degree of desire required for prohibition by affinity what is the degree of desire by which prohibition by affinity is established and marriage becomes forbidden in the matter asked about the degree of desire in a man whose health is such that he normally has an erection when desire arises is that an erection occurs at the moment of touching and if there was one already that it increases in a man who because of poor health does not normally have an erection when desire arises at the moment of touching and likewise in a woman the degree of desire is that a disturbing stirring arises in the heart and if there was such a stirring already that it increases a san al fat w 5 76 al durr al mukht r states

prohibition by affinity when there is no desire at the moment of touching while taking a piece of cloth or something similar from his paternal uncle's wife a man touched her hand without any desire at all afterwards the thought kept returning to him until desire arose and an erection occurred as well this man now wishes to marry that aunt's daughter can he marry her or not given that he is certain there was no desire whatever at the moment of the touching please inform me of the ruling of the sacred law in the case described prohibition by affinity has not been established so the man in question is permitted to marry his aunt's daughter desire that arises afterwards is not taken into account what counts is desire at the moment of touching and that was not present consider what fat al qad r states al ba r al r iq states al fat w al hindiyyah states

marriage between foster siblings who share a father one of zayd's wives breast fed a girl and zayd's other wife has a son is marriage between the two of them permissible in the case described zayd's own son and the foster daughter are foster brother and sister sharing the same father just as marriage between a brother and sister who share a father by birth is not permissible marriage between a foster brother and sister who share a father is likewise not permissible consider the hadith al hid yah states al sh m states

marrying the foster sister of one's full brother a man's full brother was breast fed in infancy by the man's maternal aunt can he marry that aunt's daughter or not in other words may a person marry the foster sister of his own full brother in the case described it is permissible to marry the foster sister of one's full brother that is the brother who did not drink the aunt's milk may marry the aunt's daughter while the brother who drank the aunt's milk in infancy may not marry the aunt's daughter consider what al lamg riyyah states al durr al mukht r states

a muslim woman marrying a non muslim man a muslim woman married a non muslim man does the sacred law regard such a marriage as valid or not under the sacred law a muslim woman's marriage to a non muslim man cannot take place at all so this marriage is invalid bad i al an i states

a sunni man marrying a sh ah woman is it permissible for a sunni young man to marry a sh ah girl or not and what is the ruling in the reverse case that is can a sunni girl be married to a sh ah young man or not those sh ah who hold any belief that contradicts the definitively established truths of islam are unbelievers and it is neither permissible nor valid to enter into a marriage tie with them sh ah commonly hold the following beliefs of unbelief 1 the belief that al may allah be pleased with him is divine 2 slandering ishah may allah be pleased with her 3 the belief that jibr l peace be upon him made a mistake 4 the belief that the qur'an has been altered 5 denying that ab bakr al idd q may allah be pleased with him was a companion and so on it is therefore essential to avoid marriage and similar ties with the people of a misguided sect who hold belie

an objection to the impermissibility of marrying a sh ah or q diy n and its answer if someone marries a q diy n or sh ah girl why is it impermissible these women have not themselves apostatised it was the father who apostatised why do they not come under the ruling of the people of the book when to all appearances they do accept the qur'an and hadith whereas the people of the book do not accept them at all the people of the book are those who do not accept the religion of islam and who are christians or jews but people who consider themselves a sect of islam while opposing islam and cutting away its roots are called heretics there is no room for entering into a marriage tie with them heretics and deniers of religion are something quite apart from the people of the book furthermore the scholars have examined the beliefs of the sh ah and the q diy n s and have declared them apostates and it is not permissible to form a marriage tie with an apostate either al fat w al hindiyyah states

marriage with communists does the sacred law permit a marriage tie to be established with communists or not communism has a complete system and outlook in every field from thought and belief through to economics its intellectual foundation is atheism and the rejection of religion and the hereafter a person who is a communist holding all of these ideas therefore neither remains a muslim nor can be counted among the people of the book he falls in the category of unbelievers and marriage with such people is absolutely impermissible they also deny private ownership whereas the qur'an and hadith are filled with private ownership so denying it amounts to denying the qur'an and hadith al fat w al hindiyyah states

marriage to a hindu woman is void if a man marries a hindu woman what is the ruling on it in the case described a muslim man's marriage to a hindu woman is void separation from this marriage is necessary and the lineage of any children will not be established either consider what al sh m states al mabs states

the difference between an irregular marriage and a void marriage what is the difference between an irregular marriage nik f sid and a void marriage nik b il a void marriage is one in which the very object of the contract is absent whereas in an irregular marriage the object of the contract is present but one of the conditions of the marriage contract is missing this is what emerges from the examples given by all mah sayyid a mad al a w may allah have mercy on him and it also appears to be the substance of the fatwa of muft rash d a mad otherwise there is sharp disagreement among the jurists all mah al sh m may allah have mercy on him has discussed it in several places and in some of them he has written that there is no difference between the two since all mah al a w 's wording on this question is clear it is his position

whether marrying the wife's sister makes the marriage irregular if a man marries his wife's sister is this marriage irregular or void and is the lineage of any children born of it established or not in the case described if the woman he has married is not a valid object of marriage that is she is in the marriage bond of another man then the marriage is void but if she is not tied to another man in marriage then although the marriage is forbidden it will be irregular rather than void and the lineage of the children will be established consider what al sh m states consider what al a w 's gloss on al durr al mukht r states

marrying women of the people of the book which community today falls under the women of the people of the book whom it is permissible to marry and what is the ruling on this marriage with the people of the book of the present age is disliked the basic permissibility is not denied but fornication indecency and illicit relationships are so widespread among them that hearing of it brings the sweat of shame to the brow of humanity and it has left even the animals behind for this reason it is better and preferable not to marry them moreover women of the people of the book means those who do not deny a revealed religion as for those who do deny it marriage with them is absolutely forbidden umar ibn al kha b may allah be pleased with him disapproved of such a marriage and ordered that the woman be released consider what mu annaf ibn ab shaybah sta

the prohibition of marriage with any unbeliever a muslim woman cannot be married to a christian or a jew some people ask for the proof of this from the noble qur'an the noble qur'an has but is there any verse in which marriage to an unbeliever a jew or a christian is also forbidden allah says this noble verse states plainly that muslim women are not lawful for unbelieving men the word unbeliever is general it covers them all whether idolater jew christian or hindu tafs r al qur ub states a k m al qur' n states fat w ma m diyyah states marrying a muslim girl to someone of another religion is absolutely forb

an adult woman of sound mind marrying by her own choice a girl has reached adulthood and wishes to marry an adult young man herself but her parents are displeased and want their daughter not to marry him can an adult woman marry by her own choice or not in the case described an adult girl of sound mind has full authority over her own marriage the permission of her parents or guardian is not required at the same time parents should not be displeased without a reason recognised by the sacred law however if there is an objection on a valid legal ground for example she has married a man who is not her equal in status then the parents or guardian will have the right to have the marriage annulled consider what taby n al aq iq states

guardianship of a non muslim in the marriage of a new muslim woman a woman has just become a muslim and intends to marry a muslim man her father and her brother are non muslims can the father or the brother act as her guardian in the marriage in the case described an unbeliever cannot act as guardian in a muslim's marriage an unbeliever may however validly act as an agent so if the new muslim woman appoints her unbelieving father or brother as her agent for the marriage and he concludes the marriage before two muslim witnesses it is valid although an adult woman of sound mind may in any case conclude her own marriage without a guardian consider what al hid yah states

a non muslim judge appointing a guardian when there is none if an adult or minor girl has no guardian recognised by the sacred law can a non muslim judge appoint a muslim as her guardian or not in the case described a non muslim judge can appoint a guardian for a muslim girl just as a non muslim ruler can appoint a judge for muslims consider what al durr al mukht r states section two equality of status in marriage

the standard of equality of status in marriage in which matters is equality of status taken into account that is what is the standard of equality kaf ah according to the hanafi school equality of status is taken into account in six matters which all mah al amaw may allah have mercy on him has set out in verse al hid yah states

whether a free adult woman's marriage to a man who is not her equal takes effect if an adult muslim woman of sound mind marries a man who is not her equal in status without her guardian's permission do the guardians have the right to object to it or not and has this marriage taken effect or not many scholars after all say that such a marriage is void in the case described according to the hir al riw yah the authoritative narration of the school the marriage of a free adult woman of sound mind to a man who is not her equal does take effect however because he is not her equal the guardians will have the right to have it annulled so long as she has not borne a child by him this is the fatwa of the majma al fiqh al isl m of india and of muft kif yatull h may allah have mercy on him after the marriage the wife is lawful for her husband if the parents are displeased the matter should be placed before the local jam iyyah or before a ruler or a scholar first an effort should be made to bring the parents round and if no way c

the effect of a difference of language on equality of status will a difference of language have any effect on equality of status or not in the case described a difference of language will have no effect on the question of equality of status because equality is taken into account in the following matters religion lineage freedom wealth and occupation a difference of language is not among them however if speakers of one language generally do not regard speakers of another language as their equals then equality of status should be taken into account consider what al sh m states al hid yah states

the contracting party acting as agent for his own marriage can the husband himself act as the agent for his own marriage or not in the case described if the woman says marry me to yourself then the husband may act as the agent for the marriage and marry that woman to himself consider what al hid yah states al fat w al lamg riyyah states fat w d r al ul m deoband states the substance of the question is this a woman said i give you pe

an agent appointing another person as agent at a wedding the person conducting the marriage asks the agent shall i perform the marriage and the agent says yes in this way he becomes the agent's agent and has the offer and acceptance made with the bridegroom is this arrangement permissible or not in the case described it is not permissible for the agent to appoint another agent however if the second agent performed the marriage in the presence of the first agent the marriage is valid even so appointing an agent without need makes no sense the offer should therefore be made by the agent himself and the acceptance taken from the bridegroom consider what al fat w al lamg riyyah states fat w al azhar states

a non muslim acting as agent in a marriage a girl has become a muslim and her marriage is about to take place while her father and the rest of her family are non muslims can the father act as the agent in her marriage in the case described if the girl is an adult of sound mind her non muslim father can act as the agent for the marriage consider what al hid yah states al sh m states fat w ma m diyyah states there is a difference between a guardian and an agent in a marriage the agent's task is only to express the w

establishing the minimum dower what should the minimum dower be what is its amount is it established by any hadith or not in the case described the minimum amount of the mahr dower is 10 dirhams less than this is not permissible this limit is established by hadith and by modern weights it comes to 30 grams 618 milligrams for the details of the modern calculation see kit b al zak h chapter one consider what fat al qad r states

an examination of ibn ab tim's chain of narration the hadith what is its standing with regard to its chain of narration the narration mentioned above is not below the grade of sound because most of the narrators in its chain are reliable consider the chain of the hadith

the amount of the f im dower and the dower of the prophet's wives how much is the f im dower and how much was the dower of the pure wives of the prophet how much difference is there between the two that is what is the difference between the f im dower and the prophetic dower in the case in question the amount of the f im dower is 480 dirhams and the dower of the pure wives is 500 dirhams so the difference between the two is 20 dirhams consider what muslim states majma al zaw id states

the f im dower and the dower of the prophet's wives in present day weights in present day weights and in rand how much is the f im dower and the dower of the pure wives the amounts of the dower in present day weights and in rand may be seen in the table below kind of dower dirhams grams rand f im dower 480 1 469 grams 664 milligrams dower of the pure wives 500 1 530 grams 900 milligrams the difference between the two 20 61 grams 236 milligrams

the dower when a anaf and a sh fi differ if a sh fi man marries a anaf girl and they differ over fixing the dower is the man's position taken into account or the woman's from the statements of the jurists it appears that the dower is the woman's right which she receives in exchange for the marital bond that is hers so when there is a difference the woman's position will be taken into account that is if a sh fi man marries a anaf girl it will not be valid to give less than the amount of 10 dirhams consider what al mabs states bad i al an i states

a marriage contracted for less than the customary dower a girl married a boy secretly before two witnesses to all appearances the boy is her equal in status but the girl's father is displeased and the matter has been brought before a scholar now if this marriage was contracted for less than the customary dower can it be annulled or not and is the annulment of an arbitrator or a judge needed for this or not in the case in question according to the school of im m ab an fah the marriage can be annulled but not at the first step the husband should first be asked to pay the customary dower in full if he does not agree then the guardian from among the paternal relatives has the right to have the marriage annulled through an arbitrator or a judge if he annuls the marriage without an arbitrator or a judge no annulment takes place a judge's decision is necessary consider what al hid yah states

holding the wal mah after the marriage contract can the wal mah be held after the marriage contract before the husband and wife have come together or not in the view of the majority of scholars the wal mah that is sunnah is the one held after the wedding night or after a valid seclusion however some other scholars hold that the wal mah may also be held after the marriage contract consider what bukh r states all mah al ayn may allah have mercy on him writes in umdat al q r

how long the wal mah may be delayed until when is it correct to delay the wal mah the wal mah that is sunnah is the one held after the husband and wife have come together since its real purpose is to announce and publicise a lawful permissible relationship so the wal mah should be held on the day following the night of seclusion with the wife or on the day after that there is also room to delay it until the third day but delaying it beyond three days is not correct consider what umdat al q r states

holding the wal mah a week later on account of an excuse a man got married and also came together with his wife but on account of certain circumstances he was unable to hold the wal mah he now wishes to hold the wal mah feast a week later is it correct to do so or not will the sunnah be fulfilled or not the proper sunnah time for the wal mah is after the couple have come together however if on account of some excuse the wal mah is held a few days later or after a week the sunnah will still be fulfilled because some narrations show that a wal mah was held several days later as for what the jurists have written what this means is that after feeding people for three consecutive days the wedding celebration and the wal mah come to an end but if the wal mah was not held at all or was delayed on account of certain circumstances there is no harm in it bukh r states

food served by the bride's family after the marriage contract is it recommended merely permissible or an innovation for the bride's family to serve food after the marriage if while remaining within the limits of the shar ah the bride's family wish of their own accord to feed the guests who come that is a permissible matter however the feasts held nowadays on the occasion of weddings involve a great deal of ostentation and extravagance which is entirely contrary to the temperament of the shar ah moderation in this is therefore absolutely necessary or else it is more appropriate to bring the practice to an end altogether consider what kif yat al muft states the food that the bride's family serve to the wedding party is in itself permissible provided it is unpremeditated or is given out of need for example when the wedding party has come from

attending a wal mah feast in which evils are present if a wal mah feast involves evils such as singing music video cameras and the intermingling of men and women may one attend such a feast or not in the case in question there is no room to attend such feasts consider what al ba r al r iq states kit b al fat w states singing music videography and photography are sins and acts of disobedience and it is not permissible to attend a feast in which acts of disobedience are committed the famous jurist all mah al sh m may allah have mercy on him seeing the abundance of open sinfulness in his own age wrote that in o

the ruling on zakat when tax money is refunded a trader paid one million in tax to the tax department a case was then brought against the department as a result of which the department refunded two hundred thousand is he now obliged to pay the zakat of the past years on it or not in the case asked about the tax department was liable for the excess amount it had collected so this became like a debt that is denied and in the case of a denied debt the zakat of past years is not due even though evidence for it exists the jurists have included such a debt under m l im r wealth a person owns but cannot get at to all appearances the trader had proof which is why he took the department to court the zakat of the past years is therefore not due on this two hundred thousand the definition of m l im r and its ruling in the light of the hadiths and the statements of the jurists has been given above and may be consulted there see further what imd d al a k m states

touching the black stone in every circuit of the aw f is it necessary to touch the black stone in every circuit of the aw f and at the time of touching it are raising the hands and facing the stone also necessary or not the sunnah character of the istil m is more emphasised at the beginning and at the end of the aw f while touching the stone in each of the intervening circuits is recommended so if someone omits the istil m at the beginning or the end of the aw f that is a disliked act but if he omits it in the intervening circuits he has only left a recommended act and his aw f will be valid without any dislike the same ruling applies to raising the hands and facing the stone at the time of the istil m indeed in their case the matter is lighter still consider what shar lub b al man sik states

divorce where a husband fails to keep his wife honourably a man of property has turned his wife out of the house and gives her nothing for her keep either so that the woman is now passing her days in the greatest distress the man in question has also transferred his property into someone else's name so no redress can be obtained through the courts either in this helpless state can this woman be entitled to obtain a divorce or not if some way to a divorce can be found please write it down in the case in question when he does not keep her honourably does not give his wife maintenance and is heedless of discharging her rights as well he ought to divorce her and if the husband does not divorce her of his own accord he will be compelled to divorce her but without a divorce the woman cannot become free of her husband's marriage the woman should place her case before the jam iyyat al ulam and those gentlemen may annul the marriage after making enquiry see what al durr al mukht r says al ba r al r iq states

giving three divorces and then claiming to have meant emphasis in the course of a quarrel a man said to his wife divorce to you divorce divorce he now says that he said it by way of emphasis and that only one divorce was intended should the wife accept what he says or not given that she has already brought the case forward if a man gives three divorces and then says that he intended emphasis the fatwa given accepting his word as a matter of conscience will be that one divorce has taken place but in the case in question the woman having heard three divorces has brought the case forward so the judge or the jam iyyat al ulam will be bound not to accept the husband's word but to decide upon the outward facts and issue a ruling of three divorces see what al durr al mukht r says tanq al fat w al midiyyah states

intending emphasis when explicit words of divorce are repeated if a man said in front of his wife the words and intended emphasis by the second and the third will one divorce take effect or three and will the divorce be revocable or irrevocable in the case in question because he intended emphasis one irrevocable divorce will take effect as a matter of conscience but in the judgement of a court his word will not be accepted fat w q kh n states al hid yah states al durr al mukht r states

divorce given with no particular intention in mind if a man said to his wife divorce upon you divorce divorce and had no intention at all his mind being empty how many divorces will take effect a rat muft far d may his shade endure says that if no intention was present to his mind then only one revocable divorce has taken effect al ashb h wa al na ir states

saying divorce but intending the divorce from the first husband a man had earlier given his wife two divorces some time later during a quarrel he said divorce but he says that what he meant by it was you were divorced by your first husband is the wife now allowed by the sharia to remain with her husband or not note that the wife had indeed been divorced by her first husband in the case described if the husband's intention was exactly what is stated in the question then no divorce has taken place and the wife may remain with her husband in future however he should avoid words of this kind al a w states in short the better course is for the couple to take their case to an arbitrator the arbitrator will put the husband on oath if he swears to it and the wife had in fact been divorced by her first husband then she may remain with her husband

saying if a man says how many divorces take effect what is the disagreement over this and whose view is the fatwa given on in the case described according to the hir al riw yah one divorce takes effect in the view of imam zufar may allah have mercy on him however two divorces take effect and the fatwa is given on imam zufar's view that is according to the position adopted for fatwa two divorces take effect al hid yah states fat al qad r states al durr al mukht r states

saying three times out of fear and without knowing its effect a new muslim's father in law got three divorces out of him in english the new muslim did not know what pronouncing three would mean out of sheer fear he uttered the words without any intention so how many divorces took effect by these words in the case described only one revocable divorce took effect because he did not mean the later two utterances as fresh divorces he merely repeated the words because he did not know the difference between one and three he will therefore be believed as a matter of conscience if however the wife brings the case before a judge the judge will rule that three divorces took place taby n al aq iq states al ashb h wa al na ir states

three divorces by saying divorce divorce divorce in the course of a quarrel between a husband and wife the husband said to his wife divorce divorce divorce are you happy now will you keep quiet now afterwards the husband says that he only spoke this way in order to silence her what is the ruling of the pure shar ah in this case in the case described three divorces have taken effect because explicit words of divorce need no intention and divorce also takes effect when spoken in play or in jest his plea that he was only silencing her will therefore not be accepted if however he had taken witnesses beforehand for instance if he had said in advance i am going to speak in this way but my intention is not to divorce her only to quieten my wife then he is believed and no divorce takes effect radd al mu t r states al durr al mukh

giving two divorces and then stating that three were given a man gave his wife two divorces then when the wife's relatives came to visit and asked him how many divorces he had given he said i gave three divorces in the eye of the shar ah how many took effect in the case described three divorces took effect through the husband's admission of three divorces even though in reality he had given only two al durr al mukht r states al fat w al t t rkh niyyah states

an examination of the jurists' maxim the jurists write what does this mean and what are its limits this expression of the jurists is used in two senses and there is a difference between them the first sense like a judge the woman has the right to decide for herself on the basis of the outward wording whether relations are lawful or unlawful for her for example the husband says you are divorced divorced divorced and then states that he intended repetition and emphasis and did not intend three and the woman has herself heard the three pronouncements from her husband's own mouth if the matter now comes before a judge's court the judge will not take the husband's intention into account but will rule in accordance with the outward wording that three divorces have occurred

whether apostasy of a thrice divorced woman removes the need for al lah a man gave his wife three divorces after that his wife became an apostate we seek refuge with allah and some time later she became a muslim again of her own accord can she now marry her former husband without al lah in the case described after three divorces the wife is not lawful for her former husband without al lah an intervening valid marriage to another man which is consummated and then comes to an end and apostasy does not remove the requirement of al lah either al durr al mukht r states

saying you are unlawful to me three times if a man said to his wife you are unlawful to me unlawful unlawful how many divorces take effect and is this expression allusive or explicit in the case described the expression you are unlawful to me is in origin an allusive one but because of customary usage an irrevocable divorce takes effect by it without any intention the later scholars have given their ruling on this basis and since one allusive divorce cannot be joined to another only one irrevocable divorce takes effect al durr al mukht r states

saying it's all over a man said to his wife it's all over everything is finished the relationship between us is over what is the ruling does a divorce take place or not and if it does is it revocable or irrevocable in the case described the husband's words it's all over that is everything is finished the relationship between us is over are in fact one of the allusive expressions if the husband said them intending divorce one irrevocable divorce has taken place if there was no such intention no divorce has taken place consider what al durr al mukht r states khul at al fat w states

saying our islamic marriage is over if a man said to his wife several times our islamic marriage is over what is the ruling in the case described the jurists have counted these words our islamic marriage is over among the allusive expressions so if he said them intending divorce one divorce has taken effect upon his wife and according to the explicit statement of the author of al ba r the divorce that takes effect by such words is a revocable one consider what al ba r al r iq states so if he said them several times and meant each utterance to establish a fresh divorce rather than merely to stress the first three divorces will have taken effect fat w q kh n states

saying get out of our house zayd said to his wife get out of our house and at her husband's word she went off to her parents' home some ten or eleven years have now passed does a divorce take effect or not and if it does which kind the point is that throughout this period zayd has never once called his wife back in the case described these words are among the allusive expressions so if zayd intended divorce when he said them one irrevocable divorce has taken effect otherwise no divorce has taken place and the woman remains his wife as before consider what al fat w al lamg riyyah states al ba r al r iq states

saying get out go to your mother's house during a quarrel with his wife these words came out of a man's mouth get out go to your mother's house after saying them when the matter of intention occurred to him he fell into doubt as to whether he had intended divorce or not now that the intention is doubtful does a divorce take effect or not in the case described these words are not explicit but allusive and so they depend on the intention since the intention is in doubt no divorce has taken effect it is a settled principle of fiqh that certainty is not removed by doubt so a ruling of divorce will not be given on the strength of mere doubt consider what al durr al mukht r states imd d a

saying i am not your husband and you are not my wife if a man said to his wife go i am not your husband and you are not my wife and he did not intend divorce does a divorce take effect or not in the case described if he said these words intending divorce a revocable divorce takes effect and if he had no intention of divorce no divorce takes effect even though he said them in anger consider what is recorded in al fat w al lamg riyyah al durr al mukht r states

what a discussion of divorce means the jurists write that when a discussion of divorce is going on a divorce takes effect by allusive words even without an intention what then does a discussion of divorce mean in the jurists' terminology a discussion of divorce means that the wife or someone else on her behalf demands a divorce or that a divorce has already been given and if the husband then utters one of the allusive words a divorce takes effect without any intention consider what all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him says al jawharah al nayyirah states

whether the waiting period is binding when the husband apostatises when a husband becomes an apostate the woman leaves his marriage automatically but may she then marry someone else straight away or is a waiting period binding on her because of the husband's apostasy his wife has left his marriage automatically but before she may marry another muslim a waiting period is binding and necessary for her too without completing the waiting period a second marriage will not be valid and the waiting period begins the moment the husband apostatises al durr al mukht r states

the waiting period after intercourse entered into by mistake a man had intercourse with another man's wife thinking she was his own wife and only afterwards learnt that she was not will the waiting period be binding on that woman or not likewise what is the ruling on the waiting period in a defective marriage and what is the ruling regarding a child born from such a union in the case described intercourse by mistake and a defective marriage in which intercourse has taken place the waiting period is binding and necessary in both situations the waiting period is three complete menstrual cycles if she does not menstruate because she is too young or too old the waiting period is three lunar months and if she is pregnant the waiting period lasts until she gives birth the child is not illegitimate its lineage is sound and it belongs to the man who had intercourse by mistake al fat w al hindiyyah states

whether the waiting period is binding on a girl who has not reached puberty an adult man married a girl who had not yet reached puberty and after they had been alone together in private he divorced her is the waiting period binding on her or not in the case described the adult husband divorced the girl after a sound seclusion so the waiting period is binding even if there was no intercourse for the waiting period to become binding it is enough that seclusion took place fat w sh m states

a fresh waiting period after intercourse by mistake with a woman already in her waiting period a man gave his wife an irrevocable divorce or three divorces and then had intercourse with her by mistake during the waiting period must she begin a fresh waiting period or does she simply complete the one she is in in the case described having intercourse by mistake during the waiting period makes a fresh waiting period binding and the two waiting periods overlap that is when the first waiting period comes to an end she completes whatever remains of the second she is not required to observe the two separately and in full as regards a further divorce taking effect and maintenance however it is the first waiting period that counts bad i al an i states

the waiting period when divorce takes place before the wife has been sent to her husband a man married and before his wife had been sent to him a divorce took place will the waiting period be binding on the wife or not in the case described if there was no seclusion of any kind after the marriage that is no meeting in private then the waiting period is not binding but if there was seclusion even a defective one the waiting period has become binding fat al qad r states fat w q kh n states al ba r

the waiting period for a young girl who is not able to have intercourse a man married a young girl who is not able to bear intercourse and after a few days a divorce took place is the waiting period binding or not in the case described even a young girl who is not fit for intercourse and cannot bear it must observe the waiting period since the divorce came after seclusion consider the following fat w d r al ul m deoba

the waiting period of death for a non muslim woman a christian woman was married to a non muslim man and the man then died may she now marry a muslim man without observing a waiting period or not in the case described a waiting period is not binding on the non muslim woman on account of the death of her non muslim husband she may marry a muslim man at once however after the marriage the muslim husband should not have relations with her immediately he may do so after she has had one menstrual period if she is pregnant she must observe the waiting period until she gives birth sh m states

the waiting period of death for a woman who has newly embraced islam a non muslim woman was married to a non muslim man the man then died and after that the woman embraced islam is the waiting period binding on her or not in the case described if any of the days of the waiting period remain she must observe it because on embracing islam she became bound by the rulings of islam and the waiting period is one of those rulings al fat w al hindiyyah states bad i al an i states fat w sh m states

how the waiting period is observed in a divorce given according to the sunnah a man gave his wife one divorce in one period of purity a second divorce in the next period of purity and then a third divorce in the third period of purity how is the waiting period to be observed now that is after the third divorce must she wait three menstrual periods or only one in the case described two menstrual periods of the waiting period have already passed after the first two divorces so after the third divorce only one menstrual period has to pass and when that one is over the waiting period is complete it is not necessary to observe three fresh menstrual periods after the third divorce a narration in ibn m jah states mu annaf ibn ab shaybah states the learned ibn al hum m may allah have mercy on him s

how a woman whose period of purity is prolonged observes her waiting period if a divorced woman who is breast feeding has a prolonged period of purity how is she to observe her waiting period and if a woman does not menstruate for a long time how should she observe the waiting period should she wait for her periods to come or observe the waiting period by months in the case described a woman who is breast feeding is not normally one whose purity is prolonged in most cases her monthly periods return after a few months so she must observe the waiting period by menstruation if however a woman really is one whose purity is prolonged so that waiting so long to complete the waiting period is more than she can bear she should take treatment to bring her periods on if that does not succeed and there is a strong fear of her falling into sin she should obtain a fatwa from a m lik mufti for a waiting period reckoned by months nine months or one year or have the matter settled by a sharia council and act on that al ba r al r iq states

the waiting period when the husband dies before the wife has been sent to him a girl was married but she had not yet been sent to her husband and no seclusion had taken place when the husband died is the waiting period binding on her or not in the case described the waiting period is binding and necessary in every case for a woman whose husband has died whether or not she had been sent to him and whether or not seclusion had taken place she must observe a waiting period of four months and ten days and if she is pregnant her waiting period lasts until she gives birth bad i states

news of a husband's death reaching his wife after the waiting period has already passed a man died but his wife could not be informed and the news reached her only after a long time is she now required to observe the waiting period given that four months and ten days indeed a good deal longer have already gone by or does the waiting period begin from the moment the news reached her kindly inform me of the ruling of the sacred law and earn a great reward in the case described the waiting period began on the very day the husband died and it came to an end as soon as four months and ten days had passed now that the news has reached her after a long time there is no need for a second waiting period because the waiting period is tied to the death itself and not to the news of it it therefore begins even without her being informed bad i states

the waiting period of death occurring during the waiting period of divorce a man divorced his wife and while she was in the waiting period of the divorce the husband died should the woman now complete the waiting period of the divorce or begin the waiting period of death or observe each separately how is she to observe the waiting period where the husband dies during the waiting period of divorce there are three situations and each has its own ruling 1 if the woman is pregnant her waiting period remains until she gives birth and the birth of the child ends both waiting periods even if it takes place within a few moments 2 if she is not pregnant and the waiting period is that of a revocable divorce the first waiting period lapses and she observes only the waiting period of death 3 if the waiting period is that of an irrevocable divorce she observes the longer of the two terms that is she takes whichever of the two is longer if one of them is completed first she also completes the remainin

the waiting period when the child dies in the womb of a pregnant woman a woman was observing the waiting period that lasts until the birth of her child when the child suddenly died in the womb how is she to complete her waiting period now in the case described the womb should be cleared by medicine or by an operation if the pregnancy was of four months or more the waiting period is over if the pregnancy was of less than four months the waiting period will end only when three menstrual periods have passed al ba r al r iq states

the waiting period when a pregnancy dries up a woman whose husband had died was pregnant and her pregnancy suddenly dried up how is she to observe her waiting period now if the pregnancy of a woman whose husband has died is established with certainty her waiting period lasts until she gives birth but if the pregnancy is not established or it was established and then dried up her waiting period will be four months and ten days consider the following if the pregnancy is not established her waiting period is four months and ten days al fat w al hindiyyah states

whether the waiting period ends when a pregnancy is aborted if a woman has her pregnancy aborted what is the ruling on her waiting period does the waiting period end with the abortion or must she still complete three menstrual periods in the case described if four months of the pregnancy had already passed and she then had it aborted the waiting period is over and no fresh waiting period is needed if however the pregnancy was of less than four months the waiting period will end only when three menstrual periods have passed the abortion alone does not bring it to an end but after four months it is impermissible and sinful to have a pregnancy aborted without a strong reason recognised by the sacred law fat w sh m states

the waiting period when divorce follows two years of separation a man has two children by his wife but because of a quarrel she has been living apart from him for two years and there has been no coming together in that time he has now divorced her some people say that since the purpose of the waiting period is to be sure that the womb is empty and that is already certain no waiting period is binding on the woman what does the sacred law rule and what are the wisdoms behind the waiting period in the case described when the divorce comes after two years of separation the waiting period of divorce is still binding and necessary the purpose of the waiting period is not only to establish that the womb is empty it is also to give expression to the regret and grief at the ending of the first marriage and the severing of that tie it is as it were a mark of respect for the marriage bond this is why the waiting period has been made binding even on women who have not reached puberty and on those who have passed the age of menstruation although a woman cannot conceive before puberty or after that age and there is no doubt at all about the mixing of lineage even so the pure sacred

the wisdom behind the obligation of the waiting period from the discussion above it becomes quite clear that there are two wisdoms behind the waiting period 1 making certain that the womb is empty and free of pregnancy this safeguards lineage 2 giving expression to regret and grief at the severing of the marriage tie isl m q n n nik o al q records the wisdom of the waiting period is that the woman grieves at her separation from her husband and mourns his death the second wisdom in the waiting period is making certain that the womb is empty that is being satisfied that nothing of the husband's semen remains in the woman's womb so that if she marries again there is no fear of lineage being mixed and of doubt arising as to w the answer to this objection is that before intercourse or seclusion the blessing of marriage has not become firmly established the woman has not yet tasted its affection and love so the blessing is not full and complete and for that reason the waiting period is not binding either the learned ibn al hum m may allah have mercy on him says section two an account of mourning

washing the head bathing and applying oil during the waiting period is it correct for a woman to wash her head bathe and apply oil during the waiting period or not in the case described washing the head bathing and applying oil during the waiting period are permissible and correct but she should not use them for the sake of adornment using them out of habit or for a genuine reason that is where not using them would bring on a headache or severe discomfort is correct al hid yah states

what is permissible during the waiting period an account of what is permissible during the waiting period 1 bathing washing the head and keeping the body and the clothes clean and tidy are permissible and correct 2 putting oil in the hair when there is a need for it and combing the hair are also permissible for instance where there is a fear of lice 3 it is not necessary for her to sit in one particular room of the house she may stay wherever she wishes in the house and she may also move about inside it 4 household work and the like are also allowed there is no prohibition in that 5 where there is a need there is scope for her to go to a hospital to see a doctor as far as possible she should call the doctor to the house fo

a woman in her waiting period leaving the house when a parent dies a woman is observing the waiting period after her husband's death or after divorce during the waiting period her mother or father dies if she does not go to see her father or mother she will carry the grief and regret for the rest of her life and will have to put up with reproaches may she go for a short while to see her mother or not please note that bringing the body to her is extremely difficult and burdensome in the case described one of her parents has died while she is in her waiting period if she does not go grief regret and distress will weigh on her for the rest of her life and there is a strong likelihood of taunts and criticism from the family in both of these situations there is room for her to go out because of the need and necessity involved the jurists have permitted a widow to go out when there is a need there is also a narration in sunan ibn m jah that the maternal aunt of j bir may allah be pleased with him was divorced she wanted to go out to harvest her date palms but a man stopped her she came to the messenger of allah and he said go and harvest them perhaps

an elderly woman spending her waiting period at her son's house a widow spent part of her waiting period in her own home but because of loneliness and old age she now wishes to spend the rest of it at her son's house is she allowed to do so or not and will she have to start the waiting period again in the case described there is room for her to spend the waiting period at her son's house because of her loneliness and old age she does not need to begin the waiting period afresh completing the remaining days is enough consider the following from al durr al mukht r

husband and wife living in the same house during the waiting period if a husband and wife live in one and the same house during the waiting period what is the ruling in the case described a woman who has received a final irrevocable divorce should spend her waiting period somewhere she will not mix with her husband and where he will not be coming and going if living in one house carries no strong likelihood of their meeting and falling into sin and the elders of the household are able to keep them apart then spending the waiting period in the same house is not forbidden al ba r al r iq states

living together after three divorces after three divorces may a husband and wife live together in old age so as to help and support each other or not in the case described the jurists have permitted them to live together so as to help and care for each other in old age likewise if there is no one to look after the woman and arranging her maintenance and lodging is difficult and there is no fear of temptation they are permitted to live together and help one another but they must not deal with each other as husband and wife consider the following from al durr al mukht r

marrying during the waiting period a man gave his wife one irrevocable divorce after one menstrual period had passed he renewed the marriage he then gave her a second irrevocable divorce after that the first menstrual period of her waiting period came from 1 march to 11 march the woman then says that a second period came from 17 march to 26 march after that she married another man then when a third period came from 12 april to 21 april the marriage was renewed and on the same day after the marriage a few drops of blood appeared is this marriage valid or not in the case described the second marriage took place during the waiting period the bleeding seen from 17 march to 26 march cannot be menstrual blood because the fifteen day interval that must follow the end of the previous period the minimum period of purity had not passed a marriage with a woman who is in another man's waiting period is void the husband is therefore obliged to leave her and if he is not willing to do so the wife should have the marriage annulled through the jamiat after that she should observe a waiting period as a precaution and then she will be free and may marry elsewhere if she wishes consider the following from al durr al mukht r

the lineage of children born of a marriage to a hindu woman if a man marries a hindu woman is the lineage of the children established or not in the case described since a marriage with a hindu woman is not valid the lineage of the children will not be established consider the following from al durr al mukht r imd d al fat w states lineage is not established through a void marriage note the necessary explanation of void and defective marriages has already been given in volume three of th

the lineage of a child born after a long separation if a man has been away travelling for the past few years and in his absence a child is born to his wife will the child's lineage be established from him or not the existence of the marriage tie is enough to establish lineage any child born while the marriage subsists therefore has its lineage established so in the case described too since the marriage is in place the separation is of no account and the child's lineage will be established from this man the husband may of course deny the lineage by li n mutual imprecation but since the law of li n is not in force in this country denial by li n is not possible either a hadith states al fat w al hindiyyah states

the lineage of children born to an abducted wife a man abducted someone's wife and has kept her with him for a long time and children have been born during this period but so far the husband has not divorced her in such a case from whom will the children's lineage be established in the case described this man's abducting another man's wife and taking his pleasure with her is fornication and lineage is not established through fornication the children's lineage will therefore be established from the actual husband consider the following hadith al durr al mukht r states al fat w al hindiyyah states

the father visiting his child daily and being refused access after a couple separate the child is brought up in its mother's care as the sharia directs during that time is the father entitled to see the child or not if the mother wishes to stop him does she have the right to do so and what is the ruling on visiting the child every day in the case described although the child is with its mother during the period of custody to stop the father from seeing and visiting the child is a wrong time should therefore be set aside for visits and the days and times should be settled between the parties indeed if the father wishes to visit every day he may do so consider the following from al fat w al lamg riyyah the jurist ab al layth may allah have mercy on him states in khiz nat al fiqh that a father may visit his child every d

whether a child is given a choice after the age of seven after a couple separate the child is handed over to the father once he reaches the age of seven but is the child entitled to choose for himself with whom he will live or must he stay with his father in the case described the child has no right of choice in the matter of custody after the age of seven rather the father has the better right to him in view of his education and upbringing however if a mufti or a q sees some benefit in the child staying with his mother then at their discretion the child may remain with her fat w sh m states

the maternal grandmother has precedence over the paternal aunt in custody a husband and wife died in an accident they have a six year old boy and two girls one aged nine and the other very young the man has a mother and a sister but the mother has refused to bring up the children the woman has a mother living now the man's sister and the woman's mother both wish to bring up the children and of the two the maternal grandmother is the more pious and respectable which of them then is entitled in law to bring up the children in the case described the children's maternal grandmother has the better right to custody as the sharia directs the children will be given into her care and upbringing and the paternal aunt has no right while the maternal grandmother is there consider the following from al fat w al lamg riyyah al fat w al t t rkh niyyah states

the paternal grandparents have no right of custody while the maternal grandmother is there what do the honourable scholars and muftis say about the following matter my daughter has been widowed since her husband's death she has been living here with her two children if she now marries again do the children's paternal grandfather and grandmother have the right to take the children from their mother by force when the children's maternal grandfather and grandmother are willing to keep them and if she does not marry again how long may the children stay with their mother the children are one boy and one girl in the case described if this woman marries a man who is not within the prohibited degrees of the children the one entitled to bring them up is their maternal grandmother so while the maternal grandmother is there the paternal grandfather and grandmother have no right of custody consider the following from al ba r al r iq

keeping children with their mother after the period of custody has ended if a man's wife has been divorced and the children are over seven and nine years of age and the mufti or the q considers it better for them to stay with their mother may such a ruling be given or not in the case described custody and upbringing turn on what benefits the child if the father's qualities and character are not such that he can bring the child up properly and there is a strong likelihood that the child's morals will be corrupted and the mufti and the q consider it in the child's interest for him to stay with his mother then it will be decided that he remain with her even though the father's right has already been established after seven years for a boy and nine years for a girl fat w sh m states

arranging a suitable marriage for a girl who is in her mother's custody a girl who has not yet reached puberty is in the custody of her mother who has been divorced may the mother arrange a marriage for the girl into a suitable family or not given that the girl's father is apparently not happy with the marriage in the case described the right to bring up a girl who has not reached puberty belongs first to her mother and once the girl turns nine the father's right is established under the sharia since the father can attend properly to her education and upbringing and the guardianship for marriage also belongs to him but if the father has for some reason ceased to be trustworthy and the girl remains in her mother's care education and upbringing even after reaching puberty and the father has no sense of responsibility and there is a fear that staying with the father would lead to her being neglected or to her morals being corrupted then the mother may keep her and once she has reached pube

telephoning the child and taking him out during holidays the child is in his mother's custody and the mother's right lasts until he is seven during that time may the child's father speak to him on the telephone or not in the case described while the child is with his mother if the father wishes to speak to him by telephone or to see him he may telephone him and he may see him he may also take him out within the city but he is not permitted to take him outside the city consider the following from fat w sh m al fat w al hindiyyah states see further j mi a k m al igh r 1 101 al fat w al t t rkh niyyah 4 90 ukm al walad inda iftir q al zawjayn al ba r al

the father's obligation to maintain a six year old child a man divorced his wife they have one son aged six who is at present in his mother's custody who is obliged to maintain the child and what does maintenance have to include in the case described the mother is responsible for the six year old child's care and custody while maintenance and similar expenses are the father's responsibility maintenance includes food and drink clothing accommodation and living costs medicine and medical treatment school fees and all other necessary expenses consider the following from al ba r al r iq

maintenance and lodging for a pregnant divorced woman who left her husband's house a pregnant woman ran away from her home in may in august her husband gave her one divorce will she now be entitled to maintenance and lodging from may to august and from august until she gives birth or not in the case described because the woman ran away from her husband's house without cause she will be regarded as disobedient and a disobedient wife is no longer entitled to maintenance her maintenance therefore lapsed from may until the birth of the child that is from the moment she left her husband's house however since her waiting period began in august during the days of the waiting period she will be entitled to lodging alone that is from august until she gives birth she will be entitled to lodging al durr al mukht r states fat w sh m states

the ruling on a child of six or seven after separation a husband and wife have been separated the child is under seven years old and the father has kept up no relationship with the child is the child's maintenance obligatory on the father or not in the case described the maintenance of a child under seven is binding on the father in every case whether or not there is any relationship between them consider al durr al mukht r which states al fat w al hindiyyah states

foster kinship through a husband sucking his wife's milk if a husband sucks his wife's breast and drinks her milk is the prohibition of foster kinship established or not and if it is not established why not in the case described foster kinship is not established between husband and wife the reason is that for foster kinship to be established the milk must be drunk within the period of suckling and according to the position on which the fatwa is given the period of suckling is two years while a husband is ordinarily well past the age of two so drinking milk after two years does not establish foster kinship if however a woman's husband were to drink her milk while under two years of age foster kinship would be established and the wife would become unlawful to him even so it is not permissible for a husband to drink milk from his wife's breasts and this must be avoided altogether
