making good an endowed property that has been sold a man sold an endowed property and now because of a legal obstacle it is impossible to take it back what form should the redress take for example it was sold to a non muslim among whom there is no concept of the rules of endowment a property that has been endowed is endowed for ever it is not lawful for anyone to sell it and if someone has sold it the sale does not take effect and the property remains endowed as before but if because of a legal obstacle its recovery is impossible then another property should be bought with the price and endowed in accordance with the endower's conditions just as the jurists have written that if a property becomes altogether unusable it is permissible and correct to sell it and to buy another in its place and endow it

putting up a building on endowed land a piece of land has been endowed for a mosque but there is no building on it so no income is being earned from the land and no benefit is being had from it it does not even cover its own expenses such as tax and the mosque does not have the means to build on it the mosque's trustees are therefore worried a man has told them that he would like to build a shop there with his own money not as an endowment but so that it remains his own property and that he will pay a reasonable rent for the land and will also keep giving the mosque a portion of the income is there room for building in this way and can a privately owned building be put up on endowed land a derelict endowed property that cannot be put to any use may be built upon so as to make it usable doing so is not merely permissible but preferable and better but when the mosque does not have the means to make it usable the mosque's trustees may give another person permission to build that building will be his own personal property until he endows it and a monthly rent will be collected from him beyond that he may of his own free will give the mosque whatever portion of the income he wishes this arrangement should however be put in writing with the signatures of both parties and kept safely in the mosque's file so that with the passage of time his heirs do not lay claim to owne

how the income of an endowment is to be spent in our city a man endowed a house for an islamic institution an islamic school the income of the house used to be distributed for the benefit of the islamic school for the past four years the house has been in the possession of the institution's administrators what may the income of the house now be spent on that is where should the income be used the income of an endowment is to be spent in accordance with the conditions laid down by the endower the trustee may however with the good of the endowment in view make such changes in its administration and in the way its income is spent as do not defeat the purposes of the endowment if the endower has laid down no condition then the income of the house should first be spent on improving and repairing the house and the land after that it should be spent on the most pressing needs and then it may be spent on those entitled to it such as the salaries of the school's teachers and staff in short it should be spent as need and benefit require consider what al durr al mukht r states

whether an endower may alter the conditions of an endowment a woman drew up a deed of endowment and set out a number of conditions in it for instance she wrote that she would live in the house for as long as she was alive that after her death the house would be endowed for the sake of allah that four people would benefit from it and that after their deaths it would be endowed for the mosque now after drawing up this deed she wants to make some changes in it for example she wants to name only one person in place of the four does she have the right to make such a change given that the deed contains no condition permitting changes once the endower has drawn up a deed of endowment and made the endowment without reserving to herself any right to make alterations she will not be permitted to change the deed afterwards in the case in question therefore she no longer has any right to change or alter it consider what fat w sh m states

whether a mosque may own property in its own right as a legal person are mosques and religious schools capable of owning property or not that is if someone gives a mosque a carpet or something similar without endowing it or sends books to a religious school without endowing them are these things endowments or are they the school's own property in the same way if someone gives the hide of a sacrificial animal to a mosque or a school does the mosque or the school become its owner or not and if they wish to spend the price of the sacrificial hide on the teachers' salaries may they do so mosques and religious schools have the standing of owners in their own right and of legal persons so if someone gives a thing to a mosque or a school without endowing it the mosque or the school becomes the owner of that thing and the trustee acquires the right to dispose of it on this basis if a person gives the hide of a sacrificial animal to a mosque or a school the mosque or the school becomes its owner and it may be sold and its price spent on the teachers' salaries in the terminology of the jurists this question is known as legal personality and its clearest and least disputed parallel is the system of the public treasury the wealth held in the public treasury is not endowed

whether the ka bah may own property in its own right as a legal person if someone makes a gift of something to the ka bah does that thing become the property of the ka bah or not in the case in question a thing given as a gift to the sacred house does become the property of the sacred house consider what lamg riyyah states i l al sunan states see also

keeping a basement separate from the mosque a man wishes to buy a piece of land for a mosque and before the purchase he forms the intention that its basement or ground floor will be used for parking or something else and that the mosque will be on the upper floor is it permitted to do this or not in the case in question the intention formed before the purchase to keep the lower floor out of the mosque is valid and to exclude it from the mosque on that basis is correct and sound so once the building is put up the upper floor will be the mosque and there will be room to use the lower floor for the other needs of the mosque consider what al durr al mukht r states

relocating a mosque when the area around it is deserted if the settlement around a mosque comes to an end and the mosque falls into disuse may it be sold and a mosque built somewhere else for example there is a mosque in a city where muslims live after some time acting on an order of the authorities those people move elsewhere and only one household or a few muslims are left or the mosque is left unused altogether what is to be done with the mosque in that case is it permitted to demolish the mosque sell the land and build a mosque elsewhere with the money obtained is it permissible to move the mosque's fans copies of the qur'an carpets and the like to another mosque if it is permissible where should they be moved may they be u according to the position on which the fatwa is given it is not permissible or correct to demolish a mosque or to sell its land it should rather be left as a mosque and the people living round about should keep it in use if however no muslim is left in its vicinity then out of necessity all the mosque's furnishings indeed even its walls may be moved to another place and a mosque built there the land of the mosque however is not to be sold because according to the stronger view that spot whatever may become of it remains subject to the ruling of a mosque

what to do with a mosque's old carpet a new carpet has been laid in a mosque what should be done with the old one the trustees hold several views on this 1 it should be distributed among the worshippers 2 it should be sold to the worshippers and the money used for the mosque 3 the carpet should be given to some other mosque which of these is correct as regards the old carpet 1 it is not correct or sound to distribute it among the worshippers because it is endowment property 2 it is permissible and correct to sell the old carpet and use its price for the mosque 3 if another mosque is in need of it it is also permissible to give it there consider what fat w lamg riyyah states al durr al mukht r states

whether a place becomes a mosque in the legal sense merely by being built a mosque's structure and courtyard are ready that is the building work has been completed but for certain reasons the trustees have not yet begun the five daily prayers in congregation there some other people want to pray in it is this correct or not and do the rulings of a mosque in the legal sense come into force as soon as the building work is finished or not three things are required for a place to become a mosque in the legal sense 1 the land must be endowed for a mosque 2 the endower must have separated the endowed land from his own ownership or from someone else's in such a way that no right of his or of anyone else remains attached to it 3 the prayer must have been performed in congregation in it at least once with the trustee's permission if all three of these are found the rulings of a mosque in the legal sense apply otherwise they do not in the case in question since the prayer has not been performed in congregation there it has not become a mosque in the legal sense and those who wish to pray there may do so with the tr

repairing the path to a mosque out of mosque funds the path leading to a mosque has fallen into a very bad state and the worshippers generally come to the mosque and leave by this path is there room to improve and repair this path out of the mosque's funds or not the path leading to a mosque is counted among the mosque's needs and it is permissible and correct to spend the mosque's funds on the mosque's needs improving and repairing the path out of the mosque's funds is therefore entirely permissible and correct consider what al durr al mukht r states lamg riyyah states

whether the right of a perpetual lease passes to the legal heirs land taken on perpetual rent which is called a lease or pa ah will inheritance operate in it or not in our province of gujarat india the lands taken from the government on lease or pa ah have a formal permanent lease agreement in which the government undertakes to give the land to the tenant on perpetual rent the one who takes it on rent is entered in all the revenue records as a tenant only and the government remains and is regarded as its owner the tenant is given the right to every kind of disposal over this land for example letting it to some other person building a house and letting it out and so on but the tenant cannot sell this land that is no sale agreement for in the case in question the right of a perpetual lease is a right that belongs to the tenant in perpetuity for this reason after the tenant's death this right will pass to his legal heirs however since there is no ownership in it it will not be permissible to sell it ownership will remain with the original owner the heirs too have only the right to use it or to let it out or to lend it the right does not pass to them by way of ownership furthermore this right passes to all the legal heirs consider what all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him says about key money

buying a house with a bond can a house be bought with a bond or not the encyclopaedia britannica defines a bond as follows the term bond' has been defined in the encyclopedia brittanica vol 2 pg 140 as follows a loan contract issued by local state and national governments and by private corporations specifying an obligation to return borrowed funds the borrower promises to pay interest on the debt when due usually semi annually at a stipulated percentage of the face value of the bond that is it is a loan given by a government or a company on the condition that the borrower will repay it together with a fixed amount of interest this definition shows that taking a bond is an interest based transaction which is counted among the ruinous sins

the degrees of dire need and ordinary need what kind of need is it in which taking an interest bearing loan is permissible when a person is under unbearable compulsion it may be hoped that there is no sin in his taking interest fat w ma m diyyah 16 378 f r qiyyah the notes on fat w ma m diyyah record for further detail see ni m al fat w 1 186 fat w ra miyyah 9 237 chapter on loans and kit b al fat w 5 320

dealing with a person who holds money obtained from interest if a person has money obtained from interest actually in his hands may we enter into any kind of transaction with him or not and if he wishes to pay it towards a debt he owes may we accept it in settlement of our debt or not is there any difference between a muslim and an unbeliever in the case asked about if it is known for certain that a particular sum of a muslim's money is unlawful then it is not permissible to sell him anything in exchange for it and to take that money where it is not known for certain there is room for it but if an unbeliever holds money obtained from interest it is permitted to accept that money in settlement of a debt so long as he has not committed something that reason itself holds forbidden and repugnant such as deception theft or robbery imd d al a k m states unbelievers are indeed addressed by the subsidiary rules in matters of penalties and transactions but for a ruling of unlawfulness and invalidity a general address is not

dealing with a company that trades in interest a person orders a machine through a company until the money is paid to the company the company charges rent for the machine the company however deals in interest with a bank it takes money from the bank at interest buys machines and the like with it and then pays interest on that money the question is whether it is permissible to buy a machine from this company or not given that the purchasers pay no interest at all and this is purely the company's own private affair in the case asked about if zayd bought the machine for say one hundred thousand rand through the company and the company paid the hundred thousand and the company will now recover one hundred and twenty thousand in instalments then this is interest even if it is called rent but if the company bought the machine for one hundred thousand and sold it to zayd for say one hundred and twenty thousand on deferred payment then this is a cost plus sale and it is permissible and if the machine remains the property of the company while zayd goes on paying it a fixed rent every month and after a set period zayd either returns the machine or the company sells it to him at a reduced price o

entering into transactions with a bank a person entered into certain investment transactions with a bank and because of the bank's rules the bank imposed interest upon him will this interest count as a debt and in the matter of zakat will the interest be deducted or not the pure sharia has declared transactions involving interest impermissible and forbidden and in the same way dealing in interest with a bank that trades in interest is impermissible and forbidden every muslim man and woman is obliged to keep away from it severe warnings have come in the qur'an and the hadiths against those who deal in interest one must therefore repent of such a transaction from the depths of one's heart nevertheless where such an interest bearing transaction has been entered into out of need and compulsion or by mistake or through sinfulness and wrongdoing and the bank has imposed interest then in the light of the statements of the jurists who counted levies e

exchanging steel utensils with a difference in quantity some people bring old steel utensils and take new utensils from a shopkeeper the shopkeeper does not weigh the old steel utensil instead he says give me such and such an amount of money along with it and take a new utensil is this procedure permissible or not steel is among the goods sold by weight in which interest operates equality on both sides is therefore necessary in buying and selling so if the two are equal in weight it will be impermissible to take an additional sum of money from one side if however a person sells the old utensil for money and then adds a further sum to that money and buys a new utensil the transaction will be entirely free of any taint note that tirmidh states

keeping money deposited in a bank some people carry out public welfare and charitable work but because they are short of funds they keep the money in a bank and take the interest so that the sum will grow and sometimes they move it from one bank to another in order to obtain more interest is this procedure permissible or not public welfare and charitable work is very good and work that brings benefit to god's creation should be done as much as possible but keeping money in a bank for the purpose of taking interest is impermissible and forbidden how can it be right to commit something forbidden for the sake of a recommended deed and to take money out of one bank and place it in another in order to get more interest is worse still whatever interest has been taken should be given away in charity to the poor without any intention of reward this should not be done in future and the people concerned should repent there is however room for keeping money in a bank for safekeeping though caution is preferable

taking possession within the same session in usurious goods zayd went to a shopkeeper and the shopkeeper sold him one kilo of wheat in exchange for one kilo of rice the shopkeeper weighed out the wheat but before he could weigh out the rice someone called zayd away he went and returned after ten minutes that is the session changed is this transaction permissible or not if the shopkeeper had weighed out the rice in zayd's presence and zayd then went away and took possession of the rice on his return the transaction is valid but if the shopkeeper had not yet weighed out the rice then the transaction lapsed when zayd left and a fresh transaction should now be made al hid yah states radd al mu t r states

whether interest is established in quantities below the sharia measure it is stated in the general works of fiqh that if a person carries out an interest bearing transaction in a quantity of less than half a it is permissible for example if he gives one handful of wheat flour and takes two handfuls this is permissible is the fatwa given on this or not and is this practice permissible or not the imams differ as to whether interest is established in the mutual exchange with a difference in quantity of usurious goods of the same kind in a quantity below the sharia measure that is less than half a 1 im m ab an fah and im m ab y suf hold that interest is not established in the case mentioned above the reason is that for interest to be established there must be a measure that is volume or weight and the sharia has fixed half a as the smallest standard of volume which is absent here 2 the position of the three imams im m m lik im m sh fi and im m a mad ibn anbal and of im m mu ammad is that interest is established in this case too and that the transa

selling one apple in exchange for two apples in our region apples are sold by number and by count if two apples are taken in place of one because the quality of the single apple is superior is this permissible or not given that apples are sold by number in this area by the rules of fiqh it ought to be permissible since apples are not goods measured by volume or by weight from the wording of ibn hum m however it appears to be impermissible so one should avoid it especially since in our times apples are sold by weight in most places ibn hum m states

selling dried dates in exchange for fresh dates if a man sells one of tamr dried dates in exchange for ru ab fresh dates im m ab an fah holds it permissible while the other imams and the two companions hold it impermissible the position of the two companions rests on a hadith that most hadith scholars and jurists have recorded the wording of the hadith is what answer does the imam give to this hadith kindly provide a satisfying reply 1 im m ab an fah says that since in common usage fresh dates are dates the two may be sold in equal quantities when im m ab an fah went to baghdad and people put this question to him he said that ab ayy sh in the chain of the hadith quoted above is weak and he added that if fresh dates are dates then both being dates they may be sold in equal quantities and if they are not dates it ought to be permissible because the two are then of different kinds mull al however raised an objection to this sometimes the kind is one and yet a sale in equal quantities is still not permissible because the measure is not equal as when roasted wheat may not be sold in exchange for u

the garage card and its ruling a company gives people a garage card on this basis when they buy petrol with the card the company itself pays the bill to the garage then at the end of the month the company works out the account and charges the purchaser a further 15 per cent and paying this extra sum is also obligatory is there any room for a transaction of this kind or not the usual way a garage card works is that one goes on filling up with petrol by means of it and at the end of each month one receives a full statement and pays an amount corresponding to the petrol taken nothing further has to be paid this arrangement is sound because no interest or other addition has been imposed as much as was borrowed has been repaid but in the case asked about there is mention of taking a further 15 per cent if that is the position there is no room for it it is plain interest if however the company grants a period of grace so that if payment is made within say one month no extra sum need be paid while if payment is made after the month a further 15 per c

taking interest money from a non muslim if interest money comes into the hands of a non muslim does it become his property or not if a non muslim offers a muslim a gift out of interest money is the muslim allowed to accept it or not and what is the ruling if a muslim gives a gift out of interest money if interest money comes into a muslim's hands the muslim does not become its owner he must return it if the owner of the money is known he should give it back to him and if the owner is not known it should be given away in charity without any intention of earning reward it should be given away as a way of ridding oneself of a burden and a calamity the money may then rightly and lawfully be given to a deserving poor or needy person who does not own the zakat threshold accepting a gift of interest money however is not permissible or correct all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him says

paying interest with interest money kh lid took a loan of 100 000 rand from a bank and bought a house with it and the bank told him that he must pay back 110 000 kh lid now wants to sell that house to zayd for 110 000 so that he can settle his debt zayd has said that he will pay 100 000 rand from lawful wealth and give 10 000 from interest money is it permissible to do this or not dealing in interest is a major sin and painful warnings about it have come in the qur'an and the hadiths kh lid should therefore repent and resolve not to take an interest bearing loan in future as for interest money the jurists have written that it should either be returned to its real owner if the owner is known or else given away in charity to the poor without any intention of earning reward as for paying interest out of interest money the ruling is that the interest money may be returned under any heading whatever to the same bank from which the interest was received but taking it from one bank and paying it to another bank is not permissible badhl al majh d states

paying government taxes with interest money is it correct to pay the following taxes out of interest money or not 1 income tax 2 temporary occasional taxes 3 vat the 14 per cent tax on goods purchased which the law obliges one to pay in the same way is it permissible to pay the following municipal charges out of interest money or not 1 the tax on vacant land 2 the tax on the land on which houses stand as far as we are aware the banks of south africa are not government or state banks but private ones it is therefore not correct to pay interest money in government taxes interest money should either be returned to the party it was taken from or given away in charity to the poor and needy without any intention of earning reward nowadays it is the second course that is acted upon since there is no way of returning the money to the bank moreover some of the government taxes mentioned above are not levied unjustly in one form or another their benefit reaches us whether we choose it or not so paying them in this way would amount to benefiting from interest ma rif al sunan states

spending interest money on public welfare projects is it allowed to dig a well for the poor and needy with interest money or not in the same way may it be used to build a madrasah wall and so on or not and is it permissible to spend it on other public welfare and charitable projects or not the great scholars and muftis differ over this question most muftis hold that interest money should not be spent on digging a well but should be given away in charity to the poor without any intention of earning reward some indian muftis however such as sayyid mufti abd al ra m l jp r may allah have mercy on him hold that interest money may be spent on public welfare projects caution lies in acting on the position of the majority though if someone has already spent it in this way there is room for that if it is genuinely necessary to spend the money on digging a well or on some other good work the following course may be adopted the interest money is given to a poor person

giving interest money to support a political party an election was held here in barbados and a muslim organisation wished to support one of the parties in it with financial assistance to support that party the organisation collected donations from muslim brothers and sisters and it also collected interest money from muslims the question now is whether it is permissible for a muslim to collect interest money for the sake of a political party if it is not permissible what is the ruling on the money that has already been collected and handed over the scholars differ over spending interest money on public welfare as has been mentioned earlier in the case in question however the general interest of the muslims in a non muslim country is bound up with this financial support and the government is a non muslim one so if interest money is collected and given as support in this way and the muslims do not use it themselves there should be room for it kif yat al muft states question may interest money be spent on religious education on public welfare and on poor muslims answer interest money that has been received may be spent on the needy and the like on paying off the debts of muslims who are in debt on education whet

paying off a loan with interest money some people buy blankets and the like with interest money and distribute them among those entitled to receive them on one occasion no interest money was available so they took a loan from the lill h general charity funds bought blankets and so on with it and then when interest money came in they repaid the loan with it is this method permissible or not the basic rule regarding interest money is that it should be returned to its real owner but if the owner is not known it should be given away in charity to the poor and needy without any intention of earning reward some scholars however have ruled it permissible to pay off a loan of this kind with interest money as well so when there is a need there is room to act on their position even so spending it after first employing the device of transferring ownership is preferable and is the more cautious course al sunan al kubr of al bayhaq states

the disposal of lost property and of interest is much the same is bank interest disposed of in the same way as lost property or in a different way in the case in question the two are disposed of in much the same way and apparently there is no difference between them for instance it is permissible to give lost property to poor non muslims and interest money may likewise be given to them in the case of lost property no transfer of ownership is necessary it may be spent on public welfare and on the shrouding and burial of the dead in the same way in the view of some scholars no transfer of ownership is necessary in the case of interest either in other words both interest and lost property must be given away in charity but neither has to be transferred into someone's ownership al durr al mukht r states

transferring ownership when giving unlawful wealth in charity money obtained by impermissible means in non muslim countries such as interest money must be given away in charity but is it necessary to give it to the poor or may it be used for some other good cause without transferring ownership to a poor person some muftis hold that wealth in which there is taint and unlawfulness must be given to the poor other muftis however say that it may also be spent on other good causes such as building a lavatory or making paths and roads these scholars draw a distinction between an obligatory charity and wealth that must be given away in charity with an obligatory charity such as zakat or adaqat al fi r they say transferring ownership to a poor person is necessary whereas with wealth that must be given away in charity it is not when the messenger of allah reached the dwellings of the people of tham d and the companions kneaded dough with water from their well he ordered that this dough be fed

profit earned with unlawful wealth a man gave someone one thousand rand and received one thousand five hundred back so the 500 must be given away in charity but if by mistake before giving it away he put the 500 rand into some business and turned it into 1 000 rand must this further 500 also be given away in charity or is there room for him to keep it and use it in the case in question if a person bought something while pointing to the unlawful wealth and then paid that very wealth pointed to as the price the income from it is impermissible and must be given away in charity but if he bought something with that wealth without pointing to it or pointed to the unlawful wealth yet paid lawful money then in the view of imam ab al asan al karkh may allah have mercy on him the profit earned will be lawful and only the original unlawful wealth will have to be given away in charity this does not mean however that one may make unlawful wealth a means of earning and profit doing that is entirely impermissible if someone has done it by mistake

giving other money in charity in place of interest money a man's money is deposited in a bank in england and interest accrues on it if this man pays the poor out of other money in his possession on behalf of the bank's interest will he be free of liability or is it binding and necessary that he withdraw that very money from the bank and give it away in charity in the case in question the superior and better course is that the actual money be given away in charity but if in place of the interest money some other money is given in charity in order to discharge the liability the liability will be discharged because currency is not specified by designation then too banks do not hand over the interest money separately they hand it over mixed with the capital so that distinguishing between the capital and the interest is impossible al durr al mukht r states

converting interest money into something else if someone buys something with interest money and gives it to a poor person is that correct for example if he buys a sewing machine with interest money and gives it to a poor person is that correct or not is it necessary to give the money itself to the poor person without any intention of earning reward or may goods of another kind be bought with it what emerges from the statements of the jurists is that unlawful wealth must be conveyed to its real owner and that when the owners of the wealth are unknown that very article or sum of money should be given away in charity converting it into something else is not correct all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him says it also states

third party insurance is third party insurance permissible or not its substance is that some liability may fall upon a person in the future and insurance is taken out in order to meet that liability for example when a car is brought onto the road there is a risk that as the result of an accident loss may be caused to someone else in which case financial compensation becomes binding upon the driver so insurance is taken out against this and at the time of an accident the insurance company pays the compensation this is generally called third party insurance in some western countries it happens that if a person does not clear the snow in front of his house and someone slips on that snow and suffers bodily there is a difference of opinion among the scholars concerning third party insurance some scholars call it impermissible for instance muft taq may his blessings continue says that insurance of every kind is forbidden and impermissible because it comprises interest and gambling see fat w uthm n 3 328 isl m awr jad d ma sh mas il 7 290 and isl m awr jad d ma shat o tij rat p 161 some others incline towards permissibility consider what jad d fiqh mab ith states if an accident has occurred through the driver's fault and a person has died in it then in the light of the sharia the responsibility for paying the blood money for accidental homicide falls upon the driv

gharar its definition and its ruling an investigation into gharar uncertainty and its ruling the scholars have stated various definitions of gharar consider a few of them below all mah al sarakhs may allah have mercy on him says all mah al ayn may allah have mercy on him says in umdat al q r

the a a company there is nowadays in our country the a a company that is a company which undertakes that if your car breaks down on the road it will help you to have the car towed and repaired and in return for this you have to pay a fixed sum every year is this valid or not and will this company be called an aj r kh a hireling engaged exclusively or an aj r mushtarak a hireling who serves the public similarly there is another company for safeguarding cars if the car is stolen that company traces it and for this too a certain amount is paid every month is this valid or not in the case asked about this transaction is valid for the reason that a service is received in exchange for the money there is however this difficulty it often happens that the car does not break down and no occasion arises for having it repaired will the company still be entitled to the wage or not if this company is an aj r kh it will be entitled to the wage but it takes on the work of others as well and for that reason it ought to come under the ruling of an aj r mushtarak the answer these companies fall neither wholly under the ruling of an aj r mushtarak nor wholly under that of an aj r kh rather they stand between the two therefore in view of the aspect of aj r kh

taking out insurance with a company a removals company transports goods for a fixed fee say 50 rand and in return for an additional fee say 10 per cent it offers insurance on the goods being transported it is possible that this company obtains the insurance from another company the item being transported is an expensive one for example a laptop computer or the like is it permissible to take out such insurance since two kinds of corruption are found in insurance 1 interest and 2 gambling and both are forbidden insurance too is impermissible therefore in the case mentioned it is impermissible for the person having his goods transported by the company to take out insurance whether the removals company itself provides the insurance or obtains it from another company that is because in this case the company is as it were an agent on behalf of the person having the goods transported and the actual contract has been concluded between him and the insurance company accordingly it is necessary to keep away from such a transaction consider what a k m al qur n states

becoming an agent for an insurance company zayd is an insurance agent on behalf of several companies those companies do long term and short term insurance business and it is obvious that the companies pay him commission for supplying them with customers most insurance companies are involved in interest based business is such an agency permissible or not and what is the ruling on taking the commission nowadays the business of most insurance companies comprises interest and gambling an agency for an interest based company is therefore not permissible and the commission received from an interest based company is also impermissible one should keep away from it yes as for companies whose business is for the most part lawful there is room for taking part in them consider what the noble qur n states

a doctor taking out insurance is it permissible for a doctor to take out medical insurance that is to enter into an insurance arrangement in the sense that if some mistake occurs on his part in an operation or in treatment and the patient suffers harm he may make it good with the help of the insurance company for muslim patients ascribe benefit and harm to the divine decree and bring no claim but disbelievers who do not believe in the divine decree file a claim in the event of a mistake and recover a great deal of money so in order to escape this difficulty may a doctor take out insurance or not generally in insurance of this kind money is obtained in exchange for money and the insurance company also pays an additional sum upon it this is plain interest which is forbidden and impermissible it is therefore binding and necessary upon a muslim in his capacity as a muslim to keep away from insurance of this kind yes if the insurance company does not pay the money over but instead in return for that money has the harm suffered by the patient made good in some large hospital through an experienced specialist doctor there will be room for it

the provident fund a monthly sum in a fixed proportion is deducted from the salaries of government employees the government does this compulsorily and the employees have no choice in it then after the employment comes to an end it is returned with a further increase is it permissible in the light of the sharia to take this money and use it or not in the case asked about taking the provident fund money on the completion of employment and using it is permissible and valid because the sum that the government deducts from the salary falls within the category of an entitlement and does not come into the employee's ownership hence the interest that the government pays upon that sum is not interest since interest is the name for a stipulated increase upon a sum that one owns whereas this sum is not owned consider what kif yat al muft states the sum that the department pays on the provident fund and likewise whatever is added under the name of interest upon the total of the two is all permissible money in the sharia it is not in

the voluntary provident fund a man is an employee of a company and his salary there is two thousand rand but two hundred rand is deducted from it every month and this deduction is made with his own consent the company then adds a further one hundred rand to it and after the employment ends the whole sum is received is it permissible to take this money or not a great many scholars have recorded the same ruling for both kinds of provident fund however in having the deduction made by one's own choice there is a resemblance to interest and for that reason one should keep away from it so that it does not become a means of consuming interest consider what a rat muft mu ammad shaf may allah have mercy on him says however if money is deducted into the provident fund by one's own choice there is in this both a resemblance to interest and the danger of turning it into a means of interest so it should be avoided pr vident fan par zak t awr s d k mas alah p 4 jad d mu mal t ke shar a k m states if an employee without compulsi

the pension fund government employees receive a monthly stipend as a pension reckoned at half their salary after their employment comes to an end is it permissible in the light of the sharia to take it or not a pension is merely a gift from the government and a form of assistance so taking it is permissible and valid consider what a rat muft kif yat all h may allah have mercy on him says the pension that an employee receives on retirement from service is permissible kif yat al muft 8 97 fat w ma m diyyah states in some departments a pension is given at the end of employment as a reward for good service this too is not called interest fat w ma m diyyah 16 394 j mi ah f r qiyyah p ke mas il states a pension has in one respect the status of a gift therefore whatever arrangement is settled between the pensioner and the government is valid and it is not gambling or

the retirement policy during his lifetime the deceased of his own choice nominated his wife for his life insurance and retirement policy now after his death the insurance company will pay his wife a large sum and a monthly pension will also continue to be received is this transaction permissible or not a life insurance and retirement policy in which money is received in exchange for money along with an additional sum is an interest based transaction and is impermissible it is binding and necessary to keep away from it but if someone had entered into such a contract by mistake or through ignorance or through sinfulness then whatever exceeds the sum paid in should be given away in charity without the intention of reward the sum that was paid in will then after the death of the deceased be distributed among all his heirs in the manner laid down by the sharia as for the company's monthly pension it comes under the ruling of a gratuity and there is room for it jad d ma sh mas

the education policy the deceased took out an insurance policy for his daughter's education paying a fixed sum every month to the insurance company when the daughter reaches the age of 25 she will receive a large sum of money from the company will it be permissible to take that large sum and to pay it out for educational fees and the like or not in educational insurance too money is received in exchange for money together with an increase this is therefore an interest based transaction and is impermissible it is permissible to take and use only the sum that was paid in the remaining additional interest bearing money should be given away in charity without the intention of reward

a mutual assistance fund among the women here the following practice is current fifty women each deposit two hundred rupees with one woman and every month by the drawing of lots that money goes to one of them then the next month to another and in this way every one of them receives it and none is left out nor is there any interest in it each woman contributes thereafter exactly the amount she has taken is this arrangement permissible in the eyes of the shar ah or not the case in question is not merely permissible it is preferable and better its status is that of financial cooperation by lending to one another that is the woman whose name comes out first has in effect been assisted by the other women by way of a loan the merits of cooperating with one another are found beyond number in the qur n and the hadiths by way of a handful as a sample of the whole heap a few are set down below

betting on horse races what do the respected muftis and eminent scholars say about the following matter there is a man who takes part in horse racing competitions he has won prize money in these competitions several times and with that prize money he has set up a shop in which he sells food drink and similar goods and he now wants to set up a further shop with the same money the question is whether it is correct for this man to take part in horse races and to take the prize money or not and if his income is not lawful will buying and selling at this shop be sound or not in the case in question laying a bet on winning or losing a horse race and taking prize money on the basis of a stake stipulated from both sides is impermissible and unlawful it is gambling and the noble qur'an has forbidden it it is not permissible to set up a shop with this unlawful money and one should also avoid buying and selling at such shops if however the prize is stipulated by only one of the two parties and not by the other it is permissible likewise if someone other than the men taking part in the contest gives the prize taking it is also permissible and correct see what the noble qur'an states

the mu allil in a horse race wager if zayd and amr stipulate in a horse race that whichever of them comes first will be given ten thousand rand by the other this form is impermissible the hadith indicates that bringing in a mu allil makes such a stipulation permissible what is the form of this mu allil the party who makes it lawful there are two ways in which a mu allil may be brought into a horse race wager so as to make it lawful the first form of the mu allil zayd and amr say to the mu allil if you win the race the sum we have agreed on goes to you and if you lose you will give nothing to the winner rather the winner will take the agreed sum from the other of us two four cases arise from this arrangement 1 if the mu allil wins he receives twenty thousand rand 2 if either zayd or amr wins he receives the other's ten thousand and the mu allil receives nothing 3 if zayd and amr both finish level with the mu allil neither of them receives anything 4 if the mu allil finishes level with ei

accepting a prize given by a third party a function is being held at a school and there is an entrance fee of 50 rand for a seat in the hall in effect a contribution to the school one or several prizes a mobile phone for example are given out by a lucky draw not by the owner of the school but by a third party if a person who has paid the fee wins such a prize is it permissible for him to take it or not in the case in question if a person who has paid the fee wins this prize taking it is permissible and correct for two reasons 1 the prize is not given in exchange for the 50 rand fee because the 50 rand is an entrance fee in other words it is a contribution to the school and is not the price of the prize for this reason it is permissible and correct 2 the second reason for its permissibility is that this prize comes from a third party and not from the owner of the school and taking a prize from a third party is permissible and correct see what bad i al an i states

prize bonds one form of prize bonds is that people each pay in 10 rand and then one man or a few men receive a prize while everybody else's money is lost that is one form of gambling the second form is that the 10 rand each person paid in is returned to him and some people receive a prize by way of a lucky draw on the face of it there is no gambling in this since no money is lost and on the face of it there is no interest either since the definition of interest is here no condition has been laid down with any individual that he will be given such and such an extra sum what is the ruling of the sacred law on this second form both of these current forms of prize bonds are impermissible see what isl m awr jad d ma sh mas il states some scholars have held prize bonds to be permissible taking the view that here there is no suspension of ownership upon a risk since whatever money a person has paid in he receives back in every case so this is not gambling and therefore becomes permissible this view however is not correct although gambling as such is not present here interest is for if a man's name comes out in the draw then in return for the hundred rupees he paid for example he will receive one hundred thousand one hundred rupees some have raised the doubt that this is n

prizes for solving a newspaper puzzle newspapers often carry announcements that whoever explains the meaning of a certain thing or solves a certain puzzle will receive a prize of such and such an amount since no fee or the like is paid along with the newspaper is it correct to take this prize or not one does of course have to buy the newspaper what is the ruling on that a prize scheme is published in the newspaper and taking the prize for solving it is permissible and correct there is no harm in it it is a one sided arrangement involving neither gambling nor interest and the money spent on buying the newspaper was paid for the newspaper which was received in exchange see what tanw r al ab r states al fat w al hindiyyah states

prizes for solving a puzzle that requires an entry fee in some places an advertisement is placed saying that whoever sends in a solution together with a fee of say one rupee will be entered among those whose solutions are correct and the prize will be given to the person whose name comes out by lottery or draw the question is whether there is any room for taking part in such schemes or not and whether it is permissible to take the prize if one does take part if those running the scheme charge an entry fee then it falls under gambling and is impermissible there is no room for taking part in such schemes and keeping away from them is obligatory and necessary if someone has mistakenly taken part and received a prize the whole sum must be given away in charity there is no room for putting it to his own use see what the noble qur'an states the jurist ab al layth al samarqand may allah have mercy on him writes in his commentary on maysir

winning money through a bank draw a certain bank in south africa has devised a new kind of account it pays no interest on this account instead whoever opens the account is automatically entered into a competition and stands a chance of winning one million rand if someone wins will it be permissible for him to take that money or not if the sum deposited is certain to remain intact and an extra sum is received along with it then in the view of some scholars this is interest and if the sum deposited can be lost then it is plain gambling both are unlawful and impermissible in the sight of the sacred law fat w sh m states in isl m awr jad d ma sh mas il a rat muft taq ib may his shade endure says some scholars

prizes in a fishing competition a place has been set up on the sea shore where a fishing competition is held a fee is taken from those who enter and prizes are then awarded in order of rank out of the money collected to whoever catches the biggest fish is this arrangement permissible or not and will it be correct to take the prize given that some entrants come away with nothing in the case in question this arrangement is forbidden and impermissible because it falls under gambling see how the scholars have defined gambling in the following words al ta r f t al fiqhiyyah states fat w sh m states a san al fat w states question the red

taking part in the vodacom competition nowadays many companies run competitions in which valuable prizes are given to the winner one instance of this is the competition offered by the vodacom company the way this company works is that a person sends a message sms to vodacom on which about ten rand is spent at the end of the day a draw is held among those who sent messages and the one whose name comes out is given a bmw car worth two hundred and fifty thousand rand nowadays our muslim brothers too take part in this competition with great enthusiasm in the sight of the sacred law is it permissible to take part in such a competition or not and if someone is given a car as a prize will it be permissible for him to take in the case in question since the vodacom competition consists of gambling taking part in it and obtaining the prize is not permissible or correct if someone does receive the car it is obligatory and necessary for him to sell it and give the money in charity he may however keep only as much as he spent on entering fat w sh m states

paying a bribe to obtain a licence a man is failed every time he goes for a driving licence it has emerged that they never pass anyone without a bribe the question is whether the sacred law allows a bribe to be paid in this situation or not if the man knows how to drive properly and is also familiar with the road rules and in spite of this he does not succeed in obtaining the licence and there is no way out except paying a bribe then it is hoped that paying a bribe under compulsion will not be called to account in the hereafter taking a bribe however is forbidden and impermissible in every case j mi al tirmidh states al hid yah states

lotteries what do the eminent scholars say about the following matter in this country and in other countries the practice is common that numbered slips are sold in ordinary shops people buy them mark a few numbers and hand them back if the numbers they have marked match the numbers drawn a large sum is received as a prize is it permissible to obtain money in this way or not these slips are sold at various prices some for 50 rand and some for 100 or 200 rand similarly in the villages children play marbles in this way they all place their marbles inside a circle and take turns aiming at them and whoever's aim is true takes them all while the rest are left with nothing is this permissible in the case in question both practices are impermissible and unlawful because they involve the suspension of ownership upon a risk in that payment from one side is certain while from the other side it is a mere hope and uncertain this is precisely what is called gambling in a k m al qur n im m al ja may allah have mercy on him states

speculative trading sa nowadays the business of speculation sa has reached its height in most of the large companies is there any room for it in the sacred law or not the object of this dealing is not the purchase of shares at all what is intended is rather that as prices rise and fall the profit and the loss should simply be settled and squared off against one another between the two parties in this form the price is not paid over by the buyer nor is the article sold handed over by the seller such a dealing is therefore impermissible and not allowed speculation is a form of qim r that is gambling in the dictionary f r z al lugh t the meanings given for sa b z are 1 a kind of gambling in which bets are laid upon the judgement given about some matter 2 a merchant's deal there are two reasons for speculation bein

prizes given by lucky draw to promote trade in most countries the practice is common in large shops that in order to sell as many goods as possible and to bring their trade to its height they hold draws for prizes and whoever's name comes out in the draw receives a prize either in cash or in kind in the purchase the buyer pays the full price but the prize is something separate which only a few out of hundreds of buyers receive the question is whether it is permissible to obtain such a prize or not given that some muftis say that such a prize is impermissible because it involves interest and gambling in the case in question fixing such a prize and obtaining it when one's name comes out in the draw is permissible and correct it falls neither under interest nor under gambling it is not interest because in the view of the jurists interest is the increase that is not in exchange for any countervalue and that is stipulated in the contract see what the author of al hid yah states nor can it be called gambling because the jurists have defined gambling as money being stipulated from both sides the following conditions must however be observed 1 the seller

a debtor who puts off payment a man has given someone a loan the debtor does not repay it and although the creditor asks for it again and again he still puts him off what is the ruling on this to withhold someone's money without any excuse recognised by the sacred law and not to give it even when it is demanded despite having the means is oppression and unlawful in the sight of the sacred law the debtor should therefore repay the loan as soon as possible see the warning that has come in the noble hadith against putting off payment despite having the means translation ab hurayrah may allah be pleased with him reports that the messenger of allah said for a man of means to put off payment is oppression

borrowing a of wheat if someone sells one of wheat in exchange for one of wheat to be handed over a month later this is impermissible but if he lends one of wheat on the understanding that it will be returned after a month this is permissible and is the standing practice even though under the rule the upshot and substance of both is one and the same the jurists say that a guarantee kaf lah made on condition that the debt is discharged is a transfer of debt aw lah and a transfer of debt made on condition that the debtor pays is a guarantee because it is the meanings that are taken into account when it is the meanings that are taken into account why is a loan permiss what the rule requires is that this loan too should be impermissible but since the messenger of allah used to take loans and passed away in a state in which he had taken a loan from a jew it is permissible by way of juristic preference on the basis of the hadith just as salam is an exception to the sale of what does not exist moreover there is need in a loan giving and taking a loan is therefore permissible see what a al bukh r states another narration states

repaying a loan of rands in dollars a man lent another man one hundred thousand rands for a term of one year if he then says to the debtor after one year you will give me 15 000 dollars instead of rands is that permissible or not in the case described if the lender says to the borrower that after one year he should return 15 000 dollars in place of the one hundred thousand rands he was lent and the one hundred thousand rands are handed over in that same sitting then this arrangement is permissible and valid no interest or anything of the sort is involved in it because currency is not money by its very nature thaman khilq but money by convention thaman urf moreover the currencies of different countries count as different kinds so mutual possession within the sitting is not required the exchange is permissible on a deferred basis as well possession of one of the two currencies is however necessary s

taking back more when the currency has lost value i gave zayd 1 000 rands as a loan and we agreed on a term of one year my question is this when zayd repays me after a year the value is no longer what a thousand was worth it has fallen so if i take the thousand at its former value that is interest and if i take a thousand at its present value i lose out is there any way in which i can both avoid the loss and not fall into interest in the case described you may take back only the thousand rands that you gave you are not permitted to take anything more than that because taking more in a loan amounts to interest in a loan once the term has ended it is the equivalent of the thing that is returned which is exactly why lending goods that are valued individually is not permissible and conventional money has the ruling of a fungible item consider what al durr al mukht r together with fat w al sh m states

reducing a debt on condition that it is paid early one man owes another 10 000 rands on a deferred basis the debtor said to him waive one thousand and i will pay 9 000 straight away is this permissible or not in the case described if this was laid down as a condition the arrangement is not permissible if however they come to a settlement without any condition then it is a favour on both sides the creditor has done the debtor a good turn by reducing the amount and the debtor has done the creditor a good turn by paying early similarly if some third party proposes a settlement saying waive such and such an amount and the debtor will pay at once there is room for that as well it is related that abdull h ibn ab adrad may allah be pleased with him owed a debt to ka b ibn m lik may allah be pleased with him and the two of them were arguing about it in the mosque ras lull h cam

taking more when a debt is recovered after twenty years twenty years ago a woman sold a car for 45 000 rands which was the market price at the time but the buyer never paid the price the buyer has now repented and wants to pay the money after 20 years however 45 000 is very little in market terms its purchasing power has changed a great deal so may the seller take more or not in the case described when the buyer pays the price of the car after 20 years he is obliged to pay 45 000 and no more the seller cannot take a larger amount this is because currency is conventional money and is fungible so any rise or fall in its value is not taken into account consider what al durr al mukht r together with fat w al sh m states

voluntary charity given by a person who is in debt can a man who is in debt give voluntary charity or not will he be rewarded for giving charity or will he be sinful voluntary charity stands at the level of an optional act while a debt stands at the level of an obligation so the obligation should be discharged first yes if a man who is in debt is also seeing to the repayment of his debt and gives voluntary charity alongside it he will be rewarded for that charity consider what umdat al q r states

paying back more than the amount of the loan is it permissible to give more than the loan at the time of repaying it or not where the extra amount is not stipulated in the contract but something extra happens to be given when the loan is repaid what is the ruling on that in the case described if something extra happens to be given at the time of repaying a loan and the extra is neither stipulated in the contract nor so customary that it is expected and no displeasure is shown when it is not given then it is correct otherwise it is not permissible consider this narration in tirmidh shar f

whether a deferred debt falls due at once when the debtor dies if a debtor passes away and the debt was deferred does it become due at once or not that is to say a man took a loan in order to buy some goods and it was agreed that this debt would be paid off by instalments over one or two years what we wish to know is whether after this man's death this loan must be paid immediately or whether it may be paid off gradually by instalments within the agreed time according to the hanafi school stating a term in a loan does not make that term binding the reason is that a loan is an act of generosity and a favour and there is no compulsion in an act of generosity so the lender may call in his loan whenever he wishes the term does have the standing of a promise and keeping a promise is binding as a matter of conscience so the debtor should be given time but once the debtor has died his wealth passes to the heirs and the debt must be paid before the estate is distributed on this basis a deferred debt becomes due at once and immediate payment becomes necessary yes if everyone agrees to deferment and payment by instalments

recovering one's debt by a stratagem or device if a man is owed a debt and the debtor refuses to pay it may the creditor recover his debt by some other means or by a stratagem or device or not the actual position of the hanafis is that recovering the debt by some other means is not correct in our own times however the fatwa is that there is room for recovering the debt by another means as well consider what fat w sh m states

recovering one's debt from an insurance company a man borrowed money from someone and is now unable to repay it and he has since died but he had life insurance can the creditor recover his debt from the insurance company or not in the case described the creditor should recover his debt from the deceased's original capital and the further interest money should be given away in charity to the poor and the needy with no intention of reward it is not permissible or correct to put it to his own use if the original capital does not cover the debt in full and the deceased left no other wealth then he may take the interest money towards his debt after carrying out the device of transferring ownership consider what kit b al fat w states taking out insurance is not permissible of the money the insurance company pays out the portion that the policy holder himself paid in is lawful the amount over and above that f

taking unlawfully acquired wealth from a non muslim in settlement of a debt if a non muslim owes a debt to a muslim and it is known that the non muslim has money that comes from interest or from usurpation or from theft is it permissible to take it from him against the debt or not from the statements of the jurists it appears that the non muslim's ownership of such unlawful wealth is established and so a muslim may recover his debt from it consider all mah al sh m may allah have mercy on him says al fat w al hindiyyah states al ba r al r iq states

taking an interest bearing loan to pay tuition fees if a wealthy man takes a loan out of interest money in order to pay his son's university fees is this permissible or not if taking a loan out of interest bearing wealth means that he takes a loan from a bank and will pay interest on it then this is not correct because a university education is not obligatory nor is it so pressing a necessity that something impermissible should be committed for its sake if on the other hand what is meant is that someone has interest money lying with him and the father takes that very interest money as a loan for his son while both father and son are wealthy then the interest money must be given away in charity immediately it is not correct to circulate it in loans yes if the son is poor and does not own the nis b the threshold of zakatable wealth and the interest

recovering a debt from a muslim out of unlawful wealth zayd is owed some money by amr zayd knows for certain that amr will pay his debt out of interest money in this case is it permissible for me to recover my debt out of interest money a muslim cannot become the owner of interest money interest money must be given away in charity at once it is therefore not permissible to use it to pay off a muslim's debt either and it is likewise impermissible for the creditor to take interest money towards his debt consider what al sh m states al durr al mukht r states

taking a minor child's wealth as a loan a man wishes to take his minor child's wealth as a loan is he permitted to do so in the sharia or not a man may take his minor child's wealth as a loan for his own use he may not lend it to anyone else consider what fat w lamg r states al sh m states

who bears the costs of processing a loan are the costs of the paperwork for taking a loan borne by the creditor or by the debtor the underlying principle here is need whoever has the need pays the cost looked at in this way the debtor's need is obvious although in one respect the creditor has a need too namely that his loan should be recovered the greater need however lies with the debtor and for that reason the cost of the paperwork should be borne by the debtor consider what al hid yah states

taking an interest bearing loan in order to avoid income tax may one take an interest bearing loan in order to avoid income tax given that the government levies less tax on those who carry larger debts in the case described the preferable and better course is certainly to keep away from every interest based dealing but if the government levies income tax unjustly at a very high rate then in a time of need there should be room for an interest bearing loan in order to ward off the harm the jurists have permitted even the giving of a bribe in order to ward off harm consider what jad d fiqh mab ith states under the heading the ruling on paying a bribe or interest in order to avoid income tax and to buy costly goods answer this arrangement is beyond doubt permissible because there is a benefit for the muslim in it as well as the warding off of harm even on the view of those who

paying a deceased person's debt out of a pension fund is it permissible to pay a deceased person's debt out of the money received from a pension fund or not the money that is received from a pension fund may be used and it is permissible and correct to pay the deceased's debt and other such dues out of it consider what kif yat al muft states the pension that an employee receives when he retires from service is permissible

a loan on which interest is charged if payment is late suppose a man took a loan from a company on the terms that if he does not repay it within three months interest will be charged on it thereafter and the borrower intends to repay within three months what is the ruling on taking loans of this kind will the borrower be sinful or not if the borrower is firmly resolved to repay within three months there will be room for it but it is preferable and better to keep away from contracts of this kind the company's stipulation that if the loan is not repaid within three months a certain percentage will be charged over and above it is an interest based dealing a loan however is not rendered invalid by an invalid condition consider what al ba r al r iq states

taking a loan in order to live in luxury may a loan be taken with no real need merely to raise one's standard of living and to live in luxury or not permission to take a loan is given at the level of genuine compulsion one should keep away from taking a loan merely for the sake of luxury consider what isl m fiqh states the sharia has permitted the taking of a loan in cases of severe financial need or to protect one's honour and good name now if a man takes a loan for extravagance and luxury or to keep up the standing that people credit him with and an artificial standard of living or if he does take a loan out of genuine need but then gives no thought to repaying it or keeps putting it off even though he is able to pay such a man is a wrongdoer both morally and in law that is to say he will be called to account in the here

exchanging a loan of wheat for rands if a man owes ten kilos of wheat as a loan and the debtor says to the creditor after 5 days i will give 10 rands in place of the wheat is this arrangement valid or not in the case described once the wheat is being exchanged for ten rands the ten rands must be handed over at once otherwise the two will have parted while a debt still stands with no countervalue taken in exchange and that is impermissible consider what al sh m states bihisht zewar states you took a loan of two seers of wheat or flour or something

making gold the standard for repaying a loan a man gave another fifteen thousand rands as a loan and said at present this is worth one ounce of gold when you repay the loan return one ounce of gold with the turn of the times after two years fifteen thousand rands buys only half an ounce of gold what we wish to know is this is he obliged to hand over one ounce of gold or will he pay only fifteen thousand rands and if he refuses to hand over the gold can he be compelled to do so or not the jurists have laid down that for a loan to be permissible the thing lent must be fungible and what this means is precisely that its equivalent is to be paid back if a condition is laid down that something of a different kind be paid then although this is a loan in form in reality it is not a loan but an exchange the ruling on it is that paper notes that is the currency in circulation are not money by their very nature but money by convention so the rules of a currency exchange do not apply to trading in them on this basis the condition of returning one ounce is valid and this transaction is permissible on a deferred basis possession must however be taken of one of the two

tying a loan to the purchasing power of the currency kh lid gave bakr ten thousand rands as a loan and laid down the condition that when he repays it after two years he will pay extra to cover whatever fall has taken place in the ten thousand that is for example if after two years the purchasing power has fallen so that ten thousand has become twelve thousand will he be obliged to pay twelve thousand in the present age currency has the ruling of an independent conventional money it is not tied to any silver or gold and since it has the ruling of an independent money no rise or fall in it is taken into account for as long as it remains in circulation unless the currency is withdrawn altogether which is another matter so after two years kh lid may recover from bakr only the ten thousand that he gave he has no right to recover more than that to do so resembles interest and is not correct consider what fat w q kh n states

stipulating that better goods be returned for a loan zayd gave amr ten kilos of ordinary grade wheat as a loan and told him when you return the loan after a month you will give fine top grade wheat is this arrangement permissible or not when goods subject to the rules of interest are exchanged for one another payment on the spot and equality are required and superior or inferior quality is not taken into account the loan transaction however is an exception to this and it is for that very reason that the sharia has declared it permissible even though it is deferred even so likeness is binding and necessary in a loan too so equality in quantity and in quality is required at the time of repayment stipulating in a loan that better goods be returned amounts to obtaining a benefit and that is impermissible consider what al ba r al r iq states

a financial penalty for delay in repaying a loan in volume four you wrote that some scholars regard a financial penalty as permissible and a good deal of evidence for it was set out what i now wish to ask is this if a debtor or borrower keeps putting off the repayment of a loan and he owes one hundred thousand and the term of the loan expired on the first of december may a financial penalty be imposed on him because of the delay in repaying the loan or not for instance he would have to pay two thousand for a delay of two months and three thousand for a delay of three months is this arrangement permissible or not this arrangement is entirely impermissible it is not permissible to take one hundred and two thousand in place of a loan of one hundred thousand this is what is called the interest spoken of in the qur'an in which the debt and the loan grow as the term is extended that is to say imposing a penalty on a loan is impermissible there is however a difference of opinion among the scholars about imposing a penalty for some improper act in the view of one group such a penalty is valid the details of this have already been given in fat w d r al ul m zakariyy volume four selling the term itself and taking a price for it is impermissible as well

recovering a debt from the person holding the debtor's deposit zayd owes umar a debt and zayd is not paying it even though he is able to in the shop of zayd the debtor there is an employee and there is also zayd's son do this employee or the son have the right to hand over to umar the creditor from zayd's shop some article or sum of money up to the amount of the debt or less umar may himself recover the amount of the debt or less than it from zayd or from the person holding zayd's deposit but zayd's employee and his son do not have the right to give anything to the creditor or lender out of the wealth of the real owner that is the debtor consider the author of al hid yah says shar al majallah states

a debtor referring his creditor to a third party bakr owes money to kh lid and kh lid in turn owes money to umar kh lid said to umar do not take the debt from me take it from bakr who is my debtor bakr accepted this now umar says that he will recover his debt from kh lid while kh lid refuses to pay and says that umar had already agreed to recover it from bakr is kh lid's refusal correct or not in short if a debtor transfers his debt to his own debtor may the creditor still claim from the debtor or not when a debtor refers his creditor to some third party and that third party accepts the creditor can no longer make a claim against his own debtor so in the case in question umar will recover from bakr the debtor of his debtor who is the third party and will not make a claim against kh lid the exception is where the money is lost in which case he may claim from the debtor for example if the third party dies leaving no property or goods or if he denies the transfer and there is no witness to it consider what the author of al hid yah says

taking back a loaned item before the agreed term ends if a person gave someone else a piece of land on loan for three years so that he could plant his saplings trees and the like on it and then after one year wants the land back while the borrower says that this will cause him a loss what should be done will the owner be liable for compensation once the saplings have been uprooted or not and if so how much in the case in question the lender does have the right to have his land vacated even before the term ends but to do so is disliked he will however be responsible for whatever loss the borrower suffers through the land being vacated early and he will pay compensation for it that is the lender gave the land for three years so that an orchard could be planted on it and now wants it back after only one year the borrower will be told to cut down his orchard and vacate the land now if the orchard had stood for three years its value would have been say five thousand rand whereas at the time it is being cleared its value is say two thousand rand so the lender will pay the borrower th

taking back a house given on loan for use a man gave a house to be used as a place of worship and the congregation began praying in it a charitable person taking it to be a place of worship had a room built in it later the congregation built their own mosque and the owner of the house sold it now the charitable person who had the room built is asking for the value of the room so that he may put the money towards some other good cause what is the ruling of the sacred law in the case in question the owner of the house had given his house on loan for use as a place of worship and no term had been fixed the owner may therefore take his house back whenever he wishes and the man who built the room will be told to pull it down and clear the house if pulling it down causes no damage to the house the lender cannot stop the builder of the room from pulling it down if however there is a risk of damage to the house or the land then the lender has the choice he may let the room stand and pay the value of the materials as demolished or if he prefers he may order it to be pulled down in short since in the case in question the lender has sold the house he
