taking back loaned land before the agreed term zayd gave amr a piece of land on loan so that he could build a house on it telling him that he could use it for twenty years amr built a house of unbaked brick after three years zayd fell out with amr and now wants to turn him out while amr regards this as a betrayal if amr now pulls his house down can he recover the loss from zayd or not amr can recover the loss from zayd suppose the building as it stands is worth twenty thousand and after demolition the rubble is worth ten thousand the difference between the two is ten thousand and amr may recover that ten thousand from zayd if however the land had been given for sowing a crop and it was asked for back before the appointed time then the crop would be left standing until it ripened and zayd could recover from amr the rent for the days between the demand and the ripening so it is stated in the books of fiqh

the borrower's liability for compensation one student took another student's mobile phone with his permission in order to use it that same night he came to return it but the owner of the phone was asleep the next day there was a search at the madrasah and the phone was destroyed now the lender is demanding the price of his phone from the borrower what is the ruling of the sacred law must its price be paid or not the ruling of the sacred law concerning a borrowed article is that for as long as it remains with the borrower it is a trust carrying no liability that is the borrower must look after it in the same way that a trust is looked after but if the article happens to break or be spoiled no responsibility falls on him in other words he bears no liability for compensation where the article was accidentally spoiled or broken if however he used it improperly or handed it over to irresponsible people and it was destroyed or he deliberately spoiled or broke it then in all these cases the borrower is liable to pay compensation now examining the case above in the light of this ruling it ap

making good damage to a borrowed article zayd borrowed amr's car to use while it was in use some damage was caused is zayd obliged to make good the damage or not and will it make any difference whether the damage was done deliberately or without intent further what is the ruling if the damage occurred because he drove faster than the set limit in the case in question if zayd used the car in the customary manner and some damage occurred without any transgression on his part then zayd is not responsible for it and no compensation is due from him if however he went beyond the customary manner and transgressed then zayd is responsible for it likewise if he drove faster than the set speed and broke the law and some damage occurred compensation will again be due from zayd al fat w al hindiyyah states

renting out a house held on loan bakr gave kh lid a house on loan to live in kh lid divided the house into two parts he lives in one part himself and has let out the other from which he collects a monthly rent is it permissible to do this or not and who is entitled to the rent in the case in question it is not permissible for kh lid to let out the borrowed house without permission such a lease is not valid and the rent must be given away in charity if however bakr has given permission for it to be let out then it is permissible and valid consider what al fat w al hindiyyah states the majallah states taby

liability of a depositary who is paid for safekeeping amr left a valuable article of his with bakr as a deposit and also pays him a monthly fee for looking after it as it happened the valuable article was destroyed while in bakr's keeping because the house was flooded amr is now demanding the article or its value will bakr be responsible for it in the sacred law or not that is is a paid depositary liable to make good the loss or not it is permissible and valid in the sacred law to make the safekeeping of a deposit or trust binding upon the depositary and to fix a fee in return for it in that case however if the deposit is destroyed in the depositary's keeping in a way that could have been guarded against the paid depositary is liable otherwise not so in the case in question if bakr was not remiss in looking after it but had put it in a safe place and it was destroyed then no liability falls on bakr but if bakr was remiss in looking after it he is liable consider what al fat w al hindiyyah states

putting money held in trust into a business zayd left one hundred thousand rand with amr as a trust after a few days the depositary amr put it into his own business and within a year earned a further two hundred thousand rand from it now it is obvious that amr must pay the hundred thousand back to zayd what needs to be established is whether the profit earned belongs to amr or to zayd amr traded for himself without permission not on zayd's behalf and must this profit be given away in charity or not if amr concluded the transaction upon the trust money itself and paid over that very money then the whole of the profit he earned must be given away in charity if he concluded the transaction upon that money but paid over other money or concluded the transaction upon money in unspecified terms and then paid over the trust money then in these cases the profit earned need not be given away in charity and there is scope for him to put it to his own use some scholars however hold that the profit must be given away in charity even where the transaction was concluded upon unspecified money so the more cautious course is to give it away consider what all mah al sarakhs may allah have

liability when money held in trust is found to be short kh lid asked bakr to keep some money for him as a trust bakr refused but when kh lid insisted he put the money away in a safe place a good many days later kh lid asked for the money back and bakr took it out and handed it over to him when kh lid looked at it it appeared to be somewhat short bakr says that he never laid a hand on the money who is responsible now the ruling on a trust is that if it becomes short or is lost without any heedlessness or slackness on the trustee's part then no responsibility rests upon him but if he was remiss or overstepped the mark that is if he was slack in safeguarding the money or took some step contrary to the depositor's instructions or used it without the depositor's permission then in all these cases he will have to pay compensation so in the case in question if bakr is truthful in his statement and the trust was not moved from where it had been placed and kh lid was content for the trust to be kept there then bakr is not responsible for it a noble hadith states that the messenger of allah said

liability when charitable funds are confiscated a man has for a long time been running charitable work in another country india for example while he himself lives in england or africa many people give him zak h lill h and other funds and some place certain sums with him as a trust before travelling to that other country india he sends the funds across from england or africa a friend who assists him receives these funds in india and puts them away in a safe place in his house this is done purely for safekeeping a few weeks ago the police acting on some suspicion searched his house in india arrested his assistant and confiscated all the funds what is the ruling now is the sender of the money responsible for these funds o when a trust is placed with someone the ruling of the sacred law is that the trustee must safeguard it as far as he is able therefore if it perishes or is lost without any excess heedlessness slackness or laziness on his part no compensation falls upon him but if the depositary was remiss in safeguarding it was heedless and overstepped the mark then he is liable for it similarly if a person appoints someone as his agent to deliver something the ruling for that agent is the same as for a trustee if the property perishes or is lost in the agent's hands without any shortcoming on his part no liability falls on him either consider what al durr al mukht r states

not paying the government the full amount of tax very often traders collect tax from their customers but do not pay the full amount over to the government is this tax a trust is it necessary to hand it over or not when traders collect it from their customers they are acting as agents of the government and the tax money is in their hands as a trust it is necessary and obligatory to pay it to the government otherwise it will be a breach of trust allah most high says al fat w al hindiyyah states

giving conditional permission for an atm to be installed a muslim runs a petrol station the land belongs to the petrol company itself and he has taken it on rent a bank wishes to install an atm machine at this petrol station a machine into which people pay money and from which they draw money the bank has laid down the condition that for the first three thousand people who use it each month this muslim will receive nothing but that after three thousand he will receive 75 cents for every use whether money is paid in or drawn out is it permissible to enter into such an arrangement or not a contract of this kind appears to be sound and valid on two grounds 1 it is a conditional gratuity that is attaching a condition to an act of kindness granting free use up to three thousand is a gratuity and making it conditional upon a lease so that the bank pays for the excess turns it into a conditional gratuity on this ground the contract is permissible and valid 2 it is a contract of hire in which a condition has been stipulated but because of custom and because it does not lead to dispute this condition does not invalidate the contract consider what al hid yah states fuller detai

prizes offered to the purchasers of a monthly magazine reader's digest is a monthly magazine which people buy by paying in advance a draw is held among them and whoever's name comes out receives a prize is this practice permissible or not and is it permissible to accept the prize when one's name comes out if the digest was bought for a price and the managers of the digest said that they would give such and such an item as a prize to whoever's name came out then there is no objection to it in the sacred law indeed it belongs to the category of a conditional gratuity that is we shall confer a favour upon those who buy the digest which is then made conditional upon the draw just as a student is granted admission on condition of paying the fee no gambling is present in this draw because in a gambling draw one person who has a right is deprived and another becomes entitled to the money whereas here nobody has a right to anything in return for their money they are entitled to the dige

making an invitation to a meal conditional upon a donation in some institutions it happens that when money is needed and expenses have grown heavy they hold a public dinner collect an additional sum from those who attend and put whatever is left over towards the expenses of their institution is it correct to take this additional sum and spend it on their own work or not the dinner is in essence a gratuity on the part of the institution and the condition of an additional payment has been attached to it without any compulsion whoever does not accept the condition has the option of not attending this arrangement therefore falls under the ruling of a conditional gratuity and is permissible and valid the references have already been given above repeating them would only make this longer

conditional gifts at a wedding feast at wedding feasts and other such gatherings it is the custom for people to collect gifts and at the end of the function the hosts go through all the gifts and write them down their purpose in doing so is that when there is a function at the giver's house they will have to give the same amount and those who give gifts have it in mind that when their own turn comes they too should receive a gift of the same value is it permissible to give and receive gifts in this way or not this is a conditional gratuity and when what is given by the other side falls short in quantity or is of poor quality it sometimes gives rise to ill feeling and backbiting for poor people this custom is a millstone round their necks and it is therefore necessary to keep away from it in the noble qur'an allah most high says tafs r uthm n states some commentators have explained the meaning of the verse thus when a man gives something to another with the object that the other will repay the favour with something greater then such giving brings no blessing or reward in the sight of allah most high although

a question concerning the conditional gratuity airlines announce that whoever travels a great deal on their aircraft and accumulates a certain number of miles will be given a free ticket or some other concession is it permissible in the sacred law to accept this or not this comes under the ruling of a conditional gratuity and is permissible and valid just as madrasahs make their fees and contributions conditional upon admission a practice which a rat mawl n afar a mad th naw may allah have mercy on him declared permissible the details have already been given above and may be consulted there section two an exposition of the rulings on gifts

the ruling on gifting an undivided share zayd being of sound mind and in full possession of his senses gifted his land to his four brothers and the land is in those brothers' possession but it was not divided up and given to them separately zayd has since died and now zayd's sisters are claiming a share of inheritance in this land is their claim valid or not the jurists generally write that in the view of im m ab an fah may allah have mercy on him the gift of an undivided share is not valid unless it is divided up and handed over the gift of an undivided share means gifting a portion of a whole this ruling is stated plainly in the standard books of fiqh and needs no reference in our own day however the question calls for fresh consideration because gifting an undivided share has become the general custom and under systems of law other than the islamic law such a gift is regarded as valid and complete on this basis the jurists have written that when the general custom runs contrary to an explicit text of the jurists general custom an

taking possession in a gift made to a minor child respected muft ib my father passed away a short while ago seven months before his death he said whatever i own here in africa belongs to my younger son usayn the witnesses to this statement are myself my brother in law abdull h and my wife what needs to be established is whether the gift is thereby complete given that apart from this no paperwork of any kind was done please note that we the remaining brothers and sisters have no objection to it in the case in question your father's words whatever i own here in africa belongs to my younger son usayn constitute a gift it should be borne in mind that a father's gift of something to his young under age son is completed by the contract alone that is there is no need for possession to be taken or for any other paperwork because the father is himself the guardian of his under age children so that the father's possession is the possession of his under age children on this basis the gift is complete consider what bad i al an i states

making a gift contingent upon a condition is a gift made contingent upon a condition valid or not for example someone says if i am married this month then this book is a present for you in the case in question a gift made contingent upon a condition is void and not valid consider what al durr al mukht r states al ba r al r iq states shiyat al a w states al fat w al

gifting something that has been lost a man's watch went missing he said to zayd if you find the missing watch it is yours zayd searched for the watch and found it and now the owner of the watch regrets what he said has the watch become zayd's property or not in the case in question zayd's ownership of the watch is not established it remains as before the property of its owner consider what fat w q kh n states al fat w al sir jiyyah states

taking away the blanket provided on an aeroplane is it correct to take away the blanket that is provided for use on an aeroplane if the air hostess gives permission or not it is not correct to take an aeroplane's blanket with the stewardess's permission because she is not the owner of that blanket the real owner is someone else moreover it is written on it that it is to be returned after use consider what al fat w al hindiyyah states

giving a qur'an as a present to a non muslim may one give a qur'an as a present to a non muslim or not if the non muslim has reverence for the noble qur'an in his heart and one is satisfied that there will be no disrespect or irreverence on his part then it is permissible and correct to give him the noble qur'an as a present it may well be that he will be granted guidance through it but if there is any fear of the opposite then it is not permissible to give it consider what a muslim records naf al muft wa al s il states

gifting a pigskin jacket to a non muslim a man bought a jacket and afterwards learned that it was made of pigskin may he give it as a gift to a non muslim or not the pig together with all its parts is intrinsically impure and it is not permissible to use any part of it a pigskin jacket is therefore forbidden to a muslim and the ruling is that he should return it and take back his money if for some reason it cannot be returned then he should give it to a non muslim without any intention of earning reward since it is not correct to give unlawful property as a gift to a muslim consider what fat w bayyin t states question among the shoes and leather goods coming into our country from china spain and other countries pigskin is being used some shoes are made of rexine but are lined with pigskin and some are made entirely of pigskin is it

charity and gifts where possession has not been handed over a man keeps a small box in his house in which he goes on putting money set aside for the sake of allah if he wishes to perform his obligatory or voluntary sacrifice with this money may he do so or not in the case in question voluntary charity and gifts are not complete without possession being taken so for as long as possession has not been handed over it is correct for him to put the money to his own use and it will therefore also be permissible for him to perform an obligatory or a voluntary sacrifice with it consider what shar al majallah states taby n al aq iq states al fat w al hindiyyah states

completing a gift by taking possession of the title documents for the completion of a gift of land or a shop is taking possession of the documents sufficient or is it necessary to vacate the property and hand it over to the donee for the completion of a gift of immovable property taking possession of the documents is sufficient that is the gift becomes complete once possession of the documents has been taken consider what shiyat al a w states shar al majallah states

gifting an undivided share to a co owner on paper the shop is jointly owned by the wife and the husband the husband said in front of a good many people i have given this shop to my wife and the wife is in possession of it the husband also goes to the shop but he does more of the outside work has the wife become the owner of this shop or not in the case described the husband's saying i have given this shop to my wife is a gift and possession was already the wife's the gift is therefore complete and the wife has become the owner of the shop whoever's name may be on the papers the gift as recognised by the sharia is not affected by that further since a shop is for the most part like a thing that does not admit of division it is valid to gift it without dividing it see what fat w q kh n says

giving away small children's old belongings as a gift if a small child's clothes become old may they be given away in charity or not or should one put a price on them keep that amount for the child and give the clothes away in charity on one's own behalf whatever items are bought for children in such a way that ownership is transferred to them belong to the children so it is not valid to give charity gifts and the like on the children's behalf yes one may put a suitable price on them and set that amount aside for the children and after that it will be permissible to give those items away as a gift on one's own behalf if by local custom such items are given only as a loan then they may be passed on to others see what fat w q kh n says

giving away a trifling item as a gift on a child's behalf if these items have no particular value may those clothes be given away so that the reward may be conveyed to the child or not will any particular benefit be taken into account here or not for instance placing the child in the service of a teacher is a benefit the pure sharia has by no means disregarded the interests of children on the contrary it has given their interests and their benefit precedence it is for this reason that it has not allowed a guardian to make gratuitous dispositions of a child's belongings since that involves loss to the child but if there are items in the children's ownership that have no particular value then there is no great harm in giving them in charity or for the conveying of reward so long as it is for the child's own benefit yes if an item has a fair value then it is not valid to give it away without compensation see what j mi a k m al igh r says

giving away a tin of milk as a gift a man bought a tin of milk for his small child if the child now has no need of this milk may he give this tin to some other child or not according to the statement of the jurists it is permissible for the parents to eat foodstuffs that the child has received as a gift therefore it will also be permissible to give to someone else those foodstuffs that the child no longer needs see what j mi a k m al igh r says

spending a child's money on his own expenses someone or the father himself gave a sum of money as a gift to a man's minor son may clothes and the like be bought for the child out of this money or not is the father to bear the child's expenses himself in the case described when the child has money of his own the father may meet the child's expenses out of that money but the father may not spend the child's money on extravagances great care is needed where children's property is concerned see what al durr al mukht r says

accepting a gift from a minor child may a teacher accept a gift from a minor child or not if something is given to children for their use it is permissible to pass it on to others with the parents' permission on this basis it will also be permissible for the teacher to accept it see what imd d al muft n says the presents that boys give are permissible on two conditions the first is that if the boys are themselves of age they should give of their own free will and if they are minors then it is a condition that their parents be willing the parents being willing means that the property is the parents' the second is that the teacher should not adopt a manner that gives the students the impression that if they do not give a present they will come to some harm imd d al m

a father gifting a shop to his son a father gifted a shop to his son the father does not conduct business in it only the son does though the father comes and sits at the shop every day the accounts and all the other affairs are handled by the son alone has the son taken possession in the eyes of the sharia or not and if the father also conducts business in it what is the ruling then in the case described if the father gifted the shop to the son and also handed over possession of it then the shop has come into the son's ownership even if after taking possession the father sits there occasionally or all the time but if the father made the gift while keeping the shop in his own possession then it has not come into the son's ownership the shop will remain the father's property as before see what al durr al mukht r says

a merely verbal gift without transfer of possession a father said to his daughter i have given you this house but the house was not registered in the daughter's name the parents lived in this house and bore all its expenses the daughter and the parents all took it that the house belonged to the daughter now after the death of the parents the other heirs are demanding their right in this house while the daughter claims that her parents gifted the house to her please tell us who is the rightful owner of the house in the case described the father gifted the house to the daughter only verbally and during his lifetime he did not give her possession of it as owner the gift was therefore not valid and the house will be divided among all the heirs according to the shares laid down by the sharia see what fat w hindiyyah says fat w ra miyyah states for a gift to be complete and valid complete possession is a condition al durr al mukht r says so since the deceased himse

giving gifts on the day of sh r what do the scholars of religion and the muftis of the firm sharia say about the following matters 1 what is the ruling on giving one another gifts on the day of sh r 2 what of the members of a family gathering together on the day of sh r 3 is it correct or not to offer congratulations on the occasion of sh r purely out of joy these days it is common to send messages by mobile phone what is the ruling on that the rule of the pure sharia is that where an act is not regarded as a sunnah or as recommended it is enough that its basis be established and that it not clash with the principles accepted in the sharia in that case there will be room for doing it there are many examples of this in the pure sharia for instance for an amulet or for reciting and blowing over someone a general proof is enough and no specific proof is required on this basis giving a gift on the day of sh r as an expression of joy affection and love is in order provided it is not regarded as necessary or as a sunnah but where it is regarded as necessary and those who do not give are reproached there it is not in o

gifts on non islamic festive occasions what is the ruling on giving and receiving presents on the occasion of christmas and other non islamic festivals may they be given to such people for the sake of business relations or not for they too give us presents on our islamic occasions and in giving to them the aim is to maintain relations not to honour their religion what is the ruling in the case described if the aim is not to honour their religion but merely to keep up an outward friendship or outward relations then there is room for exchanging presents it is better however not to give on the day of christmas itself but a little before or after it all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him says in imd d al fat w mawl n th nw may allah have mercy on him after quoting passages from the books of fiqh writes from these reports the details of the rulings on the gift exchanges asked about have become clear that if ther

depositing money in the bank in a son's name and whether it is a gift a man deposited some of his money in the bank in his son's name in order to avoid tax now because it stands in the son's name will the son be regarded as its owner or not in the case described if the purpose of depositing it in the bank was not to make the son its owner but it was deposited that way for some practical reason then the son has not become the owner yes if the transfer of ownership was intended then the son has become the owner see what muft mu ammad shaf may allah have mercy on him says if zayd had in fact not made this house his wife's property but had had her name entered in the government papers for some practical reason then this house did not become the wife's property and after her death her heirs will have no right in it rather it will remain zayd's property as before a person's name being entered in the government paper

a mother gifting a house to her son my mother gave me a house that is in india at a time when she was alive and in good health my mother has now passed away so what is the ruling regarding the house my sister is alive does she have a share in this house or not in the case described if your mother gifted the house to you and handed over possession of it or handed over possession to an agent of yours then this house is yours and no one else has a share in it see what lamg r says shar al majallah states

a creditor gifting his debt to someone other than the debtor zayd was owed a debt of five thousand rand by umar zayd the creditor was on friendly terms with bakr and he told umar the debtor not to pay that debt to him but to give it to bakr i have gifted it to him and he told bakr you take it so umar gave it to bakr later relations between bakr and zayd the creditor broke down and now he says return the five thousand to me bakr has already spent the money since zayd and umar are both scholars zayd has put forward as his evidence the ruling of fiqh what should umar do now in the case described when the creditor told the debtor to give his debt to bakr and umar gave it to bakr this gift became complete and zayd's debt was also discharged zayd can no longer make any claim against umar as for transferring ownership of a debt to someone other than the debtor when the creditor himself gives permission to the one who is not the debtor it is valid and the gift is completed see what fat al qad r says al in yah shar al hid yah states

dividing one's property during one's lifetime may a person divide his wealth property and so forth during his own lifetime or not dividing one's property during one's own lifetime is a gift and it is valid according to the view on which the fatwa is given equality should be kept in mind among the children though some disparity is also workable but it is not right to cause anyone harm without reason yes differentiating on the ground of religious commitment or of open sinfulness is permissible indeed giving somewhat more to a religious god fearing child who abides by the sharia is better and preferable see what khul at al fat w says

equality between children at the time of distribution in ordinary circumstances equality should be kept in view when distributing property among children but equality is not obligatory it is simply better and preferable the commentator on the majallah al aydar may allah have mercy on him however has said that equality is obligatory what does this mean see shar al majallah vol 2 p 433 mawl n kh lid sayf all h has likewise written that it is obligatory the hanafi position on which the fatwa is given is that in ordinary circumstances equality and parity among children at the time of distribution is better and preferable not obligatory yes if a person wishes to cause loss to some of them for no reason then equality becomes binding see what fat w hindiyyah says i l al sunan sta

a gift without transfer of possession a man died in 2006 he had written in a will that after his death his estate should be divided among his heirs in accordance with the sharia nine months after this man's death one of his sons ya y laid claim to a piece of land in the estate saying that his father had gifted this land to him during his lifetime on 2 march 2004 in proof of his claim he produced a document in which the gift is expressly set out and on this document are the signatures of ya y 's son mu ammad and of a non muslim african woman apart from these there is no other witness furthermore ya y had not taken possession of this land nor had he had it registered in his name and beyond that the other heirs know in the case described the gift was not completed the reason is that for a gift to be complete the taking of possession is necessary and possession did not take place a second reason is that the testimony of the witnesses whose signatures appear on the written agreement is also not acceptable since a son's testimony in favour of his father is not acceptable and likewise a non muslim's testimony against a muslim is not accepted on this basis the land left behind did not enter ya y 's ownership and it will therefore be divided among all the heirs according to the shares laid down by the sharia al durr al mukht r states

gifting a share of an inheritance before taking possession of it a man died and left in his estate a house that was still undivided one of the heirs gifted his share to his sister that man has now died and the other heirs do not accept this gift even though the woman to whom the gift was made has witnesses is the gift valid or not in the case described it is permissible for an heir before taking possession of his inheritance to waive his right or to transfer it to someone else moreover houses here nowadays are like undivided property that does not admit of division so a person may gift his share in one without dividing it and since witnesses are present the gift in question has been completed and the other heirs now have no right in that share see what al ashb h wa'l na ir says fat w sh m states

gifting rights is it correct to make a gift of rights or not rights that are established in their own right are transferable and are regarded as firmly established and a gift can operate in them whereas rights that are established merely to ward off harm are not transferable the right of inheritance and the right of ownership are regarded as firm rights and transfer takes place in them a gift of them will therefore also be valid see what the author of al in yah all mah akmal al d n al b bart may allah have mercy on him writes

gifts exchanged in a love affair if a man is in love with a girl and sends her presents is it correct for her to accept them or not and if the young man later repents of the affair is it correct for him to take those presents back presenting gifts to one another in an illicit relationship comes under the ruling of a bribe accepting them is not correct ownership is not established by them and the giver retains the right to ask for them back yes if after repenting he gives up his demand and forgives it there is no harm in that see what all mah ibn nujaym al mi r may allah have mercy on him says lamg r states

using a gift received in a love affair a girl gave one of our friends a mobile phone in a love affair and later the relationship came to an end the young man now wants to sell the phone may he use the money himself or is it necessary for him to give it away in charity in the case described since a gift given in a love affair comes under the ruling of a bribe it did not enter the young man's ownership it is therefore necessary to return it to the girl who gave it selling it is not correct but if he has sold it he should convey the price to that girl unless she forgives him and gives up her claim see what fat w sh m says

sending a gift with a view to marriage if a young man loves a girl and there is no illicit relationship but he sends a gift to her family so that the girl or her family may agree to the marriage will this too come under the ruling of a bribe or will it be permissible to do in the case described since there is no illicit relationship this gift is a way of winning affection and it is therefore permissible to accept it just as giving a gift or charity to those whose hearts are to be reconciled al mu allafah qul buhum was for the attainment of a religious purpose here too marriage is a religious purpose and this is a means of attaining it

customary possession is enough in a gift my father gifted me a building and it was put in my name in the papers there are two houses and four shops in this building and tenants are living in them during my father's lifetime i collect their rent and the matter of taxes and so on is also my responsibility that is i am the one who deals with the property in the situation described is my possession enough for the gift to be complete or is outward possession necessary by evicting the tenants it is obvious that under the tenancy agreement there is no way of evicting the tenants possession of anything is according to what suits that thing possession of a car is that the key be handed over to the buyer in this case possession will be effected by handing over the papers to the person to whom the gift is made and after the father's death the other heirs cannot claim any right of inheritance in this building see what radd al mu t r says jad d fiqh mab ith states the qur'an and the sunnah h

accepting a gift out of unlawful wealth if interest money comes into the hands of a non muslim does it enter his ownership or not if a non muslim presents a gift out of interest money to a muslim is the muslim permitted to accept it or not and what is the ruling if a muslim gives a gift out of interest money if interest money comes to a muslim the muslim does not become its owner on the contrary he must return it if the owner of the money is known it should be given back to him and if the owner is not known it should be given away in charity without any intention of earning reward it should be given away in charity in the sense of freeing oneself from a burden and a calamity this money may then be given permissibly and correctly to a deserving poor or needy person who does not possess the zakat threshold but accepting a gift out of interest money is not permissible or correct see what all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him says

a device for validly gifting a house that is full of the donor's belongings zayd has a large house consisting of twelve rooms and the house is full of belongings a large library a freezer a fridge several heavy machines exercise equipment a bed carpets kitchen equipment and so on this man has three sons two of them have houses of their own while one has no house lives with his father serves his father and is a religious scholar zayd wishes to gift this house to that scholar son but he does not wish to give away the contents since he thinks it better that after his death the contents be divided among all the heirs and he wants to use them during his lifetime zayd is himself a religious scholar and knows that to gift a house it is necessary to hand zayd is right that in order to hand over possession the house will have to be emptied but the jurists have set down an easy device for this by which the matter becomes simple the device is that he should place all the contents of the house with the person to whom the gift is made as a deposit and hand them over to him for which clearing the way is enough and after that gift him the house and hand over possession of it as well that is give him the key of the house and himself move out the goods left on deposit can then be taken back whenever he wishes see what shaykh al aydar says in durar al ukk m shar majallat al a k m

the definition of hire and uncertainty about its term what is the definition of the contract of hire what is the ruling on uncertainty about the term in a contract of hire and what is the ruling if the contract of hire is made with a non muslim 1 the definition of hire hire is a transaction in which a specified consideration is given in exchange for a known benefit that is hire is the name of a transaction in which one party offers a benefit and the other offers compensation or a wage for example one party has a house and gives permission to live in it while the other pays rent for it this will be called a contract of hire 2 the ruling on t

renting for a hundred years if a person takes a house a shop or a piece of land on rent for a hundred years is this permissible or not there is a difference of opinion among the jurists about renting for a hundred years some jurists say that such a hire is not valid while others say that it is permissible and valid and this latter is the preferred view on that basis in the case in question it is permissible and valid to rent a shop a house or a piece of land for a hundred years see what all mah al sarakhs may allah have mercy on him says

hiring books out for a fee if a person takes books on hire in order to study them is this permissible or not all mah sh m and other scholars have said that taking books on hire is not permissible shaykh al isl m the chief justice all mah ab al asan al al saghd may allah have mercy on him d 461 ah however declared it permissible in on this basis if a man keeps the books at home or in his own custody the hire ought to be permissible since he is withholding someone else's property moreover in our time this is the accepted custom people do take books on hire and for this reason too it ought to be permissible see what al nutaf f al fat w states

the effect on a lease of the death of one of the contracting parties if a man takes a shop on hire for twenty years and in the meantime either the tenant or the owner of the property dies the lease comes to an end in the sharia though in law it remains in force now in the sharia after the death of the tenant the other party will demand that the lease be rescinded but the law prevents this what then is the way of keeping the lease in force in the eyes of the sharia in the case asked about if it is written into the twenty year lease that the transaction of hire will continue even if one of the two the owner of the property or the tenant dies then the long term lease will run until the fixed period expires even if one of them does die that is it will remain in force by virtue of the agreement al durr al mukht r states

responsibility for repairs to a rented house some people had taken a house on rent with the owner's permission the tenant made certain alterations to the house for example he shifted a doorway to another side and so on but it had also been settled beforehand that when the house was handed back the tenant would himself at his own expense have whatever alterations he had made put right in october they moved out of that house to another place but their belongings are still in the same house and the keys of the house are also with the tenant it had been agreed that the house would be handed back in december and it had been accepted that rent would be paid up to december a promise to put the house right had also been made in n assuming the question is accurate then in the case asked about 1 the tenant is obliged to put right all the alterations he made to the house because he undertook to do so and because he made these alterations for his own benefit the owner gains nothing by them apart from these repairs to the house and the like are not obligatory or necessary for the tenant the owner of the house is himself responsible for them 2 if the owner has the repairs carried out himself and asks for the cost only the cost of the alterations the tenant made will be due from him the cost of other repairs to the house mending the roof for instance is not due from the tenant he must pay the middling

a muslim engineer taking on the building of a bar if a muslim engineer accepts the work of designing and building a bar is this permissible or not the hanafi jurists differ on this question the two disciples may allah have mercy on them say that it involves helping in sin and that such employment should therefore be avoided while im m ab an fah may allah have mercy on him says that there is no sin in the work itself so it is permissible even so there is an aspect of caution in not doing it if a man has accepted such work however the wage will not be impermissible or unlawful see what al durr al mukht r states

working on the construction of a non muslim place of worship a buddhist place of worship is being built in a certain city if a muslim wishes to work on its construction may he do so or not and will the income be lawful or unlawful there is room for a muslim to work on the construction of a non muslim place of worship accordingly the wage and the income will not be unlawful or impermissible see what a w states al ba r al r iq states al mu al burh n states

a muslim barber cutting hair in a manner contrary to the sharia if a muslim barber cuts a muslim's hair in a manner contrary to the sharia or shaves his beard what is the ruling on that barber's earnings in the pure sharia it is necessary to keep a beard of a fist's length to cut it shorter than a fist or to have it cut are both sinful and impermissible in the eyes of the sharia accordingly for a muslim barber to cut hair in a manner contrary to the sharia to shave beards and to make this his trade is impermissible and the income from it is impermissible as well it is obligatory and necessary to repent of it see what a w al mar q al fal states

taking a fee for delivering talks and sermons is it permissible to take a fee for delivering talks and sermons or not from the statements of the jurists it appears that taking a fee for talks and sermons is permissible but our elders may allah have mercy on them did not approve of it there is therefore no dispute about its permissibility in itself it is simply not something to be commended if a speaker has set himself apart for preaching as his sole occupation however there is no harm in his taking a fee see what al durr al mukht r states al fat w al hindiyyah states

a mufti or a judge taking a fee for his work may a mufti and a judge fix a fee or charge for their work or not it is not permissible or correct for a mufti or a judge to take a fee for stating a ruling by word of mouth taking a fee for writing out the answer however is permissible and correct furthermore if there are several muftis in a city it is not obligatory upon any one of them to state the ruling while the others are there so in that case too it will be permissible to take a fee for stating the ruling see what al durr al mukht r states shar man mat ibn wahb n states

renting out land or a house to a bank is it permissible to rent out one's land or house to a bank or not broadly speaking banks are involved in interest based business but nowadays banks also handle other dealings besides interest based ones indeed most of their business consists of imports and exports the payment of salaries and the paying of electricity and telephone bills and the like through them the rent of a house let out to a bank will therefore not be unlawful even so it is better and preferable to keep away from it then if the owner has had the rooms built to suit a bank it is strictly disliked but if such rooms are built not for a bank alone but for other businesses and offices as well then it is mildly disliked see what al mabs states

renting out a house for the sale of liquor or for a cinema is it permissible for a muslim to rent out his house land and so on to a man who sells liquor and where should such rent be used what is the ruling now on rent that was received in the past this question is disputed among the hanafi jurists im m ab an fah may allah have mercy on him says that in a place where the disbelievers are in the majority it is permissible to rent out a house or land for the sale of liquor and the like and that it is also correct to take the income and rent derived from it the two disciples may allah have mercy on them however say that it is disliked thus fat w q kh n states likewise al ba r al r iq states

rent from a liquor shop and a cinema in a shopping mall if there is one liquor shop in a mall and the remaining shops deal in other goods may a muslim take the rent from it or not it should also be borne in mind that most of the mall's income 80 or 90 per cent say is lawful and only 10 per cent is rent from liquor a cinema and the like is this 10 per cent of the rent lawful or unlawful may the muslim owner take it or not in the case asked about our imams differ over renting out a shop or a building for liquor a cinema and other such sinful purposes and over taking the rental income from it the two disciples may allah have mercy on them say that it is not correct since it is helping in sin while im m ab an fah may allah have mercy on him says that such a contract of hire is sound and that taking the rent for it is permissible as well because the contract of hire is concluded upon the use of the shop or building and there is no sin in that the selling of liquor is the act of one who acts by his own free choice the owner of the property did not tell the tenant to sell liquor in it so if it was

two transactions in one in a contract of hire zayd gave cloth to a dyer telling him to dye it for 50 rupees and he dyed it or he gave cloth to a tailor telling him to sew it for 200 rupees and he sewed it on the face of it this transaction is permissible and it is what people in fact do but there is a juristic objection to it since the dye and the thread come from the hired worker this becomes a case of two transactions in one because a sale and a hire have been combined the sale of a substance together with the sale of a benefit is two transactions in one there also appears to be a further defect in it namely that a contract of hire is concerned with the consuming of a benefit whereas here an actual substance is consume the jurists have declared this transaction permissible because of established practice al hid yah states al in yah the commentary on al hid yah states it is indeed a case of two transactions in one since along with the hire there is a sale of the dye and in tailoring a sale of the thread and the materials that go with it but the hire is the principal matter and the sale is

hiring out a wedding hall to a non muslim may a muslim hire out his wedding hall to a non muslim or not when it is certain that the non muslims will engage in dancing music and other unlawful things in that hall in the view of im m ab an fah may allah have mercy on him it is permissible to hire a hall out to a non muslim while in the view of the two disciples may allah have mercy on them it is disliked there is also a difference among the fatawa of our elders may allah have mercy on them hazrat mufti rash d a mad resolved this difference by saying that giving it to a non muslim involves the milder kind of dislike in the case asked about since the tenant is a non muslim this transaction will be contrary to what is preferable it will not be unlawful or strictly disliked the evidences for this have already been set out in detail and repeating them would only make the answer long

forfeiting money paid when a booking is cancelled a man books a wedding hall for a sunday and pays part of the amount in advance if for some reason he then cancels one or two days beforehand part of the amount he has paid is forfeited is it correct to do this forfeiting the money resembles a sale with an earnest deposit bay al urb n and that is impermissible if however the owners of the wedding hall fix a certain fee for the booking and that sum is non refundable say they fix a hundred rand for the booking and the paperwork telephone costs office expenses and so on are met from it then this sum will not be returned just as an admission fee for a child is non refundable a detailed discussion of the sale with an earnest deposit has already been given in the book of sales and may be consulted there for the evidences that an admission fee is permissible see

making repairs a condition upon the hirer nowadays for certain practical reasons the lessor that is the owner lays down a condition upon the lessee that is the hirer that any fault which develops in the car will be put right and repaired by him is this correct or not the general books state that it is not correct from the statements of certain books of fiqh khul ah bazz ziyyah shar al majallah and others it appears that a condition placing some responsibility upon the hirer is permissible and correct even though the particular cases are somewhat different especially since the rulings on hire depend for the most part on custom and usage and since the practical needs of the age cannot be wholly disregarded either for this reason if in view of some benefit a measure of responsibility is placed upon the hirer as well the contract will not become corrupt see what khul at al fat w states

a wage for taking responsibility for work rather than doing it if in a contract of hire the hired man is not himself required to do the work but is only responsible for it and for managing it is it permissible for him to take a wage or not in the case asked about it is permissible and correct to take a salary or wage for taking responsibility for the work as contractors and the like do nowadays they do not do the work themselves but take a salary for the management and the responsibility and this is permissible see what al hid yah states taqr r t al r fi states

uncertainty about the amount of the wage a man engaged someone as a servant in his household and told him your salary is 1500 rand and along with it food drink board and lodging are also included is this permissible or not seeing that the kinds of food the quantity and so on are all unspecified this practice is current in general custom and food drink board and lodging differ from region to region and place to place and according to a person's standing in such matters people are easy going with one another and it does not lead to dispute such a contract is therefore permissible and correct it is nevertheless most important that the rights of each party be respected for otherwise each will have to answer for it on the day of judgement see what bad i al an i states

liability of a private employee who exceeds his instructions a man entrusted goods to one of his employees to deliver to a certain place for instance to take them from roshnee to johannesburg for some business of his own the employee went to lenasia and as soon as he parked the vehicle thieves broke open the door and stole the entrusted goods which had been kept in a safe place now some muftis say that no compensation is due from him since the place was safe while others say that this employee had no business going to lenasia for his own work and that compensation will therefore be due what is the opinion of your d r al ift on this question in the case asked about the employee was bound to take the direct road to johannesburg the r 82 but by taking the lenasia road he will be reckoned to have exceeded his instructions and so compensation will be due a man travelling from roshnee to johannesburg has nothing to do with the lenasia road this employee chose the lenasia road of his own accord for his own work and went against his employer's instructions and for that reason it is only just that compensation should fall due see what al mu al burh n states

liability of a hired worker who serves the public at large a man has opened a shop for repairing machines in which he repairs freezers and most other appliances someone gave him his microwave to be repaired and the machine went missing will the shopkeeper be liable to pay compensation or not in the case asked about a man who repairs machines for a fee is called in the terminology of the sharia a hired worker who serves the public at large the basic ruling concerning him is that if something is destroyed or stolen without any transgression on his part no compensation is due in the present age however in view of the corruption of the times and the general negligence of such workers the later jurists have given the ruling that compensation is obligatory so as to safeguard people's property compensation will therefore be obligatory on account of negligence and carelessness see what shar al majallah states

a teacher who arrives ten minutes late if a teacher arrives ten minutes late what should be done to make up for it should his salary be cut or is there some other arrangement in the case asked about if the teacher has made a habit of arriving late and does not stop even after being warned repeatedly then it is correct to cut his salary but if he comes late only now and then and the madrasah overlooks it on account of his sincerity or if the teacher makes up his work at other times then there is no harm in not cutting anything see what al durr al mukht r states

making the wage depend on a condition a man said to a tailor if you sew my clothes today you will get 50 rand and if you sew them tomorrow you will get 40 rand are both these conditions valid or not what is the difference of opinion between im m ab an fah may allah have mercy on him and the two disciples may allah have mercy on them on this and has anyone given a fatwa according to the view of the two disciples or not im m ab an fah may allah have mercy on him says that the first condition is valid but the second is corrupt and that the customary wage will then be payable in the view of the two disciples may allah have mercy on them both conditions are permissible and correct among our jurists shaykh al isl m the chief justice ab al asan al al saghd may allah have mercy on him d 461 adopted the view of the two disciples may allah have mercy on them if however there is an element of deception in it then it is not permissible see what al nutaf f al fat w states
