stipulating that the owner of the capital will also work a man gave another man some money and entered into a mu rabah contract with him on the basis that whatever profit was made would be divided equally between the two of them but he laid down the condition that the owner of the capital would work alongside the working partner is such a mu rabah contract valid or not if it is not valid how may it be put right in the case described the mu rabah contract is defective and void because stipulating that the owner will work makes a mu rabah contract void see what al durr al mukht r states fat w q kh n states

the owner working without it having been stipulated if work was not made a condition upon the owner of the capital but he does some work voluntarily is there room for that or not in a mu rabah contract no work is stipulated upon the owner the capital has been handed over completely to the working partner and the owner stands in the position of a stranger to it so if he does some work voluntarily that is if he helps the working partner this is permissible and valid and the mu rabah contract will not be rendered defective by it al hid yah states shar al i

the owner of the capital working as a paid employee once a mu rabah contract has been concluded is it permissible for the working partner to take on the owner of the capital as a salaried employee or not in the case described it is not permissible to take the owner of the capital on as a salaried employee doing so makes the mu rabah contract defective there is however room for him to work as a helper bad i al an i states

fixing a set amount of profit in a mu rabah contract mid works as a commission agent ma m d gave him 2 000 000 rand to trade with according to the sharia and laid down the condition that if the profit in one year came to more than 400 000 rand then whatever was earned above 400 000 would be divided between the working partner and the owner of the capital on a fifty fifty basis so for example if mid earns 600 000 rand in profit he will receive 100 000 but if he earns only 400 000 he will receive nothing if a loss is incurred in the buying and selling of shares the owner will bear it what is the ruling on this is it permissible in the sharia or not the substance of the above case is that of whatever profit the business makes twenty per cent of the capital will go to the owner of the capital and in whatever further profit is made above that twenty per cent both the working partner and the owner will share now the jurists have written that every arrangement in which a fixed amount of the profit is set aside for one of the parties or in which the profit is divided only after a particular amount of it has been set aside is impermissible for it is possible that no profit will be made beyond that fixed amount in which case one party will be left with nothing fixing a percentage of the capital itself for one of them is likewise imp

stipulating that living expenses be taken from the capital in a mu rabah contract the working partner laid down the condition that he would take his food and drink and all his household expenses out of the capital is it permissible to make such a condition or not in a mu rabah contract if the working partner remains in his own city and trades there then it is not permissible or valid for him to take his food and drink and household expenses out of the capital and to make such a condition renders the contract defective if however he trades in another city then he may take the necessary cost of his food drink and lodging out of the capital it is not valid for him to take more than that then when the business makes a profit the capital will first be made whole and after that the remaining profit will be divided between the two of them see what shar al majallah states

fixing a set monthly sum for the owner of the capital zayd provided amr with a shop to trade from and the entire capital is zayd's as well amr is to do the trading zayd however laid down the condition that whether or not there is a profit he will collect ten thousand rand a month from amr which contract does this dealing fall under and is such a contract permissible in the sharia or not the dealing described above is called a mu rabah in a mu rabah contract it is not permissible or valid to fix a monthly sum for either the working partner or the owner of the capital such a condition renders the contract defective moreover because such a fixed sum resembles interest it is forbidden to take it see what al hid yah states shar al in yah states

leaving the profit share unspecified in a mu rabah kh lid gave bakr a sum of money and told him do business with this money and i will give you something he specified nothing explicitly neither as a percentage nor as a fixed sum what is the ruling of the sharia on this arrangement this is a mu rabah arrangement but because the profit share was left unknown the contract has become defective and in a defective mu rabah the working partner will receive the going rate for his labour see what shar al majallah states al hid yah states
the ruling on a defective mu rabah what is the ruling on a defective mu rabah fat w q kh n states bad i al an i states al durr al mukht r states

a working partner selling to his own company someone gave zayd 100 000 rand as mu rabah capital and he bought a consignment of timber with it may zayd now sell these goods to his own company or not in the case described if zayd owns the whole company then his selling to his company amounts to selling to himself and it appears from the wording of al fat w al bazz ziyyah that such a contract is permissible and valid with the permission of the owner of the capital and if zayd is only one member of the company there is still a danger of suspicion so he is permitted to sell at the going market price selling below that price is not valid because the owner of the capital would then suffer a loss and a working partner may not do anything that causes harm see what al fat w al bazz ziyyah states

a working partner making a tawliyah sale when a mu rabah contract is unrestricted is it permissible for the working partner to make a tawliyah sale that is to sell at cost price in an unrestricted mu rabah the working partner may not do anything that involves harm and loss and is not customary among traders apart from that he may do everything connected with the business he will therefore also be permitted to make a tawliyah sale indeed there are times when he has to do so for some particular benefit for instance the value of the goods may have fallen or he may wish to do the buyer a favour because the buyer has done him a good turn or may do so in the future he should not however make a practice of this he may do it now and then when there is good reason for it see what al mabs states

the owner of the capital charging rent for his own shop mid gave ma m d one of his shops to trade from and the whole of the capital is mid's as well ma m d merely does the trading mid told ma m d i shall take ten thousand rand a month from you as rent for my shop whether the business makes a profit or a loss is such a contract valid or not it appears from the statements of the jurists that the working partner may enter into a contract with the owner of the capital and a contract of hire is itself such a contract so in the case in question it is valid for the owner of the capital to take ten thousand rand a month from the working partner as rent see what al durr al mukht r states

the ruling on limited liability if someone wishes to register his company as a limited liability company is that permissible or not and is it permissible to buy shares in such a company a brief introduction to limited liability limited liability means that the liability of the shareholders is limited to the capital they have put in that is if the company runs at a loss the worst they will suffer is that the capital they invested is lost and if the company's debts mount up the shareholders will not be called upon for anything beyond the capital they invested jad d mu mal t ke shar a k m 2 42 isl m awr jad d ma sh mas il states in modern legal and economic usage limited liability describes a situati in the sharia a company and its shareholders stand in the same relation as the owner of the capital and the working partner in a mu rabah contract because the shareholders in a company put their capital into it and share in the profit without doing the work themselves the shareholders will therefore have the status of the owner of the capital the ruling on limited liability most contemporary scholars are of the view that a partnership cannot be called defective merely because of the concept of limited liability in fiqh there is a most interesting parallel to the limited company one that comes very close to it the slave who is permitted by his master to trade such a man is his mast

fixing a larger share for the partner who does the work if two men are partners in a business that is their capital is joint and one of them works while the other does not and a larger share is fixed for the one who works is this permissible or not and is this arrangement a partnership or a mu rabah in the case described this arrangement is in reality a mu rabah in which something extra 80 per cent say has been fixed for the one who works for example zayd has 100 000 rand and umar has 100 000 rand and because umar is the one who works 80 per cent is fixed for him and 20 per cent for zayd what this amounts to is that 50 per cent of the profit is the profit on umar's own capital and of the remaining 50 per cent umar receives 30 per cent for his labour and zayd receives 20 per cent for his capital the partnership here means a partnership in the profit and that is a mu rabah

giving money to a company as mu rabah capital a man gave a company a sum of money to buy a tank the company buys the tank and hands it over to its manager and the company's manager hires it out along with other tanks the profit earned is then divided among them in such a way that the manager takes about 15 per cent and the company takes 5 per cent while the rest of the profit is divided among the owners of the tanks is there room in the sharia for such a contract or not in the case described this arrangement is a mu rabah contract in the sense that the owners of the tanks have the status of the owner of the capital while the company the manager and so on have the status of the working partner mixing the mu rabah capital with other people's funds and trading with it is permissible and valid with the express permission of the owner of the capital or where he has said act as you see fit and the profit between them has been fixed as a percentage this mu rabah contract is therefore sound and valid lamg r states

terminating a mu rabah zayd and amr began a mu rabah in 2002 zayd the owner of the capital was to have a 25 per cent share and amr the working partner a 75 per cent share in 2007 the working partner gave the owner of the capital only 3 000 as profit and told him to take his capital back when the rest of the profit was asked for the working partner said that he would pay it off little by little the question is this has the mu rabah come to an end or not and is it correct to take the remaining profit later or not in the case described the mu rabah contract may be brought to an end by giving notice to the owner of the capital and if the working partner does not have the money at present it is also permissible for the rest of the profit to be collected later but if the working partner does have it it is not permissible for him to put the matter off see what bad i al an i states bi

fixing a salary for a working partner a man works in a shop on a mu rabah basis he receives 25 per cent of the profit and the owner of the capital takes 75 per cent or a man may be someone's partner may a partner or a working partner be paid a salary over and above his share or not here it is the custom to pay a salary the working partner is to be given the return for his labour as a percentage of the profit he may not take a fixed monthly salary if however the working partner works in the capacity of a salaried employee then he may take a salary and if he is paid a salary together with a reduced share of the profit that too is permissible this is because the scholars differ over whether a partner may be engaged as a hired employee most of the jurists hold it impermissible but a rat muft rash d a mad ludhy nw ib may allah have mercy on him allowed it see what sh m states al nutaf f al fat w states

cancelling a mu rabah when the business has made no profit two men entered into a mu rabah agreement whereby one would provide the capital and the other the labour a plot of land was bought for 100 000 rand on which a number of shops are to be built and whatever profit comes from it is to be divided equally between the two of them the building work will go on for about a year about five months after this agreement the owner of the capital wants to cancel it in that period about 30 000 rand of the capital has been spent on the building work the question now is if the working partner keeps this land for himself how much money must he return to the owner of the capital the second question is since no profit at all has been made so far what in a mu rabah contract both the owner of the capital and the working partner have the right to cancel the contract after giving notice and in the event of cancellation the working partner must return the capital to the owner of the capital so in the case in question the working partner should either sell the land to someone else or buy it himself and return the capital and since no profit at all has been made so far the working partner will receive nothing see what bad i al an i states

holding the working partner liable for a loss mid and ma m d started a business together it was written in the agreement that ma m d would put in 500 000 rupees as capital and that mid would do the trading that of the profit earned ma m d would take 75 per cent and mid would receive 25 per cent and that if any loss occurred ma m d alone would bear it they had been trading under this agreement for two years some time ago a number of people bought goods from mid and then disappeared without paying for them ma m d is now demanding the loss from mid even though the agreement states the opposite and mid had been trading properly and to the full extent of his ability with no shortcoming on his part what is the ruling of in a mu rabah contract the working partner is a trustee with regard to the money he receives from the owner of the capital and with regard to dealing in it he is also an agent that is he is the representative of the one who has put up the capital as a trustee it is binding upon him to safeguard the capital but if a loss happens to occur in that capital or it is destroyed the working partner is not answerable for it if however it is established that he destroyed the property deliberately then he will be answerable for it and he will likewise be answerable if he has acted against the conditions laid down by the owner of the capital keeping the above ruling of the sharia in view

how to earn profit on islamic principles if a bank or a company takes money from people in accordance with islamic principles earns a profit on that money and pays the profit to the people whose money it is how should this be done the company or bank should take the money from people on a mu rabah basis those who place their money with it will be in the position of the owner of the capital while the company or bank will be designated the working partner provided that they actually carry on trade the profit will be divided between them according to a particular agreed ratio for instance 40 per cent for the owner of the capital and 60 per cent for the working partner that is the bank now it is obvious that people do not all deposit and withdraw their money on the same dates so in this case the profit should be divided on the basis of an accounting based on the daily product daily product b

the ruling on restricting a mu rabah to a fixed term in a mu rabah profit sharing investment partnership contract if someone says you may invest the money for whatever period you like but the term must be a minimum of 5 years and a maximum of 15 years is it permissible to lay down such a condition or not in the case described it is permissible and valid to restrict a mu rabah contract to a fixed term and to lay down such a condition it is clear from the statements of the jurists however that a condition fixing a minimum term is not valid the right to dissolve the contract remains even before that term has elapsed al fat w al hindiyyah states isl m fiqh states where a term has been fixed each of the two parties has the right to bring the arrangement to an end as soon as that term expires isl m awr jad d ma sh mas il states ac

some rulings relating to mu rabah 1 if the rabb al m l the investor lays down a condition upon the mu rib the working partner that he must trade for cash may he then trade on credit he may not al mabs states question 2 can a mu rabah contract be concluded with a non muslim the answer this is a commercial transaction and sharing the same religion is not a requirement for a commercial transaction the messenger of allah himself entered into dealings with non muslims bad i al an i states

the ruling on a mu rabah with a telephone company what do the noble scholars say concerning the following matter a man has received a licence from the government to operate a telephone company for which he paid a fee of about 20 000 dollars he made great efforts to obtain the licence and spent a good deal of money on it and he has started a company to run the business but a substantial sum is needed to buy machinery and the like suppose this man says to ten people let each of you give me 15 000 dollars on the condition that i will pay you a fixed percentage of whatever profit this business earns and after one year the capital together with the profit will be paid over suppose he also stipulates that none of the ten will have an in the case described a this arrangement is a mu rabah a profit sharing investment partnership and it is permissible mu rabah means that the capital comes from one party while the other does the work and the profit is divided by percentage in accordance with the agreed condition it is not permissible however to fix a set sum of money for anyone nor is it permissible to take a percentage of the capital because that falls under the ruling of interest al durr al mukht r states

the ruling on the rabb al m l including his own son in a mu rabah contract zayd gave umar one hundred thousand rand as a mu rabah a profit sharing investment partnership and it was agreed between them that 30 percent of the profit would belong to the rabb al m l the investor and 60 percent to the mu rib the working partner and that the rabb al m l's son would work alongside the mu rib as manager and would receive 10 percent of the profit is this arrangement correct or not in the case described fixing the profit by percentage is sound and correct it is likewise correct for the rabb al m l to make his son the manager and he too will be given 10 percent of the profit because in a mu rabah contract the rabb al m l's son stands in the position of an outsider and it is permissible and correct to assign an outsider a share of the profit in return for his work shar al majallah states al fat w al hindiyyah states

the ruling on sharing in the wages without doing the work zayd is a tailor who is well known throughout the whole city he sits in a shop only occasionally and the shop runs under his supervision three men do the sewing work at this shop zayd does nothing he comes for two or three hours yet he shares equally in the wages that are earned is it permissible for zayd to take a share of the wages without doing the work or not in the terminology of the jurists the arrangement described above is construed as sharikat al an i a partnership in crafts and it is permissible by way of juristic preference isti s n although in its outward form it is a contract of hire in reality it is a contract of partnership it is also given the names sharikat al taqabbul partnership in taking on work sharikat al a m l and sharikat al abd n that is one partner accepts work from people on the strength of his reputation and standing and the wages earned are then divided between them on this basis in the case described it is permissible and correct for zayd to share in the wages without doing the work al durr al mukht

the ruling on one heir trading with the estate a man passed away and his estate had not been divided two of the deceased's sons carried on their father's business and earned a handsome profit now after a period of ten years has passed they wish to divide the estate will all the heirs share in the profit or will only what was present at the time of the deceased's death be divided whatever profit was made from the deceased's property before it was divided all the heirs will share in the entire wealth even though the remaining heirs took no part in trading with the jointly owned property they will still share in the profit and the whole of the property together with the profit will be divided among all the heirs in the manner laid down by the shar ah yes it is appropriate if those who did the work are given something over and above their share but this is not obligatory in the shar ah al ashb h wa'l na ir states

the ruling on selling one's own share two brothers own a house worth two million one brother already has a house of his own and wants to rent this one out he does not want to sell it the other has no house and wants to sell it whose wish is to be given effect if the two held the property as partners from the outset or received it by inheritance then each of them may sell his own share without the other's permission but if the sale would cause harm to the other partner or harm to the seller or the buyer then he may not sell his share as with a building trees or a standing crop which may not be sold without the other partner's permission accordingly in the case described the wish of the brother who does not want to sell will be given effect and one partner may not sell the house without the other's permission because the house consists of a building shar al majallah states

the ruling on profit made by selling shares that are not shar ah compliant in 2004 a man bought 20 000 rand worth of shares in awais investments at a time when it was operating under shar ah rules now according to this man it no longer operates on shar ah rules so the shareholder sold his shares and received a total of 47 000 that is he made a profit over and above his capital may he use the profit he has received or not for as long as the company traded in accordance with shar ah rules the profit of that period is lawful and permissible but from the time it began trading on non shar ah lines the profit should be given away in charity without the intention of earning reward fiqh maq l t states there are four conditions for the permissibility of buying and selling shares 1 the underlying business must be lawful 2 if the company carries out some interest based dealings one must raise one's voice against this at its annual meeting 3 when the profits are distributed whatever portion of the profit was derived from interest bearing deposits must be given away in charity

the ruling on the labourers of a jointly owned company there is a jointly owned company with several partners and one of these partners belongs to a church and its associated bodies the company has various departments the work of one department is to make all the arrangements for labourers food drink sleeping quarters and so on and then to place those same labourers in employment with other companies in return for a payment the matter to be determined is this is it permissible to deal with this department of the company and to take these labourers into employment or not given that the company is connected with the church people where the labourers work however they do not perform any worship or the like they only work in the case described it is permissible and correct to hire non muslims and to have work done by them since they will not be performing their worship on your premises nor is this cooperation in sin because you will be paying wages for your own work and not for anything else there is therefore no harm in dealing with such a company yes if this company were engaged in some covert conspiracy against muslims then it should be avoided a al bukh r states

the ruling on a partnership for making bricks the jurists have written that a partnership for gathering firewood i ti b is not valid rather whoever gathers the wood is its owner if that is so what is the difference between gathering firewood and making bricks is a partnership for making bricks permissible or not a partnership for gathering firewood is not permissible because a partnership for acquiring something that is free for all to take is not valid as for a partnership for making bricks the ruling is that if the clay is owned the partnership is permissible and valid but if the clay is free for all and unowned then it is just like gathering firewood and there is no difference that is whoever did a particular piece of work owns it and if the two worked together and it is not known how much each of them did then each will receive a half al durr al mukht r states

the conditions and ruling of sharikat al muf wa ah what are the conditions of sharikat al muf wa ah a partnership of full equality and if the conditions are not met in what form will the partnership remain muf wa ah means entrusting things to one another this partnership is called muf wa ah because each partner entrusts his wealth to the other capital is necessary in it and equality in the profit is a condition the following are required for this partnership 1 the capital of the two must be equal from beginning to end 2 both must be equal sharers in the profit 3 each partner will have the authority to buy and sell the property to deal with it and to lend it out 4 if a partner buys something for his own personal needs the other partner has no right to say anything about it but if he has taken those goods on credit the shopkeeper has the right to demand payment from the other

the ruling on a partnership in goods if partners form a partnership in goods instead of cash for example zayd has cloth and umar has books and they conclude a partnership between themselves on the condition of half the profit each is this permissible or not the jurists say that for a sharikat al muf wa ah and a sharikat al in n the capital that the partners put together must be of the category of cash it must consist of gold silver current coinage or the like a partnership in goods will not be sound or valid shar al majallah states mawl n afar a mad uthm n may allah have mercy on him however gave a fatwa in imd d al a k

who bears the cost of valuing jointly owned property six people are partners in a piece of land one of them wishes to withdraw from the partnership so the land will now have to be valued in order that he may be paid a sum corresponding to his share who will bear the cost of valuing this land will the cost of the valuation be divided equally among all the partners or will it fall upon that one partner in the case in question all the partners will share equally in the cost of valuing the land because the benefit is shared by all of them each will come to know the value of the land and just as the fee of the divider falls equally upon all the partners so too the cost of the valuation will fall equally upon them all consider what al hid yah states majma al anhur states

the ruling on pre emption when three people are partners in a piece of land three brothers are partners in a piece of land ab bakr imr n and afw n ab bakr sold his share to imr n can afw n claim the right of pre emption or not and if he can over how much of it afw n can claim the right of pre emption of whatever share belonged to ab bakr afw n may take half and the remaining half will stay with imr n al durr al mukht r states durar al ukk m states

the ruling on pre emption in endowed land if a piece of land next to a madrasah is being sold can the principal of the madrasah claim the right of pre emption over that land or not there is no right of pre emption in endowed land nor may the endower or the trustee exercise pre emption on behalf of endowed land for the right of pre emption to be established ownership of the land is necessary and an endowment has no owner al durr al mukht r states shiyat al a w states

the ruling on pre emption when a house has two neighbours if a house has two neighbours and the owner of the house sold it to one of the neighbours can the other neighbour claim the right of pre emption or not if two neighbours claim the right of pre emption the house will be divided into three portions between the buyer and the two pre emptors and if there is only one neighbour the house will be divided into two portions al fat w al hindiyyah states fat w sh m states

the ruling on lending out a pledged item if a pledgor placed a car with the pledgee as a pledge but instead of leaving the car idle he left the car's papers with the pledgee and continued to use the car himself which is called using it on loan is this permissible or not in this way the car would be saved from lying idle what is the ruling in the sharia this is permissible and sound in the sharia because lending out a pledged item does not nullify the contract of pledge since the pledgee may take the pledged item back whenever he wishes yes on account of its being lent out the pledged item will pass out of the pledgee's liability bad i al an i states it is written in another place

the ruling on lending a pledged house back to the pledgor if zayd lent umar 200 000 rand and umar placed a house with zayd as a pledge but zayd did not take possession of the house and instead gave that same house to umar on loan will this action have any effect on the pledge or not that is will the house be regarded as pledged or not in the case in question lending the pledged item back to the pledgor will have no effect upon the pledge and the house will remain pledged as before it will however pass out of the pledgee's liability taby n al aq iq states

the ruling on pledging a shop held on pag zayd has a shop held on pag key money paid for tenancy rights zayd obtained the shop by paying two hundred thousand rupees as pag zayd now needs a large sum in connection with his business for which a pledge is required can zayd pledge the shop held on pag or not if zayd holds the pag shop permanently then it is like his own property in which no one else has any share he may therefore pledge that shop majallah fiqh isl m compiled by q muj hid al isl m ib states if the custom of the locality is that on account of this dealing in pag the original owner is dispossessed of the shop or house all his rights of ownership being taken away and passing to the tenant then this takes the ruling of a sale the pag money stands in the position of the price and the shop and building in the position of the goods sold while the rent is for the land upon which the shop and building stand it is as though the land belongs to the owner and th

the ruling on appointing the pledgee as agent for the sale if mid lent ma m d money and ma m d placed his house with mid as a pledge laying down the condition that if ma m d did not repay the debt within one year then mid the pledgee would have the right to sell the house and recover his debt is it permissible to lay down such a condition or not and in the event that the house is sold will the right belong to the pledgee alone or will the pledgor have a right as well in the case in question it is permissible and sound to lay down such a condition because the pledgor is the owner of the house so he may sell it himself and may also appoint another as his agent for the sale then of the money realised after the sale of the house mid the pledgee will take only what is his by right and the remaining money he will return to ma m d the pledgor that is the owner of the house because the pledgee has no right to the surplus al hid yah states taby n al aq iq states

the ruling on selling a pledge without the pledgor's permission a man needed a house or a piece of land but did not have the money he approached a bank and the bank staff bought that land as his agent and handed it over to him the matter was settled on instalments namely that he would pay the bank a certain sum every month the bank took something as a pledge that is it kept the papers of that item with itself after some time this man stopped paying the instalments the bank demanded payment but even so he refused to pay the matter to be determined now is whether the bank can sell that item and recover what is due to it or not in the case in question it is sound to sell with the pledgor's permission but it is not sound to sell without his permission yes if the pledgor neither discharges the debt nor is willing to sell then concerning this the jurists generally write that it will be permissible to sell by the order of the ruler or the judge shar al majallah states

the ruling on taking impermissible assets as a pledge if a bank took shares as a pledge and these shares are shares in an impermissible company answers are sought to the following questions 1 may al baraka bank take such impermissible shares as a pledge or not 2 if the debtor did not repay the loan may al baraka bank sell these impermissible shares 3 is the profit obtained from these impermissible shares impermissible for the pledgee as well in the case in question shares that are wholly impermissible must be given away in charity it is not sound for either the pledgor or the pledgee to take them as a pledge or to derive benefit from them shar al majallah states the upshot of this passage is that things which are not valued property and are not f

the ruling on the pledgee taking possession of the pledge under government law if a pledgor placed his land with a pledgee as a pledge and did not discharge the debt for a long period about twenty years and the law of the government is that after a long period the pledgee becomes the owner of the land will the pledgee be regarded in the sharia as the owner of the land or not in the case in question if the pledgor is unable to repay the debt within a particular period and the pledgee under the law of the government forcibly keeps the pledge with himself and becomes its owner or if under government law a suit is brought and the pledgee wins the case in both situations the pledgee will not become the owner of that land or item in the sharia a hadith states

the ruling on taking possession in a gift of a pledged item mid took a loan from ma m d and pledged jewellery against it mid then repaid the loan and made a gift of that jewellery to ma m d since ma m d has studied books of fiqh in which it is written that possession by way of liability does not stand in place of possession by way of trust a renewal of possession is required yet mid lives far away in another country what should be done now this question has already been dealt with in detail in our collection of fatwas it is enough to write here that all mah q sim ibn qu l bugh may allah have mercy on him wrote in al ta wa l tarj that for the renewal of possession it is sufficient that ma m d remain in the presence of the item for as long as would allow him to take possession of it he writes

the ruling on a usurped item after compensation has been paid i had a machine for checking blood pressure which was reckoned among the very finest machines in my absence a certain person took that machine from our house without my permission and told me afterwards some days later i asked for the machine to be returned he said very well but after searching he said that the machine had been lost and he paid compensation some time later he brought the good news that my machine had been found may i now take my machine back or not in the case in question if the compensation was paid in accordance with the owner's own valuation the owner cannot forcibly take the machine back but if the compensation received was not in accordance with the owner's valuation but in accordance with the usurper's then the owner may take the machine back and return the compensation money al hid yah states

the ruling on compensation when a usurped item is damaged one companion took another companion's mobile phone without his permission and it was damaged is compensation due for it or not and if he took it with permission what is the ruling then in the case in question if he took it without permission and there was no customary permission between them either and the phone was damaged then compensation is due but if he took it with permission then it is a trust and no compensation will be due in the absence of transgression or negligence shar al majallah states

the ruling on the usurpation of immovable property i am a weak man a ruffian took possession of a piece of my land and kept it in his possession for five years during this period he himself derived benefit from it for three years and for two years he let the land out on rent and collected the rent in short by employing various means the land was recovered from his possession the matter to be determined now is whether compensation for this period is binding upon him or not it should be borne in mind that during this period no change occurred in the value of the land in the case in question if no loss was caused to the land through its usurpation then no compensation is obligatory or binding upon the usurper if however the owner wishes to demand rent for the period of use there is room for that shar al majallah states

the ruling when a usurped item has lost value a man usurped another man's machine and returned it after some time but in the meantime its value had fallen greatly about half its value remained although it was not broken is compensation obligatory or not in the case in question if the value fell on account of the usurper's use of it then compensation is obligatory upon the usurper but if the decrease occurred without any use on his part and he handed it back at the place of the usurpation then the usurper is not answerable for it the author of al in yah all mah akmal al d n al b bart states

the ruling on the benefits derived from a usurped item a man usurped someone's vehicle drove it for three months and earned a good many rand with it and then returned the vehicle to its owner will compensation be due from him according to the anaf school or not it should also be borne in mind that no damage was caused to the vehicle according to the school of the anaf s after driving the vehicle and obtaining rent for it if the rent money is still in hand it will be given to the owner and if the usurper has already spent it there is no compensation but the position given as the fatwa position in our time is that if the vehicle is one kept for hire then rent is due for as many days as the usurper used it indeed according to the view of the researcher ibn al hum m may allah have mercy on him of shaykh al alab may allah have mercy on him and of the commentator on the majallah shaykh al aydar may allah have mercy on him compensation will be due even if the vehicle is not one kept for hire and this i

the ruling on compensation for usurping a house a man took forcible and usurping possession of another's house and lived in it for two months then the house was recovered from that man is rent due from the usurper or not the question of the usurpation of immovable property has already been mentioned the upshot is that if no loss was caused to the house compensation is not obligatory if however the house had been prepared for letting then two months' rent will be due furthermore even if it was not kept for letting compensation ought still to be due fat w sh m states al bin yah shar al hid yah states for further evidence see the questions

the ruling on usurping grain and sowing it a man stole some grain and sowed it raising a crop from it afterwards he was granted the ability to repent will he now give the whole crop to the owner or only the stolen grain and what will he then do with the remainder furthermore if he sold it and started a business with the proceeds and earned a large profit what is the ruling on that in the view of the anaf s if such a change comes about in a usurped item through the act of the usurper that the very name of the item is altered and most of its uses are also lost then the usurper becomes the owner of that item and the benefits obtained from it will likewise be in the usurper's ownership yes it will be binding upon the usurper to pay the substitute for the usurped item and before paying it benefiting from the profits will not be lawful for him then the ruling concerning such benefiting is this if he bought something by pointing to the usurped property and handed over that very property indicated as the price then the income from it is impermissible and must be g

the ruling on benefiting from a usurped item if a person usurped or stole something and then gave the owner its equivalent or the owner being unknown gave its value away in charity on his behalf will the use of that thing now be permissible or not in the case in question it is binding and necessary to convey the usurped item itself to its owner and any kind of benefiting from it is impermissible if the owner is not known it is obligatory to give that item away in charity on the owner's behalf unless the usurped item is destroyed in which case its value becomes due yes if the owner himself forgives it or gladly gives permission to benefit from it then that is within his discretion al hid yah with shar al in yah states

the ruling on recovering one's right from goods of a different kind if a person usurped zayd's property may zayd take in place of his own property some other thing of the same value or not the original position of the school is that it is impermissible to recover one's right from goods of a different kind but in the present age on account of the corruption of the times the fatwa is that recovering one's right from goods of a different kind is permissible and sound fat w sh m states

the ruling on compensation for abducting a child a man abducted someone's three year old child and the child died while with the abductor is compensation or blood money due from him or not and if he abducted an older child of 15 years and he died what is the ruling in the case in question if he kept the child in an ordinary place and the child died of himself or from a fever or the like then liability is not due from the abductor but if he kept him in a place that was not ordinary and he died from an epidemic or from a disease of that place or a snake or the like bit him or he died through some calamity then blood money will be due from the abductor's family by a small child is meant one so small that he cannot identify himself for example a three year old child and if he abducted an adolescent boy and then kept him in such confinement that he was unable to protect himself and perished then compensation will be due but if he was able to pr

the ruling on the profits of usurped property a man stole or usurped someone's property and by trading with that property greatly increased it now through the blessing of the tabl gh jam at allah most high has granted him the ability to repent does all this earned wealth now belong to the owner or will only the stolen and usurped property be returned and will the remaining wealth then be permissible for the repentant man or not in the case described the stolen and usurped property will be returned and as for the wealth earned by means of that property the following several cases are possible 1 he designated the usurped property and bought lawful goods against it and then paid over that usurped or stolen property as the price 2 he bought a lawful item without designating the usurped property and then paid over the usurped property as the price 3 he designated lawful property and paid over the usurped property 4 he designated the usurped property and paid over lawful property in the first case the income obtained will be impermissible and must be given away in charity in the remaining cases a

the ruling on giving charity on behalf of a non muslim from whom something was usurped if a person usurped the property of a non muslim and does not know his whereabouts what should the muslim do with it if he gives it away in charity on his behalf can charity be given on behalf of a non muslim the ruling on the usurped item itself is that it should be returned to its true owner so long as it still exists if it has been destroyed compensation will be due but if the owner's exact whereabouts are unknown and it is not easy to trace him then it will be given away in charity on his behalf however the conveying of reward cannot be made to a non muslim so he should give it without the intention of reward just as a dead dog and the like is taken out of the house and thrown away fat w sh m states

whether a non muslim is rewarded in the hereafter for his good deeds if a person steals or seizes the property of a non muslim will the non muslim be given that muslim's good deeds on the day of judgement or not and will the burden of this act fall on the muslim or not in the case described the muslim's good deeds will not be given to the disbeliever because disbelievers are not fit to receive them that is they do not have the capacity to deserve reward as for the good works they did in this world those may bring them some reduction in punishment according to some scholars however the disbeliever's sins other than his disbelief may be placed upon the muslim by disbeliever here is meant the dhimm a non muslim living under muslim rule and the musta min a non muslim granted safe conduct that is one who is not a combatant and not in a state of war a arb a non muslim at war is also included however when a peace treaty is in force

a bag of flour found in a kitchen zayd found a bag of flour in the students' communal kitchen it had been lying there for about two months and no owner is known what is the ruling on this bag now is there any room for him to use it in the case described the bag of flour comes under the ruling of lost property luq ah the rule for lost property is that the person who finds it must announce it and publicise it until the owner is identified but if after every possible effort and a thorough search no trace of the owner is found and one has completely given up hope of his coming forward then the finder himself may use it if he is poor and in need and if he is a person of means it is to be given away in charity on the owner's behalf consider what the hadiths say about lost property

finding something valuable inside goods one has bought these days grain foodstuffs and the like come packed by the companies and are sold in the shops if after buying such a bag the purchaser finds something valuable in it a gold coin for example whose will it be is it to be returned to the company or does it belong to the seller or may the purchaser keep it himself in the case described the seller and the seller's own supplier should be asked about it if they say they know nothing of it or say that it is not theirs then it comes under the ruling of lost property luq ah the finder must look for the owner and hand it over to him if the owner is not found then the purchaser may use it if he is himself in need otherwise he should give it away in charity consider what fat w sh m states al hid yah states

a trust held for someone whose owner cannot be traced a person is holding something entrusted to him for safe keeping a long time has passed and there is still no trace of its owner what is the ruling on this trust now for how much longer is it to be kept and what is to be done with it if the owner does not come in the case described if it is most likely that the owner has died or will not come back and no heir of his is known either then the ruling is the same as that of lost property if the holder is well off he should give it away in charity and if he is himself in need he is permitted to use it if the owner does come and asks for the trust however its value must be paid to him consider what fat w sh m states

the property of a deceased person who leaves no known heir a man has died and the person in whose house he died knows nothing about his heirs what should he do with the dead man's property he left no bequest either in the case described the ruling is the same as that of lost property if the householder is himself poor he may use it and if not he should distribute it among the poor consider what al durr al mukht r states al ikht

selling an article one has found a man found an article and sold it to someone else at a very low price the owner has still not been traced what should the finder do now should he give the amount he received in charity or the real value of the article or is it not necessary for him to give anything in charity at all the rule for lost property is that its owner is to be sought out and the article itself handed over to him if the owner cannot be traced it is to be publicised continually until there is no longer any hope of his coming forward and then it is to be given away in charity and if the finder is himself poor he is permitted to use it lost property should not be sold however because the owner's ownership of it has not lapsed if the finder has sold it he should give the price away in charity and if the owner does come forward the real value of the article will have to be returned to him i l al sunan states

how lost property is to be publicised how is lost property to be announced and publicised is there any particular method for doing so the jurists have written that announcements should be made at public gatherings at the doors of mosques and in the markets and that notices and advertisements should be put up nowadays publicity can also be given through broadcasting media such as radio islam and the like in short it should be publicised by every means possible if the owner comes forward and the marks he describes make one certain or make it most likely that this is indeed its owner the article should be handed over to him consider what a hadith states

using things washed down by a flood if something is washed down by a flood is it permissible to make use of it or not given that there is no way of knowing whose these things are or where they have come from in the case described things washed down by a flood are of several kinds 1 ordinary items about which one is certain or it is most likely that the owner will not come looking for them using such things is permissible and correct and there is no particular need to publicise them 2 valuable items which owners generally do search for using such things is not correct their ruling is that of lost property that is they must be announced and publicised 3 a valuable item which is likely to spoil quickly a large quantity of fruit for example using such things is correct but if the owner comes and asks for it its value will have to be returned to him consider what majma

an article left for repair whose owner never came back for it kh lid repairs articles for a fee r il gave him something of his to be repaired several years have now passed but the man has not come to collect it what should kh lid do with it now may he use it or sell it and keep the money or not if it is kept any longer there is a risk of its being spoilt if kh lid has given up hope of the owner's coming back and there is a risk of the article being spoilt if it is kept any longer then in that case it should be given away in charity and if kh lid is himself poor and in need he may use it in both cases however if the owner turns up and asks for it its value will have to be paid to him consider what fat w sh m states

books and notebooks left behind by students at a madrasah at the end of the year many students both local and foreign go home leaving their own books and notebooks behind in the classrooms in the residence rooms and in various other places around the madrasah usually they have no further interest in these things and it is quite certain that they will never come back to collect their book or notebook would it be correct for another student to use such books and keep them for himself or not in the case described if the owner of a book is known and his name is written on it he should be contacted and asked what he wants done with the book the name is generally written on the book if no name is written on it and the owner is not known then these books come under the ruling of lost property enquiries should be made about the owner and if it is most likely that the owner will not be found the books should be given to needy students on the owners' behalf if the person who picked the book up does not himself own the nisab the threshold amount of wealth he may take it for himself the evidence on lost property has been given in detail earlier it may be consulted there

the sharia ruling on sharecropping if a person gives his land to another on a sharecropping basis on the terms that half the crop will be his and half the owner's is this permissible or not and if it is permissible will the contract be invalid if no fixed period is agreed also after how long may the owner remove the sharecropper from the arrangement the original position of imam ab an fah may allah have mercy on him is that sharecropping muz ra ah is not permissible but his two companions may allah have mercy on them hold that it is permissible and in the hanafi school the fatwa is given on the view of the two companions this arrangement is therefore permissible and correct sharecropping for a half a third or a quarter of the crop is likewise all permissible in the same way if no period has been fixed the arrangement is still permissible and correct according to the view on which the fatwa is given but it will then apply only to the first harvest consider the evidence for the permissibility of sharecropping

giving land on sharecropping without fixing a period a man gave his land to someone on a crop share basis that is on sharecropping but did not state whether it was for one year or for two is the sharecropping contract invalid or not and if it is valid for how long does it run in the case described fixing the period is a condition of sharecropping just like its other conditions so leaving the period entirely unknown invalidates the contract but if the period is determined by local custom such uncertainty does not invalidate it rather the sharecropping will run until the first crop is harvested consider what al hid yah records al in yah states taby n al aq iq states sha

some forms of sharecropping and their rulings i have read in a booklet that the following forms of sharecropping are permissible and the rest are not 1 the land belongs to one party and everything else the seed the tractor the labour belongs to the other this is permissible 2 the land and the seed belong to one party and the labour and the tractor to the other or the land and the tractor belong to one party and the labour and the seed to the other this too is permissible nowadays however a great deal of expense goes into working land and so the custom and practice is that the land belongs to the owner the labour is the cultivator's and the two share the seed the tractor and the pesticides between them can this as a rule the hanafi jurists may allah have mercy on them have declared only four forms of sharecropping to be permissible ibn bid n al sh m may allah have mercy on him and others however have set out further permissible forms besides these and ibn bid n also stated that there is no single comprehensive rule in this matter within which all the permissible forms of sharecropping can be confined the upshot is that sharecropping turns essentially on custom and common practice it was on the basis of common practice that imam ab y suf may allah have mercy on him declared some conditions permissible which on the standard transmitted position invalidate the contract on this

cultivating someone else's land if a person cultivates another man's land without permission or by force whose will the crop be and what will the cultivator receive 1 if that land is set aside for sharecropping cultivation on a share of the crop and the cultivator's share is known by custom then it is a sharecropping arrangement 2 if his share is not known and varies from case to case then it comes under the ruling of usurpation so if any damage has been done to the land compensation is due if no damage has been done the usurper is not liable the owner may however claim rent for the period of use 3 as for the grain and produce that the cultivator has obtained by putting seed into that land he is permitted to use as much as he himself put in and it is necessary for him to give the rest away in charity

the sharia ruling on an orchard tending partnership zayd employed umar at a salary of three thousand rand a month to look after his orchard to water it and so on but the man was negligent in caring for the orchard and it did not bear fruit as it should have because all he was concerned about was his own salary zayd now wants to know whether there is any arrangement other than employing a man on wages in which the worker gains and he gains as well in the case described the remedy the sacred law provides for making good such a loss is mus q t an orchard tending partnership mus q t means handing over one's trees or orchard to someone else so that he may water them look after them and bring them to a state in which they bear more fruit on the agreed condition that a fixed share of the fruit produced will be given to him as his wage according to the view on which the fatwa is given this arrangement is permissible and correct in the sharia the prophet made this very arrangement with the people of khaybar on this basis in the case described zayd should tell the man you are to tend the orchard water it and so on and you w

facing the qiblah at the time of slaughter at the time of slaughter is it necessary for the slaughterer and the animal to face the qiblah or is it an emphasised sunnah or merely recommended and what is the position of the other imams on this matter please explain in detail in the anaf school there are two positions regarding the slaughterer and the animal facing the qiblah according to the research of some jurists all mah al sh m all mah sayyid a mad al a w and others it is an emphasised sunnah while according to others such as all mah ab bakr al k s n the author of bad i al an i it is recommended shaykh al isl m q al qu t ab al asan al al sughd may allah have mercy on him the author of al nutaf f al fat w counts facing the qiblah among the etiquettes of slaughter consider the following passages shiyat al a w al al durr states

the doubt that sacrifice is obligatory on the basis of the noble verse is sacrifice obligatory or necessary the noble verse requires that sacrifice be obligatory because is an imperative form and an imperative requires obligation why then is it held to be merely necessary if a noble verse is definitive in its transmission and definitive in its indication then an obligation is established from it as with but if the noble verse is open to interpretation that is definitive in transmission but speculative in indication then necessity is established from it and the noble verse is open to interpretation some have taken to mean placing the hands upon the chest in prayer although that report is not sound this report is transmitted from a rat al may allah be pleased with him but all mah m rd n declared it weak in al jawhar al naq it is also transmitted from ibn abb s may allah be pleased with him

qurb n becoming w jib upon a woman on account of her jewellery a girl has a pair of earrings equal to one tol of gold and she also has 300 rand if those earrings are converted into silver and the three hundred rand are added to them the ni b will be complete and qurb n will become w jib but in order to make the qurb n she will have to sell the earrings is qurb n therefore w jib upon her or not and if silver is not taken as the standard but the two are combined by their parts amm bi al ajz is that correct or not what does amm bi al ajz mean has any jurist given a fatw on it or not the jurists generally write that silver will be taken as the standard because that is more beneficial to the poor on this basis qurb n will be w jib upon the girl mentioned provided that adding the gold to the rand makes up the ni b of silver this is the well known position of the anaf s some respected muft s however incline to the view that the combining should be by parts amm bi al ajz which is the position of ibayn and on that basis qurb n will not be w jib upon the girl mentioned muft kh lid sayf all h ra m n and muft ghul m q dir incline to this view some muft s have also taken gold as the standard but nowadays the price of gold is so high that taking it as t

whether qurb n is w jib upon a minor child if a minor child owns the ni b is qurb n w jib upon him or not and is qurb n w jib upon his father on his behalf or not according to the preponderant view upon which fatw is given qurb n is not w jib upon a minor child and likewise it is not w jib upon his father or his guardian and the like on his behalf all mah sh m may allah have mercy on him however has quoted from q kh n may allah have mercy on him the view that it is recommended see al durr al mukht r which states

performing qurb n on a husband's behalf without his permission a woman performed her husband's w jib qurb n without his permission was the w jib qurb n discharged or not and was the qurb n of the other shareholders valid or not when performing qurb n on someone else's behalf the best and preferable course is that it be done with express permission prior permission or customary permission however is also sufficient therefore in the case in question since customary permission was present the qurb n performed on the husband's behalf was discharged see fat w sh m which states fat w q kh n states

whether the sacrifice is necessary upon every member of the household is the sacrifice necessary upon every owner of the nisab in a household or upon one senior person if it is necessary upon all of them will the obligation be discharged on behalf of them all by one person offering a sacrifice or not the sacrifice is necessary w jib upon every free resident muslim who owns the nisab even if there are several people in one house if all of them own the nisab then just as with adaqat al fi r the sacrifice will be necessary upon all of them and the obligation will not be discharged on behalf of them all by one person offering a sacrifice however if all the sons bring their earnings and give them to the father and individually they do not own the nisab but only the father does then the sacrifice will be binding on the father alone see the noble hadith which states

when one of the shareholders intends a missed sacrifice in a sacrificial animal one man intended this year's sacrifice and another intended last year's sacrifice has the sacrifice been valid or not has it been valid for both of them or for neither of them or for one and not for the other in the case asked about the sacrifice of the one who intended this year's sacrifice has been fulfilled and the sacrifice of the one who intended last year's has been fulfilled as a voluntary sacrifice the missed sacrifice has not been made up he must therefore give the price of a goat in charity and the whole meat of the sacrifice must also be given away in charity see fat w q kh n which states

sacrificing on behalf of the owners without specifying the animals if an institution or a bank offers the sacrifice of a hundred animals on behalf of a hundred men but does not specify that this animal is zayd's and this one amr's will the sacrifices be valid or not in the case asked about the institution or the bank buys the animals in the capacity of an agent and then offers the sacrifice on behalf of the owners it is not necessary for an agent at the time of buying to specify on whose behalf he is buying nor is it necessary at the time of offering the sacrifice to call out each person's name separately or to designate a particular animal for each one the sacrifices will be fulfilled on behalf of them all it is not necessary for an agent to make a specification on behalf of his principal at the time of buying see the proofs of this point

sacrificing three cows without specifying the shareholders twenty one men together offered the sacrifice of three cows but they did not specify which seven persons were sharing in which cow have the sacrifices been fulfilled or not the intention of offering the sacrifice is enough it is not necessary to fix the shares for each one on this basis in the case asked about the sacrifices have been fulfilled on behalf of all of them it is however preferable and better that in future the seven persons sharing in each large animal be specified see imd d al a k m which states question if fourteen men share in two cows and offer the sacrifice in such a way that each one's share is not fixed in a particular cow and it is not said that this cow is for seven persons and the other cow for the other seven but rather it is said that both these cows are jointly on behalf of the fourteen persons will the sacrifice be val

slaughtering each other's animals by mistake m s and s both bought two goats and each designated one for himself then by mistake m s slaughtered the goat designated by s and s slaughtered m s 's goat have the sacrifices of both of them been valid or not or is it binding on them to offer them again since both of them bought two goats for themselves and designated them for the sacrifice the sacrifices have been fulfilled on behalf of both of them and each of them will be regarded as having acted as a helper for the other see al mu al burh n which states al maws ah al fiqhiyyah al kuwaytiyyah

when one of the shareholders intends the meat if one of the shareholders intends the meat will the sacrifice of his companions be valid or not this although eating the meat of the sacrifice is recommended and desirable in the sharia which is the very reason why it is desired that the sacrificial animal be fat why then is intending the meat blameworthy when people generally do intend the meat as well in the books of fiqh one generally finds the statement that if one of the shareholders intends the meat the sacrifice is not fulfilled but the meaning of this statement is that such a man offers the sacrifice merely to obtain meat and does not regard it as necessary or as an act of worship if a man while regarding it as an act that earns reward wishes the meat to be good and of better quality that is correct and is desired in the sharia otherwise the fact that a fat plump animal is desired and enjoined in the hadiths and the books of fiqh would be pointless j mi al tirmidh states

a poor man substituting the sacrificial animal a poor man bought a sacrificial animal on the first of dh al ijjah and afterwards on account of some need wishes to sell it may he sell this animal or not and is the sacrifice binding upon him because he bought it or not if a poor man bought the sacrificial animal before the days of sacrifice he is permitted to substitute it but if he bought it during the days of sacrifice he is now not permitted to substitute it nor is he permitted to use it for any other purpose yes if some genuinely pressing need arises he may substitute a sacrificial animal bought during the days of sacrifice see shar al in yah which states

selling shares in the sacrifice at more than the purchase price a man bought a sacrificial animal for seven thousand rand intending that if other companions were found he would take them as partners in this large animal and keep the seventh share for himself as it happened six men were found now if this man sells the remaining six shares to his companions for a sum higher than his purchase price instead of for six thousand will this be permissible or not for example if he sells the six shares for seven or eight thousand no explicit ruling on the question mentioned above has come to my notice nevertheless its ruling may be derived from a parallel case in fiqh namely that one should not do this and if someone has done it he should give the extra money away in charity see fat w q kh n which states

taking a partner after the sacrificial animal has been bought six men bought a cow with the intention of sacrifice then an old woman begged and pleaded to be taken in as a partner as well can she be made a partner after the cow has been bought or not if at the time of buying there was the intention that another would be taken as a partner it is permissible without any dislikedness and if there was no such prior intention it is permissible but contrary to what is preferable see fat w q kh n which states bad i al an i states

the ruling on performing the sacrifice on the thirteenth of dh al ijjah how many are the days of sacrifice where we live some of the ghayr muqallids perform the sacrifice on the fourth day of eid is it permissible and valid to perform the sacrifice on the fourth day in the case asked about the position of the anaf s the m lik s and the anbal s is that the days of sacrifice are three the day of sacrifice and the two days after it that is the 10th 11th and 12th of dh al ijjah and that the sacrifice is not permissible on the 13th of dh al ijjah in the view of the sh fi s however the sacrifice is permissible on the thirteenth of dh al ijjah as well that is the days of sacrifice are four as for the ghayr muqallid he has no school at all the position of all mah ibn taymiyyah may allah have mercy on him and fi ibn al qayyim may allah have mercy on him is however the same as that of im m sh fi may allah have mercy on him
