the ruling on sacrificing a usurped goat a man usurped someone's goat and then sacrificed it now if the owner gives him permission has the sacrifice on behalf of the usurper been fulfilled or not has the obligation been discharged from his liability or not and if it has been fulfilled how seeing that here the permission relates to something that no longer exists in the case asked about if the owner holds him liable for the value of the goat while alive then this sacrifice has been fulfilled on behalf of the usurper although he bears the sin of usurpation or theft as for the point that the goat had already been slaughtered so that the permission relates to something that no longer exists which is void the answer is that by paying the compensation the usurper became the owner of that goat and since the cause of the obligation to compensate is the usurpation the payment of compensation is attributed back to the time of the usurpation the meaning of this is that the usurper became owner at the time of the usurpation and the slaughter took p

the ruling on sacrificing a stolen goat if someone stole an animal and sacrificed it and afterwards regretted it and conveyed its price to the owner has his sacrifice now been valid or not some scholars say that in the books of fiqh one finds the case of usurpation that if a person pays compensation after sacrificing a usurped animal the sacrifice is valid but that the case of theft is not found could you please provide a reference for the case of theft in the case asked about the thief who slaughtered the animal paid the price of the stolen goat and for that reason his sacrifice has been fulfilled yes because he began a good deed with an act of disobedience repentance and seeking forgiveness are binding upon him the explicit reference for theft is given below all mah ibn al shi nah al alab has written that the sacrifice is permissible in bad i a

the ruling on sacrificing a goat bought through an invalid sale a man buys an animal for sacrifice the seller who is a non muslim says very well but i shall fix the price when the animal has been slaughtered and the meat is then weighed i shall take the price according to that weight the buyer also agreed and having bought the animal he sacrificed it has the sacrifice been valid or not seeing that this sale was outwardly not valid in the case asked about since the price was not fixed in the sale this sale was invalid the ruling on an invalid sale is that as long as the item sold is still there it should be returned but where the item sold has perished the buyer became its owner by virtue of his taking possession and the sacrifice too was valid though the fair market value becomes due see fat w sh m which states shar al majallah states

the ruling on sacrificing a deer a man wishes to offer a deer as a sacrifice and as an aq qah may a deer be offered as a sacrifice or as an aq qah or not the animals for sacrifice and for aq qah are fixed apart from these no other wild animal may be offered as a sacrifice or an aq qah the sacrificial animals are the following the camel male and female the cow and the bull the buffalo male and female the goat male and female the sheep and the lamb only these animals may validly be sacrificed so a deer may not be offered as a sacrifice or as an aq qah and if an animal is of mixed parentage the mother is what counts if the mother is domestic a goat or a cow for example the sacrifice is permissible otherwise not bad i al an i states

the most excellent and best animal for sacrifice which animal is better for the sacrifice a male or a female and is a share in a large animal better or is a small animal without sharing more excellent for sacrificial animals it is better and recommended that they be fat and well grown handsome of the most wholesome flesh and free of any defect that would make them appear ugly to the eye in a large animal however the female is more excellent without qualification among small animals the castrated male is more excellent and if there is no castrated male then the female is more excellent moreover the sacrifice of a small animal is more excellent than a seventh share in a large animal provided the small animal is fat well grown and of good quality bad i al an i states

the ruling on sacrificing a cow less than two years old if a cow is to be sacrificed it must have completed two years but if a cow younger than two years is fat and well grown so that it appears equal to a two year old is its sacrifice valid or not in the shar ah the sacrifice of a cow less than two years old is not valid yes in the case of a lamb there is this concession if a six month old lamb appears equal to a one year old its sacrifice is valid a narration in a muslim states cow more than two years old

the ruling on the teeth of a sacrificial animal if a cow is to be sacrificed is one with two teeth sufficient or not how many teeth must it have the ages of sacrificial animals are fixed a cow must have completed two full years and the teeth are not the criterion so long as it can eat its grass and fodder properly yes if it cannot eat grass and fodder properly then its sacrifice is not permissible al hid yah states bad i al an i states

the ruling on sacrificing an animal with a broken horn nowadays it is common practice among farmers to pull out the horns of their animals from the root the reason being that they keep animals in large numbers and there is a strong fear of their attacking one another and in particular a good deal of difficulty is faced in taking them to the abattoir so is the sacrifice of such hornless animals valid or not animals that have no horns at all or whose horns have broken may validly be sacrificed yes if the horns have broken off at the root or have been pulled out from the root and the effect of this has reached the brain then the sacrifice of such animals is not permissible or valid bad i al an i states

the ruling when a horn breaks off at the root at the time of slaughter a sacrificial animal ran away at the time of slaughter and its horn broke off at the root will the sacrifice of such an animal be valid or not if a disqualifying defect befalls an animal at the time of slaughter its sacrifice is permissible so in the case in question the sacrifice of an animal whose horn broke off at the root at the time of slaughter will be permissible and sound because avoiding such a thing is impossible al hid yah states majma al anhur states

the ruling on sacrificing an animal that has no ears from birth is it permissible to sacrifice an animal that has no ears from birth or no tail from birth or not and what is the ruling on the sacrifice of an animal whose ear has been cut the well known position and the one on which fatwa is given is that the sacrifice of an animal which has no ears or no tail from birth is not permissible there is however a report from im m ab an fah may allah have mercy on him that if the ear or the tail is absent from birth the sacrifice of that animal is permissible and sound so if someone has already offered such a sacrifice in the light of this report he will not be ordered to repeat it and if more than a third of the ear has been cut off its sacrifice is not permissible where less than that has been cut off there is scope fat w sh m states

the ruling on sacrificing an animal whose ears are small from birth if an animal's ears are very small from birth is its sacrifice permissible or not the sacrifice of an animal whose ears are small from birth is permissible and sound al durr al mukht r states al fat w al lamg riyyah states fat w ra miyyah states the sacrifice of an animal whose ears are small from birth is permissible

sacrificing an animal that is sharq or kharq the noble hadith forbids the sacrifice of an animal that is sharq or kharq yet in the view of the jurists there is scope for sacrificing such an animal if less than a half or a third has been cut off is this statement of the jurists not contrary to the hadith consider the noble hadith the reports quoted above show that it is not permissible to sacrifice an animal that is kharq or sharq these reports however are unelaborated while the hadith of a rat qat dah may allah have mercy on him is explanatory in it we are told that an animal half or more of whose ear has been cut off may not be sacrificed whereas if less than half has been cut off the sacrifice of that animal is va

sacrificing an animal whose tail has been docked here in south africa the tails of most fat tailed sheep are cut off after birth and the experts say that if the tail is left there is a strong likelihood of a particular disease or of jaundice weakness and the like the matters we wish to ask about are as follows 1 if a fat tailed sheep whose tail has been docked has reached the required age is it permissible to sacrifice it or not 2 the jurists have written that it is impermissible is this ruling based on a text or have they declared it impermissible by reckoning it a defect whereas here in south africa it is not a defect 3 after the sheep has grown it does not appear to have a docked tail to ordinary observation it se 1 on this question the views of the muftis of the present age differ most of them in the light of the passages of the jurists hold it impermissible some however say that in view of the local conditions and climate here this practice is not reckoned a defect but is regarded as making for better health therefore taking into account general custom and the opinion of qualified experts it should not be reckoned a defect and there ought to be scope for sacrificing an animal whose tail has been docked indeed the sacrifice of an animal with a docked tail is mentioned in the hadith and no limit is stated there as to how much of it may be cut off even so the cautious course is that if

sacrificing an animal whose teats are damaged if one or two of an animal's teats are defective may it be sacrificed or not if the animal is one with four teats a cow a buffalo or a she camel for example and one of its teats is defective the sacrifice is permissible but if two teats are defective the sacrifice is not permissible if it is an animal with two teats a goat or a sheep for example and one of its teats is defective the sacrifice is not permissible likewise if more than a third of a single teat is defective it is not permissible either consider what fat w sh m states

sacrificing a cow that has lost one teat one of a cow's teats has fallen off and three remain in this case will the sacrifice be permissible or not the sacrifice of a cow that has lost one teat or one of whose teats is defective is permissible and correct if however two teats are missing or defective the sacrifice is not valid consider what all mah ibn al shi nah al alab writes in lis n al ukk m f ma rifat al a k m fat w d r al ul m deoband states if a cow has lost one teat its sacrifice is valid

sacrificing a cow that has no milk in three of its teats a man bought a milk cow for sacrifice three of this cow's teats have no milk in them and one teat has milk is the sacrifice of this cow valid or not it appears from the passages of the jurists that if no milk comes into a cow's teat and this is not because of any disease but the milk has simply stopped without any cause then the sacrifice of such a cow is permissible but if the milk in two or more of the cow's teats has stopped because of some disease then the sacrifice of such a cow is impermissible accordingly in the case in question if no milk comes into three of the cow's teats without any cause or disease the sacrifice is valid but if it is so because of some disease then it is not permissible or correct to sacrifice this cow consider what khul at al fat w states

sacrificing an animal whose milk has dried up without any illness the milk in a goat's teats has dried up and it had not been afflicted by any illness or anything of the sort is the sacrifice of such an animal valid or not if the milk has dried up without any illness or disease the sacrifice of this animal will be permissible consider what fat w sh m records al fat w al lamg riyyah states

sacrificing a pregnant animal a man bought an animal for sacrifice and afterwards found out that it was pregnant should it be slaughtered or not that is what is the ruling on sacrificing a pregnant animal if the time of the pregnant animal's giving birth is not very close the sacrifice is valid slaughtering an animal that is close to giving birth however is disliked consider what fat w sh m states khul at al fat w states

money left over from a patient's treatment fund after his death a man was suffering from a fatal illness and a large sum was needed for his treatment a collection was made for this and friends acquaintances and relatives gave generously all this money was transferred into the patient's account and was spent on his treatment as the need arose until the patient died what should now be done with the money that is left over must it be returned to the donors or will it be included in the deceased's estate in the case described the donors paid the money into the patient's account intending it as charity so the patient became the owner of all of it now after his death it will form part of his estate and will be divided among all the sharia heirs according to the shares fixed by the sharia it is not obligatory or necessary to return it to the donors they have already earned the reward of their charity and their gift see what a hadith states

claiming blood money from the government for a killing carried out by the government in 1971 a man was unlawfully killed this year the court held an inquiry and it came to light that the south african police that is the government had killed him can his heirs now demand blood money from the government if the government pays the blood money how is it to be divided among the heirs and if the government pays more than the amount of the blood money will it be permissible to take the extra or not an unlawful killing by the government comes under deliberate homicide and the ruling for that is that retaliation is due from the killer in the case in question however it is difficult to demand retaliation from the government and the killer himself is not known and identified either so it is correct to demand blood money when the government pays the blood money it will be divided among all the sharia heirs of the victim those who were alive at the time he was killed according to the shares fixed by the sharia if the government pays something more it is likewise permissible and correct to take it see what a hadith states

a second wife waiving her right of inheritance before the marriage a man wants to marry a second time in secret because his first wife is not willing for him to marry again but since a share will be taken out for the second wife when the estate is divided after his death everyone will then come to know that he had married again the woman has therefore said that she does not want any inheritance and has also said i promise that after your death i shall make no claim at all to my right in the estate can the second wife waive her right in the estate now before the marriage in the sacred sharia the right of inheritance is established only after death so how can a right that has not yet been established be waived once the right is established after death it will indeed lapse if it is then given up for the present nothing more than a promise can be made and it is to be fulfilled after the death see what al bin yah records

inheriting unlawfully acquired wealth a man's father had unlawfully acquired wealth after his death may his heirs take this wealth or not that is does inheritance run in unlawful wealth or not in the case described if an heir knows for certain of a particular item that it was obtained by unlawful means he is obliged to hand that very item over to its owner it is not permissible for him to take it as part of the inheritance but if he does not know for certain of a particular item that it was obtained wrongfully and knows only that the deceased used to acquire money by every means interest bribery and the rest while he also had lawful ways of earning and the lawful ways predominated then because the wealth is mixed and the unlawful part cannot be identified inheritance will run in the whole of it it is nevertheless better if the heirs by mutual agreement give some p

zakat on jointly held inherited property before the estate is divided a man died five years ago and his property has still not been divided further money of his keeps arriving from time to time along with profits from a bank and from a company the heirs can receive the inheritance only once the lawyers have completed all the formalities and had them approved by the court my question is who is to pay the zakat on this money and for how long a period must it be paid in the case described if the estate has not been divided among the heirs and none of them has yet taken possession of his share or is deriving any kind of profit from it then in that case zakat is not obligatory or binding on any of the heirs in respect of the jointly held inherited property if however one of them is receiving profit of some kind from the inherited property then in that case zakat is obligatory on his share provided that his share reaches the zakat threshold on the rest zakat is not obligatory see what all mah al sarakhs may allah have mercy on him says

the cost of dividing jointly held estate property some time ago a man died his estate includes a great deal of wealth land properties and houses the division among the heirs was carried out through lawyers and three hundred thousand rand was spent on the process the question now is this will the expense deducted from the estate be borne in proportion to the heirs' shares or will it be divided by the number of heirs for example if the deceased leaves three sons two daughters and a wife will the expense of three hundred thousand rand be divided equally among these six persons so that each bears 50 000 or will it be borne in proportion to their shares so that the wife bears one eighth and the sons and daughters bear it in the case described the cost of dividing the jointly held property three hundred thousand rand will be borne equally by the six persons see what al hid yah records majma al anhur f shar multaq al ab ur states

using dirty impure water after it has been filtered these days dirty water is filtered by chemical means and used again so that it looks even cleaner than fresh water to filter it the dirty water is passed through the following four stages 1 sedimentation in this process the water is collected in a large tank so that all the filth settles to the bottom 2 the clean water on the surface is strained off 3 the bacteria present in this water are killed by chemicals 4 chlorine is used to prevent the bacteria from forming again according to the experts after these stages no trace of impurity remains in the colour smell or taste of the water what we wish to know is this will such water be regarded as pure in the sharia and can on the above question the scholars fall into two groups 1 one group says that after filtration the water becomes pure and that its use is therefore permissible and correct this is the view of most of the arab scholars 2 the second group says that after filtration the water becomes clean but does not become pure this second view accords with the temper of the sharia and the fatwa of our elders may allah have mercy on them is also on it see what ni m al fat w records question the substance of the question is this if the putrid and harmful constituents of urine are distilled out by a machine and removed so that it becomes like water just as sea water is changed from salty

how to purify cloth dyed with an impure dye a man dyed some clothes green the cloth dried and took the colour and it later came to light that the dye was impure now that the cloth has taken a fast colour what is the way to make it pure on the above question the scholars hold three views 1 the cloth becomes pure by being washed three times whether the colour comes out or not 2 the cloth should be washed until clean water drips from it that is until no trace of the dye is left in the water this second view is the stronger one and the fatwa is on it 3 the cloth should be washed three times after clean water begins to drip from it consider the evidence al mu aqqiq ibn al hum m may allah have mercy on him says

the purity of the placental membrane and the ruling on using it the mash mah is the membrane in which a baby is wrapped in its mother's womb and which comes out with the baby at the time of birth is it impure or not whether it is from an animal that has been slaughtered or has come out after a miscarriage or has come out in a natural birth is it permissible to eat the mash mah or not and is its external use in order for instance in cosmetics in creams applied to the body in shampoo and so on according to the hanafis the membrane of a cow or a goat is pure and lawful and its use whether internal or external is therefore permissible and correct in the hanafi school of the limbs and parts of an animal slaughtered in accordance with the sharia a goat a cow and the like all may be eaten apart from seven only seven parts may not be eaten and they are the blood that flows out the genitals the two testicles the glands the bladder the gall bladder and the male organ the mash mah is not one of these parts so its internal use is permissible see the report in mu annaf abd al razz q

washing clothes in a washing machine if a large number of clothes are washed together in a washing machine pure and impure ones mixed together will all these clothes become pure or not washing machines nowadays are built in such a way that clothes come out of them completely clean and pure the details are these in the first stage the machine applies soap to the clothes and loosens the impurity in the second stage it washes them with water in the third stage it rinses them clean with fresh water and then it cleans them thoroughly by rinses and spins after passing through these stages the clothes become pure water is used more than three times and the wringing out is done as well consider the evidence and the supporting texts from the books of fiqh on the cleaning of clothes

how to purify a household water tank or cistern in most cities today it is usual to have a pipe system for bringing water into the bathrooms and other parts of a house the arrangement is that the municipal water is collected in one place in a tank or cistern and is then sent by a hand pump to the various parts of the house the question is this if such a tank which is generally far smaller than the ten by ten cubits of a large pool becomes impure what is the way to purify it a rat muft mu ammad shaf may allah have mercy on him says if impurity falls into the cistern below or the tank above at a time when its water is running on both sides for instance the municipal water is coming into the tank and going out by the other pipe to the various parts of the house then in the view of most of the jurists this tank will not become impure at all since it has the ruling of flowing water if the cistern or tank is not running on both sides but is closed on both sides or on one of them then it will become impure when impurity falls into it the way to purify it is then as follows if the impurity that has fallen in has body and substance it should first

cleaning the ears the sharia instructs us to keep our clothes clean and our hair clean is anything mentioned in any narration about cleaning the ears or not along with the cleaning of clothes and hair the sacred sharia also instructs us to remove the dirt and grime from the ears and to keep them clean the commentators on hadith have stated this in their commentaries see what all mah badr al d n al ayn may allah have mercy on him says in his commentary on sunan ab d w d imam al nawaw may allah have mercy on him says in his commentary on a muslim

the reward for performing ablution without making an intention if a person performs ablution but does not make the intention for ablution will he receive the reward of ablution or not according to the hanafis making an intention in ablution is a sunnah if ablution is performed with the intention of ablution the reward will be received otherwise it will not see what imd d al fatt states ghamz uy n al ba ir

using a filter made from animal bones vessels for filtering water are made from the bones of various animals and this is the method used by some companies is it permissible in the sharia to keep water in such a vessel or to drink from it or not with the exception of human beings and pigs the bones of all animals are pure and it is permissible and correct to use a filter made from them the reason is that if the animal was slaughtered its purity is obvious and if it died of itself death does not enter the bones since there is no life in them see what al hid yah states

using water heated by a solar geyser the use of solar geysers for heating water has become common these days instead of electricity this geyser heats the water by the sun is its use in order or not given that a hadith has come forbidding the use of water heated by the sun it is permissible and correct to use water heated by a solar geyser which is a modern way of heating water in the view of most of the scholars of hadith the hadith narrated in prohibition of it is weak or else belongs to what is merely contrary to the preferable course strict dislike or prohibition cannot be derived from it consider the statements of the jurists

performing tayammum on a wall covered with oil paint if a wall has been coated with oil paint is it permissible to perform tayammum on it or not tayammum is permissible on everything that is of the genus of the earth and that neither burns when it is put in fire nor melts when it is heated oil paint is not of the genus of the earth and it does melt when heated moreover a layer of oil paint forms on the wall which prevents the hand from reaching the wall itself for this reason tayammum on a wall coated with oil paint is not permissible or valid see what al durr al mukht r states

facing the qiblah during marital relations what is the ruling on facing the qiblah or turning one's back towards it at the time of intercourse with one's wife in the urdu fatwa collections the view generally reported is that it is disliked all mah al a w may allah have mercy on him however has said that there is no dislike in facing the qiblah at the time of intercourse it merely falls under what is contrary to the preferable course it may nevertheless be said that when facing the qiblah is forbidden in the case of the lesser impurity that is urinating and relieving oneself then it ought all the more to be forbidden in the case of the greater impurity which makes a ritual bath necessary see what al a w writes in his marginal notes

bleeding that occurs after the womb has been removed if a woman's womb has been removed and after some days she notices spots of blood what is the ruling that is will it be counted as menstruation or not the blood that comes from a woman's womb during her particular days is called menstruation but once the womb has been removed it will not be counted as menstruation it is rather isti ah irregular bleeding see what multaq al ab ur states majma al anhur states

being in a state of ablution when entering the mosque is it obligatory or necessary to be in a state of ablution in order to enter a mosque being in a state of ablution in order to enter a mosque is neither obligatory nor necessary it is recommended if however a muslim is in a state of major ritual impurity then a ritual bath is necessary for him and it is forbidden and impermissible for him to enter the mosque without it see what fat w al sh m states bad i al an i records q m s al fiqh states among the cases in which performing ablution is recommended is doing so for the purpose of entering a mosque

ablution and the ritual bath when a special substance has been applied to the hair nowadays a special kind of substance is used to treat the hair which sets it firm in english it is called brasil cacau keratin it generally remains for up to three months and there is no easy way of removing it what then is the ruling regarding the purity ablution ritual bath prayer and so on of those who use it is its use permissible or not in the case in question if a layer forms from this substance like a plaster then according to the well known view held by the majority of the scholars it is a barrier to ablution and the ritual bath ablution and the bath will therefore not be valid without removing it and for that reason the prayer too will not be valid according to some scholars however if there is hardship in removing it the ablution and the bath will be valid its ruling is like that of nail polish but if no layer like a plaster forms and it is rather like the colour of henna then in no one's view is its removal necessary in any case one ought to avoid using such doubtful things see what al durr al mukht r s

the ruling on using shampoo that contains impure ingredients these days all sorts of products are being manufactured for washing the hair shampoo cream soap and so on sometimes they contain ingredients taken from animals that were not slaughtered according to the sharia or from pigs is it correct to use such products for washing one's head or one's clothes or not the disposition of the sharia is that one should keep away from doubtful items of this kind however if nothing else is available and there is a genuine need to use them then the ruling is that once the reality and essence of an impure substance has changed its former ruling no longer applies to it a change of reality means that the original substance and its identity are altered completely or that its distinguishing properties no longer remain experience has shown that in shampoo soap cream and the like the impure ingredients lose their original reality on that basis their use is permitted consider what fat al qad r records

the ruling on taking non muslim schoolchildren around a mosque for the purpose of da wah and tabl gh is it permissible to take non muslim schoolchildren around a mosque or not and is it permissible to bring men and women among whom there may also be non muslim women who are menstruating in the case in question the better and preferable course is to make the arrangements in the mosque courtyard outside the boundaries of the mosque proper and to present the invitation to islam there but if it is necessary to bring them into the mosque then non muslims may enter it so long as no outward impurity is known of them and so long as there is no fear of any other harm mischief or trial a screen should then be arranged between the men and the women in the same way a non muslim man in a state of major ritual impurity and a non muslim woman who is menstruating may all enter the mosque so long as their bodies are not soiled with any visible impurity consider what al ba r al r

evidence from the qur'an and hadith for reciting supplications in a toilet with a closed lid a scholar stated the following ruling that if the lid of a pedestal toilet is closed the remembrances prescribed for ablution may be recited inside it a student then asked him whether there is any evidence for this in the qur'an and hadith he said that he would look into it and let him know if there is any evidence for it in the qur'an the hadith and fiqh please write it out consider first the evidence from the qur'an when y nus peace be upon him was in the belly of the fish he supplicated for his deliverance and that supplication is recorded in the qur'an there is filth inside the belly of a fish yet he kept up the remembrance of allah in its very presence this shows that y nus peace be upon him supplicated close to filth but because the filth was covered over the supplication was in order now consider the evidence from the hadith

the ruling on wiping over leather socks when the zip has come open if the zip of khuffayn that is leather socks has been left open is the wiping over them invalidated or not will the ablution have to be repeated if the zip has come open above the ankles there is no harm in it if it has come open below them and the extent of three toes of the foot is visible while walking then the wiping is invalidated consider what shar munyat al mu all states bihisht zewar record

the ruling on wiping when two socks are worn one over the other if a man has put on two socks together one over the other may he wipe over the upper one or not and if he wipes over the upper one and then takes it off will it be necessary to wipe over the lower one again or not in the case in question it is the upper sock that counts for the wiping if the upper sock is taken off it will be necessary to wipe over the lower one again consider what bad i al an i states al mas il states if a person puts on two leather socks together it is the upper sock that counts so if he has wiped over t

the ruling on blood seen before childbirth a woman was pregnant in the morning before giving birth she saw blood after that no blood appeared and then she gave birth at night during that interval she did not perform the zuhr asr maghrib and ish prayers was it correct for her to leave those prayers and is she now required to make them up or not a pregnant woman does not menstruate because pregnancy closes the mouth of the womb and the blood that comes after childbirth is called nif s post natal bleeding in the case in question therefore the blood that came before the birth is isti ah irregular bleeding which is no bar to prayer it was accordingly not correct for her to leave the prayers and now once she becomes pure from nif s she must make up the zuhr asr and maghrib prayers the ish prayer however does not have to be made up consider the narration in sunan al d rim

the ruling on wiping over a sock on one foot when the other foot is bandaged if a person has a bandage tied on one of his feet is it permissible for him to put a sock on the other foot and wipe over it or not in the case in question wiping over a splint or a bandage carries the ruling of washing whereas wiping over a leather sock or an ordinary sock does not carry the ruling of washing but is a substitute for it on that basis the two washing and wiping cannot be combined it is therefore not correct to wipe over the bandage on one foot and over the sock on the other foot rather the other sock must be taken off and the foot washed if however he wiped over the bandage and then put his socks on wiping over both socks is correct consider what al mu al burh n states

the ruling on wiping over socks that have been made waterproof with a spray i know the ruling that there are three conditions for wiping over leather socks 1 that water does not seep through them 2 that they stay in place of themselves without being fastened 3 that it is possible to walk continuously in them i also know that it is permissible to wipe over seal skinz but what about ordinary cotton socks through which water does seep if such socks are made waterproof by means of a spray will it be permissible to wipe over them or not this spray keeps water from penetrating for up to 24 hours it is clear from the statements of the jurists that for wiping to be valid the socks themselves must be made in such a way that the conditions mentioned are found in them the conditions must not be met by means of something external ordinary socks may therefore not be wiped over and a spray is an external thing so it is of no account consider what al durr al mukht r records imd d al fatt states

the ruling on fitting urinals to the walls at business premises at ordinary business premises and garages urinals are provided for people and are generally fixed to the walls for the most part it is non muslim men who use them in western style toilets too men urinate standing up is it permissible to build such toilets and urinals or not the natural and sunnah way of relieving oneself is to do so sitting down that is more comfortable more dignified and more modest and it also keeps one safe from splashes of urine urinating while standing on the other hand is contrary to decency contrary to the sunnah and disliked if there is a reasonable excuse however it is acceptable consider what al ba r al r iq states fat w al sh m states

the acts of worship a menstruating woman may perform which acts of worship may a menstruating woman perform and which may she not may she look at a copy of the qur'an and recite from memory may she recite the salutations upon the prophet may she supplicate for a menstruating woman prayer fasting performing aw f reciting the noble qur'an touching the qur'an and entering a mosque are all impermissible remembrance of allah the supplications that occur in the qur'an and the hadith reciting them with the intention of supplication and making supplication are all permissible a menstruating woman who teaches may also teach a verse by breaking it up as she goes she may likewise recite certain verses of the noble qur'an for example with the intention of remembrance and supplication but with the intention of reciting the qur'an it is not permissible consider what al durr al mukht r states

what a woman should do if her menses begin while she is in the sacred mosque a woman is sitting in the sacred mosque when her menses begin and because of the great crowd it is difficult for her to get out immediately what should she do as soon as her menses begin a woman should leave the mosque if however leaving is difficult because of the crowd then out of necessity she should perform tayammum dry ablution and remain sitting where she is while continuing to try to get out as far as she is able this is like what the jurists have written concerning a man in a state of major ritual impurity if he has a wet dream in the mosque he should leave it at once but if there is danger in going out he may perform tayammum and remain in the mosque consider what is recorded in fat w al sh m

how a woman wipes her head in ablution what is the method by which a woman wipes her head the method by which women wipe the head is exactly the same as that of men there is no difference between the two the books of fiqh mention no separate method for women consider what fat w sh m states fat al qad r records for further detail see fat w d r al ul m zakariyy volume one p 680 bombay

the ruling on repeating prayers in which the head was not wiped during ablution after reaching puberty a girl never wiped her head whenever she performed ablution for prayer she did not know that wiping the head is also obligatory later she went to study at a madrasah and learnt of it is she now required to repeat all the prayers she has performed since reaching puberty or not in our time a muslim's being unaware of the obligations of islam is not an acceptable excuse because acquiring knowledge of the fundamentals of islam after reaching puberty is a matter of the greatest importance and necessity on that basis in the case in question it is binding and necessary to make up all the prayers from puberty onwards consider what al fat w al hindiyyah records states

the correct way of using the misw k is the misw k used lengthwise or crosswise is anything established about this in the hadith and what is written in the books of fiqh in the matter in question some weak narrations encourage using the misw k crosswise and some jurists have said lengthwise what the latter means however is using it lengthwise on the tongue since brushing the teeth lengthwise risks injuring the gums if there is no risk of injury then there is no harm in using it lengthwise either consider what im m sakh w may allah have mercy on him says in al maq id al asanah

the ruling on making do with tissue paper when the impurity exceeds the size of a dirham when non liquid impurity greater than the size of a dirham is present at the place of istinj which form of istinj is obligatory with water or with stones also what is meant by the size of a dirham its weight or its area and what is the ruling when the impurity is exactly the size of a dirham in the case in question if impurity greater than the size of a dirham is on the place of istinj then cleaning with water is necessary istinj with stones is not sufficient by the size of a dirham its weight is meant when the impurity is a solid substance if it is not solid then its area is meant impurity of exactly the size of a dirham is no bar though prayer with it will be disliked consider the following evidence

an examination of a hadith on the merit of ablution i would like a hadith examined what is the grading of this hadith this hadith is mentioned in a number of books and it is a asan hadith consider what fi ibn ajar may allah have mercy on him writes in it f al maharah almost every narrator of this report is reliable only one narrator amr n calls for discussion consider what im m dhahab writes in m z n al i tid l

an examination of the narration that laughing aloud in prayer breaks the ablution if a person laughs out loud during prayer his ablution is broken is this established from the hadith or not if it is established what is the grading of the hadith please give a reply with references a great many narrations have been reported concerning the breaking of ablution by laughing out loud in prayer some of them are mursal and some are weak im m d raqu n may allah have mercy on him after citing some forty eight hadith in his sunan discussed the chain of each one and im m zayla may allah have mercy on him traced all of these hadith in na b al r yah some of the narrations however are authentic consider what is recorded in sunan al d raqu n

the ruling on the ritual bath when urine is drawn off by catheter a woman had her urine drawn off by means of a catheter does this make a ritual bath necessary or not a catheter is a method of treatment in which a tube is inserted into the patient's private part and urine is drawn out through it this procedure does not make a ritual bath necessary the ablution however is broken because urine has come out consider what is recorded in al durr al mukht r with radd al mu t r fat w d

a toilet must face at least 45 degrees away from the direction of the qiblah if a person praying is within 45 degrees of the direction of the qiblah his prayer is valid that is 45 degrees is still reckoned as the direction of the qiblah so when a toilet is to be built will it likewise be necessary to build it more than 45 degrees away from the qiblah or will a slight turn away from the exact qiblah be enough to escape the warning the scholars have written that just as the validity of prayer depends on being within 45 degrees so too the 45 degrees will be taken into account when a toilet is built that is the toilet must face more than 45 degrees away from the direction of the qiblah otherwise the sin of having the toilet face the direction of the qiblah will be incurred consider what a bukh r shar f states al durr al mukht r states

the purity or impurity of snake venom and the ruling on using it i would like an investigation into snake venom is it pure or impure and is it permissible to use it or not will there be any difference between external and internal use snake venom is used in some medicines and in some cosmetics is it permissible to use such things or not the skin flesh and venom of a snake are all impure and their external and internal use is impermissible because venom combines three things impurity foulness and harm if however its reality and essence are altered by being put into medicines and these three things impurity foulness and harm are removed then the external and internal use of such medicines is permissible and correct consider what bad i al an i records

the ruling on using a cream made from snake venom these days snake venom is used in cosmetics and in various medicines for instance a cream is on sale in which snake venom is used it is applied to the face so that the signs of ageing do not show is it permissible to use such a cream or not in the view of the hanafis the snake is one of the forbidden animals and its venom is impure if its reality is not altered in a medicine then using it externally for the purpose of treatment when there is a need is in order but not otherwise in the case in question beautifying oneself is not a matter of need and so using an impure substance is neither permissible nor correct consider what fat w al sh m states

whether the prayer is invalidated when a verse is recited wrongly in the fajr prayer an imam in place of the noble verse of s rat al a l recited as follows was the prayer valid or not where one verse is recited in place of another during prayer the position is as follows if no corruption of the meaning results the prayer is by agreement valid and correct if a corruption of the meaning does result then the prayer is valid if he paused fully at the end of the first verse before reciting the second otherwise it is not on this basis in the case in question if the imam paused at and then recited the prayer was valid otherwise it was not consider what al durr al mukht r states

the prostration of recitation for one who hears the verse of prostration and joins in the second rak ah a man was performing ablution while the imam was reciting s rah alif l m m m al sajdah on friday morning he heard the verse of prostration over the loudspeaker and then joined the prayer in the second rak ah is the prostration of recitation due from him or not in the case in question the prostration of recitation is necessary for the man mentioned and he should perform it after the prayer if however he had heard the verse of prostration outside the prayer and joined in that same rak ah the imam's prostration would suffice for him and there would be no need to perform another consider what al hid yah states

the correct time for the ishr q prayer in south africa how many minutes after sunrise does the time for the ishr q prayer begin the time of ishr q begins once the sun has risen high enough that the eye cannot rest on it properly and this comes about ten minutes after sunrise the ishr q prayer should therefore be performed after ten or twelve minutes or to be on the safe side after fifteen or twenty minutes consider what umdat al q r records states

whether a delay in the prostration of recitation makes the prostration of forgetfulness necessary an imam recited a verse of prostration and did not prostrate at that moment he made the prostration after four or five verses did the prostration of forgetfulness become necessary or not what is the ruling on the prostration of recitation in the final rak ah and if an imam after making the prostration of recitation stood up and began s rat al f ti ah and then on being prompted began the recitation of a s rah is the prostration of forgetfulness necessary or not in the case in question on account of the long interval the more correct view is that the prostration of forgetfulness will be necessary by performing the prostration of forgetfulness the prayer will be valid likewise one should perform the prostration in whichever pillar of the prayer one remembers it as for the imam's having begun s rat al f ti ah after the prostration of recitation the prostration of forgetfulness is not necessary because the repetition of al f ti ah occurred after a s rah had been joined to it consider the proofs

performing two prostrations after reciting a verse of prostration a fi recited a verse of prostration in the prayer and performed two prostrations instead of one was the prayer valid or not in the case in question on account of the one additional prostration the prostration of forgetfulness became necessary the prayer will therefore be valid by performing the prostration of forgetfulness see what fat w hindiyyah states

repeating the prostration when a verse is repeated in the memorisation class in the memorisation class the students memorise their lesson in their own places and then go to the teacher to recite it to him will this come under the ruling of a change of sitting and will two prostrations be obligatory or one 2 when the teacher corrects a student how many prostrations become obligatory 3 if a student while revising his memorised portion takes a short break and goes off to drink water will this come under the ruling of a change of sitting or not 1 in the case in question if the place of the teacher and of the student is one then only one prostration will be obligatory upon both and moving two or three steps does no harm and if the places of the two are different then two prostrations will be obligatory 2 at the time of correcting and pointing out a mistake if most of the verse is recited along with the word of prostration the prostration will be obligatory otherwise not yes if in one sitting a person recites a verse of prostration and then hears that same verse from another as well even then one prostration will be obligatory 3 if while revising his memorised portion the student drinks a few sips of water while s

the ruling on the sunnah of uhr when because time was short only two rak ahs were prayed before it a man reached the mosque at such a time that only two minutes remained in which there was no room to pray four rak ahs so he prayed two rak ahs with the intention of the sunnah now have these two rak ahs taken the place of the sunnah of uhr or will he have to pray four rak ahs with the intention of the sunnah after the uhr prayer and if he omitted them because of haste will he be sinful or not the four rak ahs before uhr with a single sal m are an emphasised sunnah two rak ahs will not take their place yes if on some occasion such a thing happens because of some necessary work there will be no sin for omitting the sunnah but one should not make it a regular practice to make it one's habit to omit an emphasised sunnah without an excuse is sinful and blameworthy consider what al durr al mukht r states

further research on a newcomer joining a repeated congregation in the second volume of fat w d r al ul m zakariyy you wrote that concerning the participation of a newcomer in a repeated prayer there are two positions of the jurists 1 he may follow the imam this is the easier view 2 he may not follow the imam this is the more cautious view now i wish to know which of the two positions is stronger in terms of the proofs which position the majority of the jurists have preferred and which position is supported by the hadiths and the reports of the early generations kindly carry out the research it would be a great kindness in a repeated congregation where the repetition is on account of the omission of an obligatory element w jib the strong position concerning the participation of a newcomer and the preferred one in the view of the majority of the jurists is that he should not follow the imam because the discharge of the far was realised by the first prayer and the second congregation is in one respect supererogatory and in one respect obligatory in that it completes the far consider the following proofs and evidences first by way of corroboration and support consider the noble hadith

when some water comes into the mouth during prayer after eating a man ate before the maghrib prayer when he went into prostration during the prayer he belched and along with the belch some water came into his mouth he threw the water out to one side and continued with the prayer was the prayer valid or not if the water that came into the mouth came up from the stomach and was a mouthful then the ablution has broken and the prayer has been lost as well he should perform ablution and pray afresh but if it was not a mouthful or if it came from the throat and did not come up from the stomach then both the ablution and the prayer remain intact and there is no need to repeat them see what is recorded in al durr al mukht r

a way of passing in front of someone praying when there is no sutrah if a person wants to pass in front of someone who is praying and it is necessary for him to pass but there is no sutrah or anything of the sort can he stand in front of him and then move forward and pass explain and be rewarded passing in front of someone praying when there is no sutrah is a sin and is forbidden but if there is no sutrah and it is necessary to pass then he should stand with his back towards the person praying and then move forward and go on his way in fat al mulhim a rat mawl n shabb r a mad uthm n may allah have mercy on him writes i l al sunan states

the wisdom in performing acts of worship in the arabic language why are the acts of worship that muslims perform prayer recitation of the qur'an remembrance of allah supplications and so on in the arabic language why do they not perform them in their own national and local languages explain and be rewarded the arabic language possesses certain features that are not to be had in other languages if an attempt were made to perform the acts of worship in some other local language a very great difference would arise on account of which there would be a strong danger of distortion and alteration in the words and the meanings for example if is transferred into english it becomes and means heart while means dog furthermore arabic words are oceans of meaning a single word carries several meanings and this would no longer be preserved through translation into another language jaw hir al fiqh states as far as has been established by research many of the letters that exis

making a habit of praying fajr at home am i sinful for not praying the fajr prayer in the mosque i start my work at ten and work until eight i become very tired and do not go to the mosque for the fajr prayer because i am very lazy and do not want to cut down on my sleep so that my work should not suffer my question is am i sinful will i still get the same reward as praying in the mosque explain and be rewarded to leave the congregation in the mosque without a valid excuse recognised by the shar ah is to deprive oneself of an immense reward laziness and tiredness are no excuse for abandoning the congregation in the mosque so after repenting and seeking forgiveness make a point from now on of performing the fajr prayer in congregation in the mosque every day consider the merit of prayer in congregation prayer in congregation is twenty seven degrees better than praying alone other merits of praying in congregation in the mosque are mentioned in the hadiths as well

taking a pulpit to the eid prayer ground for the eid sermon some people say that taking a pulpit to the eid prayer ground is an innovation and that the sermon should be delivered without a pulpit is this correct and what is the ruling on taking a pulpit out to the open ground explain and be rewarded some hadiths show that the practice of the noble prophet in this matter varied sometimes he delivered the eid sermon from a pulpit sometimes without a pulpit and occasionally from some elevated spot on this basis taking a pulpit out to the open ground so that the preacher may deliver the sermon from it and the people may easily see him and hear the sermon is correct and permissible and it is not correct to call it an innovation consider a few hadiths and reports concerning the delivery of the eid sermon from the pulpit

delivering the friday sermon away from the pulpit an imam delivered the sermon on friday away from the pulpit from another side of the mosque some of the worshippers object to this the question is is delivering the sermon away from the pulpit in accordance with the practice of the prophet also what is the position regarding delivering the sermon from the pulpit on friday explain and be rewarded delivering the friday sermon from the pulpit is exactly in accordance with the practice of the noble prophet and of the rightly guided caliphs and it is the inherited practice of the muslim community on this basis the imam should deliver the sermon from the pulpit to leave the pulpit without any excuse is contrary to the sunnah accordingly in the view of most of the scholars delivering the sermon from the pulpit is a sunnah some scholars do say that sunnah here means recommended but then because of the inherited practice it stands above the merely recommended see what is stated in bukh r shar f

the ruling on astronomical calculation for prayer times and for establishing the new moon some people rely on the word of the astronomers in establishing the new moon and they say when their calculated timetables are relied upon for the times of prayer why are they not reliable for establishing the new moon is this analogy of theirs sound or not the sacred law has made the establishing of the new moon the basis for determining the islamic months and the establishing of the new moon depends on sighting it not on its mere existence the sacred law acknowledges the existence of the moon but it has made the establishing of the new moon rest upon sighting and there is a great difference between the two which the noble hadith has made clear that is if the new moon is veiled and cannot be seen then count thirty days of sha b n this shows that a thing that exists can be hidden from the eyes whereas for something non existent there is no sense in speaking of its being hidden using calendars and clocks by con

whether flying over one's own city by aeroplane makes one a resident if a person travelled by aeroplane from cape town to johannesburg and this person is a resident of johannesburg and the aeroplane flew over johannesburg and then landed at the airport has this person become a resident by flying over his own city or is he still a traveller explain and be rewarded it appears from the statements of the jurists that travel status is cancelled by entering one's own city and flying over a city is not called entering it for instance if a person flies over the city of durban it will not be said that so and so entered durban rather this is called entering its airspace furthermore the jurists call passing over a miq t or passing level with a miq t being in line with it mu dh t they do not call it entering the miq t in the same way passing overhead in an aeroplane is being in line with a city not entering it and travel status is cancelled only by entering one's own city see what the jurists write that entering the city cancels travel stat

the wisdom behind not praying at the time of sunrise and sunset al h is forbidden at the time of sunrise and sunset on account of resemblance to the disbelievers against this the objection arises that the disbelievers worship the sun at that time so the muslims ought to confront them by facing the bayt all h and worshipping allah most high what then is the reason for the prohibition apparently the wisdom behind the prohibition of praying at these times may be this since the devils fly up into the atmosphere and take the sun between their horns satanic influences fall upon the whole atmosphere and sunlight of that region and at that time the entire region becomes tainted with these influences the very object of satan is that people should worship and pray at that time and thus become tainted with satanic influences the command of the shar ah therefore is do not fulfil satan's object and even if one were to pray in the other direction towards the ka bah away from the direction of the sun the sunlight and the atmosphere remain tainted with satanic influences

giving zakat money to the owner of landed property someone owns land it is not held for trade but its value is more than the threshold and apart from this land the man has no other wealth there are two situations with this land 1 land from which no income can be obtained that is nobody is willing to take it on rent 2 land from which income could be obtained but the owner has paid no attention to it out of indifference can this man take zakat or will he be counted as wealthy are the charity of the fast breaking and the sacrifice obligatory upon him or not various statements are found in the books of fatwa about the owner of an estate so please give a detailed and satisfying answer it is necessary for the man in question to put the land to productive use and to live off that income or else to sell it and meet his needs from the proceeds but if neither course is possible and at present he has nothing to live on then he is permitted to take zakat and once he is established as deserving of zakat the charity of the fast breaking and the sacrifice will not be obligatory upon him yes once he sells the land and obtains cash he can no longer take zakat and the charity of the fast breaking rather since he will then own the threshold amount zakat will be obligatory upon him after a year has passed consider what is stated in fat w sh m

zakat when the wealth is spent on one's own needs after the year has passed a man had to pay zakat on 80 000 rand when his year ended in january but he did not pay it at that time and spent some of the money on his own needs he now has only 28 000 rand the question is should he pay zakat on 80 000 rand or on 28 000 rand the basic principle regarding a decrease in wealth after the year has passed is that if part of the wealth is destroyed the zakat due on that part falls away but if he has spent it on his own needs then it is necessary for him to pay the zakat on the whole amount so in the case in question he should pay zakat on 80 000 rand by way of a caution one should bear in mind that in paying zakat the lunar year is what counts not the solar year zakat should therefore be paid by the reckoning of the lunar year otherwise every three years there will be a shortfall of one month and in 33 or 36 years one full year's zakat will remain outstanding consider the proofs shiyat al a w al
